general rule rather than a case list. An empty label would leave the violations a special causes
unnamed. A data block is data: `import` and `print` have nothing to do there, and the plan's
"cannot touch the filesystem" must hold on this path too. `tiny-keccak` (CC0-1.0, a public-domain
dedication with no copyleft obligation) comes with `rhai`, which enables `ahash`'s compile-time
RNG whatever its features; the plan's policy admits such a license without asking.
Plan: `aatf_rules.md` "The ruleset schema" (required keys, load-time rules);
`core/distribution.md` (the allowlist); `deny.toml`.

## 2026-10-12 — aatf — the script API's accessors, the views' names, and the team settings deferred
Decision: a script sees a team as `TeamView` and its players as `PlayerView` (not the plan's
`TeamContext` and `PlayerEntry`), values on the game's scale; the accessor list is fixed in the
plan's table, with `rating_at(pos)` returning the rating label in place of a boolean
`playable_at`, and a stat a version lacks, a style outside the version's table or an absent colour
code crossing as `()`. The logic and a data block run on one engine: `Engine::new_raw()` plus
`StandardPackage`. The team settings' accessors wait for two facts: PES 16's man-marking
assignments in `pes_savefile`'s model with PES 17-21's man-marking instruction, and which auto
substitution byte means off.
Why: `PlayerEntry` and `TeamEntry` are `pes_savefile`'s records, and a second `PlayerEntry` in the
same workspace would make every import ambiguous. A rating label answers A, B and the
`no_b_ratings` check with one accessor where a boolean needs two. `()` lets the logic skip what a
version does not have instead of reading a 0 as a value. `new_raw` keeps the file resolver and
`print` out, which a check never needs; the standard package keeps arrays, maps and strings.
Guessing the auto substitution's off byte would make every VGL team pass or fail on a guess.
Plan: `aatf_rules.md` "The host" (the API table, the engine block, the tactics paragraph, the
team settings' prerequisites) and "Crate layout" (`team.rs`).

## 2026-10-12 — aatf — empty names refused, brackets ascending, weight bounds required
Decision: a ruleset is refused on load when a `name`, id or label is empty, when a bracket's
heights do not all lie above the earlier brackets', or when an `exactly` list is empty; a present
`universal.weight` must give all three bounds; an empty `any_player` counts as none on every
system.
Why: each is what an organizer leaves behind mid-edit (an emptied string, list or map, a
reordered bracket), and each would otherwise load and misjudge teams at check time: a blank label
shows no rule, a shadowed bracket takes no player, a defaulted bound demands weight = height.
Each is one general rule, not a case list.
Plan: `aatf_rules.md` "The ruleset schema" (`BracketHeights` doc, required keys, load-time rules).

## 2026-10-12 — aatf — no empty string, colour codes of eight characters, suggestion words reserved
Decision: a ruleset is refused on load when any string in it is empty (the `forbid` text and
`name_colors` entries join names, ids, labels and group keys), when a `name_colors` entry is not
eight characters, or when a card group id is one of `suggestions`' seven words.
Why: an empty `forbid` shows a blank violation and an empty colour code matches every name; a
partial colour-code paste matches none, so a ban silently stops applying; a group named `cards`
makes `suggestions: ["cards"]` mean two allowances. One general rule each, replacing the list of
fields the empty-name rule named.
Plan: `aatf_rules.md` "The ruleset schema" (`card_groups`' and `Heights::systems`' docs, the
load-time rules).

## 2026-10-12 — aatf — the latest two rulesets of each cup kind are templates; VTL10 joins
Decision: `libs/aatf` embeds as Ruleset editor templates the latest two rulesets of each kind of
cup: the 4cc's (Autumn 26, the default, and Spring 26), VGL's (VGL27, VGL26) and VTL's (VTL11,
VTL10). A newer ruleset of a kind replaces the older of its two and stays a test ruleset. Minor
invitationals (VTLA, UnityCup) get none. VTL10 is a new data block, transcribed from VTLEditor
at `2cf222f`, the last commit before its first matchday (2026-03-13), with a parity run on the
VTL10 cup save.
Why: the maintainer's ruling: an organizer starts from the cup closest to theirs, and the 4cc,
VGL and VTL are the three cups with an organization of their own; two per kind lets one compare
the latest change. VGL26 alone (the plan's template until now) covered one kind.
Plan: `aatf_rules.md` "Embedded rulesets" (new), the ruleset sections' status lines, "VTL10"
(new), "Crate layout", "Development phase and verification"; `ruleset_editor.md` start page
and verification.

## 2026-10-12 — methodology — the spec moves to `docs/spec/`; `docs/plans/` holds only work not built
Decision (maintainer): what the suite does is described in `docs/spec/`, the work not built yet in
`docs/plans/`, under the same file paths and headings, so a section partly built keeps its heading
in both trees, the plan's part pointing at the spec section it builds on. A phase's close moves
what it delivered (correcting what was built differently) instead of rewriting it in place.
Phases 1 to 4's sections moved on 2026-10-12; Phase 5's move at its close. Plans are written in
the present tense, the folder saying they are future; older future-tense text converts when its
section is next edited or moves. Every plan file opens with a banner saying it is a plan. Code
points at the spec only. A gate, `just doc-pointers`, fails on a section pointer whose file or
section is gone, so a move lists every pointer it breaks. Supersedes 2026-09-10 "plan-driven
kept" point (4) (the present-tense rewrite in place, "not a separate `docs/specs/` tree") and the
single-home rule of `plans/README.md` ("The specification stays here, in `docs/plans/`").
Why: a folder called `plans` holding the specification of what exists misleads every reader, and
the project is planned past 1.0.0, so renaming the folder once everything is built never comes.
The single-home argument (two homes drift) holds for one behavior in two documents, not for
built and unbuilt work in two trees with one layout: each sentence still has one home. The
banner exists because an excerpt read without its path (a brief, a reviewer's prompt) would pass
present-tense plan text off as fact. Entries in this log and in `LOG.md` keep the pointers they
were written with: they are append-only, and a pointer there names the tree of its day.
Plan: `plans/README.md` "How these documents evolve" (rewritten), `spec/README.md` (new);
`AGENTS.md` "Working documents" (table, closing a phase), "Read order by task"; `GLOSSARY.md`
"Plan", "Spec"; `CONTRIBUTING.md` "Testing and verification" (the gate); `WORKLOG.md` "Phases".

## 2026-10-12 — aatf — violations cross as kind-tagged maps; the sample team is a Team TOML document
Decision (lead, where the plan was silent): a violation map names its `ViolationKind` variant in
`kind` and carries the variant's fields under their names, `slot` and `severity` optional (the
team; an error); a map the host cannot convert fails the check with its index. The sample team
of load step 3 is a Team TOML document (`sample/team.toml`, a PES 15 team of the 2026 Summer Cup
save, renamed, no appearance tables), read through a new `TeamView::from_team_toml`, which
applies a document onto bare records. The logic section's extent and the current logic's place
in `LOGIC_VERSIONS` are fixed. `RequiredCard` carries a `Card`, not a `Skill` (`require_cards`
lists cards). `Rules` and the violations get modules of their own instead of `lib.rs`.
Why: one tag plus the variant's own field names is the spelling a custom-check author can read
off the Rust block, and refusing a bad map rather than skipping it keeps a buggy check from
passing a team. The 2026 cups run on PES 15, whose team export is a 5.6 MB encrypted container,
and a whole save is 5-11 MB; a Team TOML team is 146 KB of text, reviewable, and applied onto
bare records it reproduces every value the check reads (measured on the chosen team: every
player's age, height, weight, stats, positions and skills, and the tactics, equal, no import
notes). The Team creator checks the documents it writes the same way. Appearance needs a real
player's face data to apply onto (`NoIngameFaceRun` on a bare record), and no ruleset reads it.
Plan: `aatf_rules.md` "The interpreter" (the map paragraph, `RequiredCard`), "The host" (the
Team TOML constructor), "Loading and validation" (steps 1 and 3, logic identity), "Crate
layout".

## 2026-10-12 — aatf — man marking is the per-preset assignment bytes on PES 16 to 21; auto substitution off is 0
Decision (lead, from measurements the plan asked for): `TeamSettings::man_marking` reads the
eleven man-marking assignment bytes of each preset (any set: man marking), on PES 16 at tactics
record +0x73/+0xEE/+0x169 and on PES 17 to 21 at +0x95/+0x135/+0x1D5, instead of a defending
advanced instruction on 17 to 21, which the plan assumed. Auto substitution's off value is 0.
Why: Edit mode on PES 16 and 21 offers no man marking at all; members set it in a match's
pre-game plan and load it into the team through a copy preset (maintainer). The PES 16 offsets
are VTLEditor's and hold on the 2024 Summer Cup save; on 17 to 21 a census of every save on
disk shows the same shape (three 11-byte runs, 0xA0 apart, 0xFF but for a few teams of the cup
saves, values formation slots). Tight Marking, the instruction the plan's wording pointed at, is
a stronger, separate instruction (maintainer). Auto substitution was set in-game to each choice
and saved (PES 21: Off 0, Very Late 1, Flexible 2, Very Early 3; PES 16: Off 0, Very Late 1).
Plan: `aatf_rules.md` "The ruleset schema" (`TeamSettings`), "The host" (the team settings).

## 2026-10-13 — aatf — PES 15's man marking and auto flags are measured; the marking target is the opponent's formation slot
The previous entry left PES 15 unmeasured. Measured in-game on PES 15: Auto Substitution is the
tactics record's +0x1FE (Off 0, Very Late 1, Flexible 2), followed by the offside trap (+0x1FF)
and the automatic preset change (+0x200), each 0 or 1, the order PES 16 uses at +0x202. Man
marking is three 11-byte runs at +0x73, +0xED and +0x167 (presets 0x7A apart). A match's Mark
Settings (Game Plan > Preset Tactics; disabled in Edit mode) showed a cup team's four assignments
exactly where its bytes put them, which also settles what a value is: the opponent's formation
slot (its starting-eleven index), read against whichever team is played; measured on PES 15
only, and taken to hold for 16 to 21, which store the same shape. Plan: `aatf_rules.md` "The host" (the team settings).

## 2026-10-13 — pes_savefile — man marking joins the team model and Team TOML; the schema generator carries measured fields
Read back in-game on PES 21 (a cup team's three preset-3 assignments), so the PES 17-21 runs at
+0x95, +0x135 and +0x1D5 are measured, not only inferred, and an advanced instruction's player
byte is a roster slot. The model gains each preset's eleven man-marking bytes on PES 15 to 21
and PES 15's three auto flags. The reference editor reads neither, so the schema generator gets
a table of measured fields beside `WIDTH_FIXES`, rather than hand edits to its generated tables,
which a regeneration would drop. Team TOML carries the bytes too (`man_marking` per preset, 255
none): without them a team carried through Team TOML loses its marking silently, and an AATF
check of a Team TOML document could never see it. Plans: `aatf_rules.md` "The host";
`pes_savefile/operations.md` "Team TOML" when the step lands.

## 2026-10-13 — pes_savefile — the ingame-face run is decoded in-game before 1.0.0
The run's undecoded bits (about 350 of PES 21's 400: hair, the face sliders, colours beyond
skin and iris) stay authorable only as `[appearance.unknown]` `face` hex until measured, and no
legacy tool or published source decodes them. The maintainer wants nothing undecoded by 1.0.0,
so the lead measures them in the game: one changed setting per player and many players per
save, which attributes each diff to its setting and needs about four saves per twenty
settings, against one save per setting. PES 21 is measured whole and the other versions by spot
check, since the fifteen named fields share one layout. Plan: `pes_savefile/model.md`
"Decoding the rest of the ingame-face run".

## 2026-10-13 — settings.toml — every bit of the ingame-face run is a key or measured unused; `[appearance.unknown]` goes
Decision: step 5.0l named every bit of the run in the games. Each one becomes a `settings.toml`
key, or a measured-unused bit that a compile writes at the games' own value and generation
drops. `[appearance.unknown]` leaves `settings.toml` and Team TOML. This supersedes the entry of
2026-10-12, "the ingame-face run's undecoded bits travel between versions".
Why: that entry rested on the run having one layout on every version. Its risk came true: PES 15
stores its hair at the same bytes in another coding. A hex key carried across versions would
write a PES 15 hair id into PES 21's hairstyle bits and draw no hair, or crash the game. Named
keys convert per field. No release ever carried the table, so dropping it needs no migration.
Plan: `pes_savefile/model.md` "The ingame-face run, decoded"; `aesthetics_export/settings_toml.md`
(template, rules); `pes_savefile/operations.md` "Team TOML".

## 2026-10-13 — pes_savefile — two layout families of the run; list fields as wide as PES 15's
Decision: the run has two layouts, PES 15 and PES 16 to 21, in one field table whose rows name
the versions they exist on.
- Every list field takes PES 15's width; on 16 to 21 its ranges keep the high bits 0.
- The sliders only PES 15 draws are `pes15_` keys. They are stored on every version, so they are
  written on every version.
- The family-only hair keys and `pes15_nose_angle` are skipped on the other family with no
  finding, like `dribbling`.

Why: on 16 to 21 the bits above each list field are 0 in every Konami and cup face, and set,
they draw past the shipped models. They are the high bits of PES 15's wider lists, so one width
covers both families. The `pes15_` sliders carry real values from Konami's tables on every
version. Writing them everywhere keeps those values through Team TOML and through a conversion to
PES 15, which draws them.
Plan: `pes_savefile/model.md` "The ingame-face run, decoded".

## 2026-10-13 — pes_savefile — PES 15's face-type caps are its measured ranges
Decision: `face_type_cap` gets a PES 15 column of its own, the editor's range joined with the
game's faces: cheek 14, forehead 6, facial hair 29, laughter lines 6, eyelids 14, eyebrow 17,
neck line 5, nose 11, lips 7. PES 17 to 19 stay assumed equal to 16.
Why: the old caps assumed PES 15 equal to 16. A PES 15 export or conversion would then reset
most of its faces' eyebrows and eyelids to type 0. Neck line 4 and 5 and lips 7 are past the
editor but drawn as distinct models, and the game's own faces use them.
Plan: `pes_savefile/operations.md` "Cross-version player conversion";
`aesthetics_export/settings_toml.md` (ranges).

## 2026-10-13 — settings.toml — absent face and hair keys take the game's default face
Decision: an absent slider is 0 and an absent feature type 0, as before. The other new keys take
what PES 17's facial reset writes: very short Normal hair, dark brown (14, 10, 7) hair, eyebrows
and facial hair. This settles the open "Default 0" rule.
Why: an all-zero run is the editor's Preset look, every slider at -7, so "absent = 0" would
distort every face that leaves the sliders out. The reset's own jaw height +2 and lips 1 are not
taken: a slider at 0 reads as an offset from the editor's centre.
Plan: `aesthetics_export/settings_toml.md`, the ingame-face run's rules.

## 2026-10-13 — pes_savefile — a run converts field by field between PES 15 and 16+
Decision: a cross-version conversion whose two versions sit in different layout families copies
the shared fields onto the target's run and re-codes the nose. The target keeps its own
family-only and unused bits. The prefix copy and `FaceRunTruncated` go. Within one family the
run is still copied whole.
Why: a prefix copy turns a PES 15 variation id into a 16 to 21 hairstyle and cropped style. The
hair vanishes, or PES 21 crashes on a cropped-style high bit.
Plan: `pes_savefile/operations.md` "Cross-version player conversion".

## 2026-10-13 — settings.toml — the hair lists' ranges hold the 0 real saves store
Decision: every PES 16 to 21 hair list key (`style`, `cropped_style`, `length`, `front_style`,
`parted`, `side_back_style`, `hairline`, `forehead_width`) accepts 0, and `wave_level` (stored
as the level plus 1) accepts -1. The template's defaults stay the editor's.
Why: the fixture cup saves of PES 16 to 18 hold 0 there, outside the editors' 1-based lists
(1,651 PES 18 cup players in `style`, `front_style` and `parted`), so the editor ranges made
`from_player` refuse those players and a settings export of those cups fail. `variation`
already takes the 0 the games write. What a 0 draws is unmeasured (worklog Issues).
Plan: `aesthetics_export/settings_toml.md`, the template block's hair comments and the
paragraph after the ingame-face run's rules.

## 2026-10-13 — aatf — `serde_path_to_error` for schema errors' key paths
Decision: `libs/aatf` takes `serde_path_to_error` (dtolnay, MIT/Apache, depends on `serde` and
`itoa`) to report a `RULESET` schema error's key path. The maintainer approved the dependency.
Why: `rhai::serde::from_dynamic`'s errors name the bad key or type but not where it sits; a
deserializer wrapper of our own doing the same is the crate's whole job, several hundred lines.
Plan: `aatf_rules.md` "Loading and validation".

## 2026-10-13 — pes_savefile — a dropped PES 15 nose angle is a note; a nose type PES 15 cannot code is refused
Decision: converting PES 15 to 16-21 pushes `ConvertNote::NoseAngleDropped { angle }` for a
non-zero nose angle (16 to 21 have no field for it). Converting 16-21 to PES 15, a nose type
above 21 is refused as `CodecError::ValueTooWide`, all-or-nothing, not capped.
Why: the module notes every loss that depends on the player's data. PES 15 codes 3 × type +
angle in six bits, so a type past 21 has no coding; no game writes one (the widest cap is 7),
and a second cap pass for it would serve no real save.
Plan: `spec/pes_savefile/operations.md` "What the Rust module is".

## 2026-10-13 — match_tracker — PES 2019 registers first, then PES 2021, then the others
Decision: the Match tracker registers PES 2019 first, PES 2021 second, and the other versions
(PES 2017 among them) after: the maintainer's answer to the version-scope question. PES 2017's
open points (bucket 8 of its phase map, its refuted pointer chain) gate registering PES 2017,
not the first release. On every version, extra time (buckets 6 and 7) stays `Phase::Unknown`
until recorded, the unofficial fork's pointer chains, substitution journal and direct clock
read stay unregistered until verified, and heatmaps register only where the grid is measured
(PES 2017 and PES 2021, not PES 2019).
Why: the cup plays PES 2019 and PES 2021, and both layouts are measured (the README's
"Independent measurements", PR #1), so a first release that registered PES 2017 alone, the
version the original was written for, would track no cup match; and PES 2017's own open
points would gate every version's release.
Plan: `match_tracker/README.md` "Priority", "Independent measurements" (the executable
note), "Key decisions" (Game versions); `reading_the_game.md` "Game structures";
`match_model.md` "Match model and event derivation" (clock reconstruction); `testing.md`
"Verifying source-derived findings".

## 2026-10-13 — music player and match tracker plans — the fork survey's rulings
Decision: from the survey of the ATF bot author's Rigdio fork (v2.2.1) and SEN:P-AI 1.3.0
rebuild: `libs/music_export` keeps `event` entries in `MusicExport::events: Vec<EventClip>`
(player, kind, entry), apart from `slots`; they are never in a slot's priority list, the
`randomise` all-entries check or the `goal` fallback, their conditions are never evaluated,
they play once and honour `start`. Auto team loading looks up `<library>/<name>/<name>.4ccm`
first (the in-game name, slashes stripped, case-insensitive), the `name`-field scan as the
fallback; the same pair detected again is a no-op that keeps the score. An optional stoppage
chant: on `ClockStopped` past the first minute for a reason other than a goal, an own goal or
a half end, Full mode plays a random chant with probability
`autopilot_stoppage_chant_percent`, default 0. Victory anthems stay manual, the rebuild's
independent finding cited; event clips check only the side the feed names and pick one of a
player's several clips at random. Normalization parity runs against Rigdio's source or the
fork's build, never the packaged v2.2.0 exe. The stale "dead code" / "only had event clips" /
"only consumer" statements name upstream and the forks apart ("the 1.3.0 rebuild", "the
unofficial fork"). Left out: the survey's recommendations the plan already rules out; a
throw-in `StopReason` withdrawn (SEN:P-AI never infers a throw-in: `MatchReader.cpp` has
the case commented out, upstream and rebuild alike, so no variant is needed); the fuzzy
scorer match, the chant's default and an inbound control API are questions in
`QUESTIONS.md`.
Why: a separate `events` list keeps slot selection a plain loop rather than a loop with a
skip that the `randomise` check and the `goal` append would each have to repeat; the fixed
path is what the forks' tooling already produces and costs one file probe; a default of 0
for the chant keeps today's behaviour until the maintainer picks; an unreachable
`StopReason` variant is a case the `Unknown` reason already covers.
Plan: `music_player.md` "Background", "Relationship to the old codebase", "Instructions",
"Model", "Song selection", "Autopilot", "Loudness normalization", "Settings (tool
section)", "Improvements over Rigdio", "Dropped features and compatibility notes", "Key
decisions"; `match_tracker/README.md` "Background", "Unofficial fork (unverified
findings)", "Relationship to the old codebase"; `GLOSSARY.md` "Event clip" edited.

## 2026-10-13 — pes_savefile — a converted motion past the target's range is capped at the top
Decision: a cross-version player conversion caps a motion at the target version's top value
instead of copying it through.
Why: measured on PES 18 from a patched save, a stored value past the range shows the list's
top (hunching 3 "3", corner kick 7 "6", celebration 150 "127") with no crash, and a save with
another row of the screen edited kept two of them but rewrote the corner kick to 0, the first
entry: which values survive is per field, so a copied value is unstable and can turn into the
first entry on the player's next in-game save. The top is what the game shows for it anyway.
Plan: `pes_savefile/operations.md` "Cross-version player conversion".

## 2026-10-13 — save_editor — a save's later team of an already-listed name is left out of the teams list
Decision: `export-teams-list` merges the first team in record order under a name; a later team
whose name folds to the same one is left out and reported as `teams_list_name_duplicate`
(Error, exit 1), naming the team kept.
Why: the list holds a name once, and the clash is in the save, where it is fixed; renaming or
renumbering a team in the list would invent an identity the cup never gave it. The PES 21
fixture, a real cup save, holds `/4ccg/` at 784 and 852.
Plan: `save_editor.md` "CLI" (SE-TL-04).

## 2026-10-13 — save_editor — `diff` names a field by its schema name
Decision: a `diff` row names its field by the schema enum's variant name (`BootsId`,
`NeckLength`) until `pes_savefile` offers a label of its own.
Why: the comparator's rows carry the enum, and its variant names are the schema's, stable per
version; a second naming table in the tool would drift from the schema.
Plan: `save_editor.md` "Comparator (gameplay + aesthetics)".

## 2026-10-14 — music_export — the format crate's rulings where the plan was silent
Decision: `Condition::eval` is pure: `once` is `True` every time and the slot's selection
unloads it after its first check; `not` of a never-again condition is `True` (the old reader
propagated the unload); `time` without a minute is `False`. Fallback `goal` entries evaluate
under the name `goal`, so their `goals` counts the default goalhorn button's presses. The
serializer writes `==`, lowercase match types, `knockouts` expanded, the shortest `start` form,
and a fourth `# event clips` section. The parser refuses what the old reader crashed on or
misread (empty fields, reserved words after an entry, extra arguments, `every 0`, `speed 0`,
`event` on a reserved slot); `random` and `randomize` are not aliases of `randomise`; `speed`
takes any positive number, its 0.25-4.00 range left to the editor's validation. Song
selection (`PriorityList`) lives in the crate, beside the evaluator it walks.
Why: a pure evaluator cannot remember a check, and the three-valued verdict covers the rest;
the old reader's `not` unload unloads `not time <= 45` after the 45th minute. The census over
the machine's 61 files is the measurement behind each refusal: none hits one except three
history copies with `random`/`randomize` and one with `goals>=3`, which Rigdio refuses too,
so an alias would let a file work here that fails in Rigdio. Selection over `MatchState` is a
pure function, so its scenario tests need no player.
Plan: `music_player.md` "The `.4ccm` format" (Conditions, Model), "Song selection (per button press)".

## 2026-10-14 — pes_savefile — one table of motion tops per version; a value past the widest range stays refused
Decision: the measured motion tops (`settings_toml.md` "The motion ranges were measured") live
in one per-version table in `pes_savefile`, which the keys' widest ranges, the template's
comments and the cross-version conversion's cap all read; PES 19 gets its own face-cap column
(cheek 5, forehead 6, measured), narrower 20 and 21 left as measured. A stored value past a
key's widest range (a PES 16 cup player's `goal_celebration_2 = 183`) stays refused when the
player is read into a `settings.toml`.
Why: the template's ranges were copied from the reference editor and were wrong on five
versions; with one table, a later measurement changes one row. Accepting 183 would write a
`settings.toml` value no editor offers and whose match look is unmeasured; the refusal names
the key, and the member picks a celebration in range.
Plan: `aesthetics_export/settings_toml.md` "The motion ranges were measured";
`pes_savefile/operations.md` "Cross-version player conversion".

## 2026-10-14 — core — every GUI is drafted as a web page first, with egui's widgets only
Decision: each tool's GUI (and each new shell element) is first an interactive, self-contained
HTML draft in `docs/prototypes/`, refined with the maintainer before the egui view is written,
and limited to what egui draws (the list in `core/gui.md` "Prototypes before implementation").
The Ruleset editor's draft comes first, after the AATF steps, with a check that the ruleset
schema covers a contributor's independent proposal.
Why: the maintainer's request: a page is quicker to iterate than a view and members can open it
without building anything; restricting it to egui's widgets keeps it a specification the
implementation can meet. A draft in egui itself (Studio Web) was the alternative: exact, but
much slower to iterate.
Plan: `core/gui.md` "Prototypes before implementation".

## 2026-10-14 — aatf — Red CBs count 4 cm shorter at every height, as `aatf.cpp` does
Decision: the official file's "Red CBs up to 189" special applies its 4 cm allowance at every
height, as `aatf.cpp` does: a Red regular CB fielded only at CB is tall at 189, mid at 180 to
184, a manlet at 179 or below, and in no bracket at 185 to 188.
Why: the maintainer's ruling: follow the old checker even where the label suggests a bound (the
side-lead had bounded the allowance to 189, as the goalkeepers' special is); the parity run then
expects no difference on Red CBs.
Plan: `aatf_rules.md` "The official ruleset".

## 2026-10-14 — aatf — the interpreter's rulings at 5.2c3 and 5.2d
Decision: `gk_not_second_a` fires for any player holding GK among several A positions, a
goalkeeper with a second A included, as `aatf.cpp` tests it. `apply_tier` takes the team
view, the player's view and the record. A legal team "reports nothing" but suggestions, which
are listed apart and uncounted; a weak-foot suggestion is one `Unused` per value below its
limit. rhai's expression depths are pinned at 64, top level and functions.
Why: the plan's "an outfield player's second A" is the narrower reading, and the old checker
is the parity standard; the specials depend on the team (system, captain) and the write goes
to the record, where the plan's `(player, tier, rules)` named no team; rhai's depth defaults
differ between debug and release builds, and the interpreter nests past the debug function
limit of 16, so a file would parse in the tests and not in the binary, or the reverse.
Plan: `aatf_rules.md` "The interpreter", "The host".

## 2026-10-14 — aatf — a tier's name colour, written by `apply_tier`
Decision: `Tier::name_color` is the colour code a tier's names start with; when any tier sets
one, a player of a tier that sets none carries none of those codes. `apply_tier` writes the
tier's code over the name's leading one, and under a tier that sets none removes a code
another tier sets, keeping any other. A mismatch is a `NameColor` violation.
Why: VTL11 requires medals' names to carry a gold or silver code and forbids it to the rest;
as a condition alone, the quick action would produce a medal the checker rejects, against
"neither tool can produce a player the checker then rejects". Leaving the colour to the
member was the alternative; the maintainer chose the field (the VGL fork's editor also writes
the colour itself).
Plan: `aatf_rules.md` "The ruleset schema", "The interpreter" (violation kinds), "The host";
`ruleset_editor.md` "The editor" (Tiers).

## 2026-10-14 — aatf — the schema covers a member's plain-language proposal
Decision: four additions make the schema express everything the proposal does: a condition's
`ranges` (any ability stat, age, weight, form, injury resistance, weak foot), `strong_foot`
and `any` (one of several sub-conditions); `form` and `injury_resistance` effects, added to
the tier's values. Per-preset coordinates and single-preset positions stay custom checks,
over a new `team.formation` accessor and the existing `team.fielded_positions`. The format
itself is not adopted.
Why: `any` is needed rather than two specials because a player meeting both cases would get
an additive effect twice; ranges cover every comparison on a player number with one field,
not one per variable. Coordinate rules have no precedent and no single shape a form could
take, so a custom check is cheaper than a field nobody fills in. A plain text format was
rejected because the Ruleset editor's forms are easier still and the file must also carry
the interpreter.
Plan: `aatf_rules.md` "Coverage of a plain-language proposal", "The ruleset schema", "The
host"; `ruleset_editor.md` "The editor".

## 2026-10-14 — aatf — a present `weak_foot` names both halves
Decision: a `weak_foot` written in a tier or an effect requires both `usage` and `accuracy`;
one left out fails the load (`Schema`), as a present `weight` missing a bound does.
Why: required, not defaulted to the empty value, because a missing half defaulting to 0 caps
that half below the game's lowest value (1), so every player the tier or special reaches
violates it; an author writing `usage: 4` alone means something else, and the load is where
the slip can still be named.
Plan: `aatf_rules.md` "The ruleset schema", the paragraph after the Rust block.

## 2026-10-14 — pes_savefile — the playable ratings read C 0, B 1, A 2, in the save's own position order
Decision: `labels::RATINGS` becomes `C`, `B`, `A`, `3` (index = the stored 2-bit value) and
`PlayerPositions::playable` is read in the order CF, SS, LWF, RWF, AMF, DMF, CMF, LMF, RMF, CB,
LB, RB, GK, not as the registered order reversed. The Team TOML's `playable` keys and labels
follow; a stored 3 is labelled `"3"`.
Why: measured, not guessed: of 11 799 rated fixture players, 11 795 store 2 at their
registered position under this order, 5 683 under the reversal, and none stores a 3; every cup
rule requires A at the registered position, so 2 is A. The four-entry table keeps the writer
total over the field's two bits (a dump carries what the save holds); the unused value is
spelled as its number, because a word would claim a meaning nothing has shown.
Plan: `spec/pes_savefile/operations.md` "Team TOML" (the `playable` line); the model's docs
follow in the code.

## 2026-10-14 — aatf — VGL26 follows its rules page on goalkeepers' height; fielding at GK checked in preset 1 only
Decision: VGL26's goalkeeper tier is recognized by registered position alone, and a special
forbids a registered goalkeeper at any height but 185 cm. The page's "medal and buffed players
cannot be played as a goalkeeper at any time" stays checked in preset 1 only.
Why: the rules page says goalkeepers must be 185 cm, and the plan follows the page where it is
stricter; the checker read a goalkeeper at 180 as a regular, which let him pass. One forbid
reports it once, where a height in the tier's condition would have read him as a regular and
reported every stat. Presets 2 and 3 would need a condition on fielded positions that no other
ruleset uses; preset 1 already refuses it (no outfielder is rated A at GK, and preset 1 fields A
positions alone), so the gap is a member fielding an outfielder in goal in a reserve preset.
Plan: `aatf_rules.md` "VGL26" (the "on purpose" paragraph).

## 2026-10-14 — aatf — VGL27's goalkeepers and captain follow its rules page
Decision: in VGL27 every tier but the goalkeeper excludes GK in its `when`, the regular
included; a goalkeeper at 185 cm is forbidden by a special, and one at 175 or 180 cm is in
those brackets; the captain's extra allowance is a `choice` of one card, one COM style or one A
position.
Why: the plan's "a registered GK is a goalkeeper whatever his rating" needs the regular's
exclusion too, or a goalkeeper rated under 77 falls back to the regular (the last tier whose
`when` holds). The page's tall bracket takes outfielders at 185 and goalkeepers at 189, and its
other brackets name no position: forbidding every height but 189 would refuse goalkeepers the
page allows, and the brackets' exact heights already refuse 181 to 188 but 185. The page offers
the captain three alternatives where the checker grants a card, and a VGL ruleset follows its
page.
Plan: `aatf_rules.md` "VGL27" (the recognition row and the "on purpose" paragraph).

## 2026-10-14 — aatf — a ruleset file in `rulesets/` may carry its own custom checks
Decision: a `rulesets/` file holds the data block and, when the ruleset has custom checks, its
CUSTOM CHECKS section after it; `assemble` puts the current logic between the two (the empty
stub when there is no section). VTL11's skill-card cap of 11 applies on every version, not on
PES 21 only, as its checker does.
Why: VTL11's rule on the 188 cm players' positions is a custom check (decision 2026-10-06), and
a custom check written into a test instead of beside its data would not ship with the ruleset
when the Ruleset editor's templates embed it. The cap: the plan had misread the checker, whose
test is unconditional.
Plan: `aatf_rules.md` "Crate layout" (the paragraph after the tree), "Background" (VTL11) and
the schema's `max_skill_cards` doc.

## 2026-10-14 — aatf — VTL11's goalkeeper count is exact, its maximum a custom check
Decision: VTL11 sets `min_goalkeepers: 2`, and its custom checks report a third goalkeeper.
Why: its checker refuses a team with fewer or more than two goalkeepers, and the schema has a
minimum only; a third goalkeeper is otherwise a regular among ten and passes every count. A
`max_goalkeepers` field for one ruleset would widen the schema for a rule the escape hatch
already carries.
Plan: no plan edit needed (the plan's VTL11 paragraph lists the custom check; the goalkeeper
count is the checker's, transcribed).

## 2026-10-14 — aatf — the parity differences every legacy checker shows are kept
Decision: a player of no tier stays reported once, as `NoTier`; the checkers' overall-rating
line gets no kind; a tier over its count stays a team finding. VTL11's two playing-style
warnings are added to its data block (step 5.2f-r1), and VTL10 stays the checker's ruleset.
Why: the parity runs (5.2f) agreed on every team's legality outside VGL's support settings;
what differed was these three reporting choices and VTL11's warnings. Running the tier-free
checks for a player of no tier would report a weight or a missing card one run earlier, at the
cost of a second path through the checks for a player the member must look at anyway; the
rating line repeats the stats that make it; naming one excess medal picks an arbitrary player.
The warnings are the checker's and the schema carries them as data. On the VTL10 save the
checker's 43 legal teams are exactly the data block's, so the wiki page is not the cup's ruleset.
Plan: `aatf_rules.md` "Development phase and verification" (the differences), "Background"
(VTL11's warnings), "VTL10" (the page settled).

## 2026-10-14 — studio_core — a command's result text is an event; the running-PES probe matches exe names
Decision: `PipelineEvent::Output(String)` carries a CLI command's result text (the console prints
it verbatim to stdout; a command printing one reports nothing else on success). The running-PES
probe, `pes_process::running_pes()`, lists `PES2015.exe` to `PES2021.exe` processes by name
(Toolhelp on Windows, `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` on Linux for Wine and Proton), each with its version
and, when the process allows, its exe path.
Why: the printer thread owns stdout during a command, so text returned from `cli_run` and printed
by the binary would interleave with its lines; an event keeps one writer. The game takes no lock
on its save and its window title follows its language, so the process name is the one stable
mark; the CLI needs a one-shot probe before the GUI's poll exists, and the poll reuses it.
Plan: `plans/core/architecture.md` "Crate structure" (the running-PES probe) and "Event system"
(a command's result text).

## 2026-10-14 — save_editor — how `check-aatf` prints a violation, its setting and `--teams`
Decision: one finding line per violation, code `aatf_violation`, at the violation's severity, its
context the team, the player's id (a player's violation), `rule` (the `ViolationKind` name as a
rules file writes it) and the kind's fields by their rules-file labels; suggestions are not
printed; a team whose `check_team` fails is an `aatf_check_failed` error line and the run goes on;
`--teams` ids and ranges, an id the save lacks refused; the setting key `aatf_rules`, empty for the
embedded official file.
Why: one code with the rule as context, not one code per kind, because the kinds are `aatf`'s and
a second list of 32 codes in the tool would drift from it, while the context already names the
rule; the console prints a finding's code and context, so the line reads like the tool's other
findings. Suggestions are a GUI toggle, off by default, and the CLI has no flag for it. A failed
team stops nothing else: the other teams' results are still true, and the failure is a bug the
line names. Rules-file labels (`CF`, `dribbling`) because the reader of the line is the person
who wrote or edits the rules file.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "CLI", the `check-aatf` bullet.

## 2026-10-14 — save_editor — the write refusal applies to the running game of the save's version only
Decision: a Save editor command that writes a save refuses only while the PES of that save's
version runs; the save is opened (read) first, so the refusal comes after reading and before any
write. A running PES of another version does not block it.
Why: a game writes back only its own version's save on exit, so a PES 2021 running cannot
overwrite a PES 15 save; refusing on any running game blocked those edits, and a copy of a save
kept elsewhere, and made the Save editor's own tests fail on a machine with any PES open. Matching
the save folder as well was rejected: it needs each version's save path (Documents may be
redirected) and misses a save copied into that folder later, while version matching needs no
path knowledge. The Team compiler's savefile step (step 5.3b, not built) writes the target
version's local save, so the same rule fits it; its plan is unchanged until that step.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "CLI", the "Writing a save" bullet, and SE-CLI-02.

## 2026-10-14 — team_compiler — the savefile step skips only while the compile target's PES runs
Decision: the Team compiler's savefile step is skipped (`savefile_skipped_pes_running`) only
while the PES of the compile target's version runs, the same rule as the Save editor's writing
commands (entry above).
Why: one rule for one danger: the compiler's savefile is always the target's version, and a game
only writes back its own version's save, so another version's game running never threatens it;
two tools refusing on different conditions would confuse the user and the code.
Plan: `plans/team_compiler/pipeline.md` "Post-processing", `messages.md`
(`savefile_skipped_pes_running`), `README.md` TC-SAV-10, `plans/core/architecture.md` "The
running-PES probe".

## 2026-10-14 — aatf — "switch preset tactic" is checked against a byte that may not hold it
Decision: the maintainer's answer to the VGL question: every cup manager keeps "switch preset
tactic" on, so a cup save showing it off on every team means the EDIT file's byte is not the
in-game setting (the SYSTEM file is the candidate). The rulesets stay as they are until an
in-game check (step 5.2f-r2) names where PES 21 stores it.
Why: VGL26/VGL27 require the byte on and VTL10/VTL11 off; on real cup saves the first fails every
team and the second passes every team, both without meaning if the byte is not the setting.
Changing four rulesets on an inference would trade one unverified reading for another.
Plan: `plans/aatf_rules.md` "VGL26", the support-settings paragraph.

## 2026-10-14 — aatf — VGL26 and VGL27 require the automatic preset change off
Decision: VGL26's and VGL27's "Support settings" team rule requires `auto_preset_change` off, with
auto substitution and the offside trap; the rules pages' "switch preset tactic", which must be on,
is checked by no ruleset. Supersedes this day's earlier entry ("switch preset tactic" checked
against a byte that may not hold it).
Why: the maintainer explained the two settings. "Switch preset tactic" is the tactics menu's option
offering all three presets instead of one, a manager's own setting, not stored per team; the byte
is "Auto change Preset Tactics" (the 4cc wiki's Edit-file page), the game switching presets during
a match, which is a support setting and so off. Every team of the three PES 21 cup saves holds it
off, and VTL10 and VTL11 already require it off.
Plan: `plans/aatf_rules.md` "Background" (the rules pages' list) and "VGL26" (its team settings
row and the support-settings paragraph).

## 2026-10-14 — aatf — the paid-card limit is signed
Decision: `ViolationKind::Cards` and `CardLimits` carry the paid limit as `i8`: a player with more
extra A positions than cards has a limit below zero and is over it with no card at all.
Why: the logic clamped the limit at 0 so it fit a `u8`, not a negative number, and then a regular
rated A at five positions with three cards held nothing over a limit of 0 and passed; an
overspend paid in A positions is still an overspend (Astra I.A1, concern 1).
Plan: `plans/aatf_rules.md` "The card economy", "The interpreter" (`card_limits`,
`ViolationKind::Cards`).

## 2026-10-14 — aatf — a Team TOML's omitted key reads 0 on every field
Decision: `TeamView::from_team_toml` applies the document onto bare records that carry every
field of the document's version at zero, so an omitted key reads 0 whether or not some version
lacks the field.
Why: `PlayerEntry::default()` leaves version-gated fields absent, which the logic reads as "this
version lacks the stat": an omitted `catching` switched its check off while an omitted `speed`
was reported (Astra I.A1, concern 2). Rejecting incomplete documents instead would refuse the
partial documents a check of only some values needs.
Plan: `plans/aatf_rules.md` "The host", the paragraph on `TeamView::from_team_toml`.

## 2026-10-14 — aatf — choices: free_cards options, replacing effects, and disjoint card groups
Decision: a `free_cards` choice option is used when one of its cards is held and paid; a chosen
option's replacing effect (`max_a_positions`, `weak_foot`) gives way to one a later special sets;
a ruleset whose card groups overlap, or hold a COM style, is refused on load.
Why: an option was taken when its card was held and not free by name, even when a group already
covered it, blocking the option that helped; choices resolve after every special (their use
depends on the other effects), which let an earlier special's option override a later special's
replacement against the specials' order; overlapping groups made the greedy allocation, and so a
team's legality, depend on the groups' names. Refusing overlaps is simpler than an
order-independent allocation, and no shipped ruleset overlaps (Astra I.A1, concerns 3 to 5).
Plan: `plans/aatf_rules.md` "The ruleset schema" (`card_groups`, `Effects::choice`, the load
rules).

## 2026-10-14 — aatf — apply_tier resolves the values it writes
Decision: `apply_tier` writes onto a copy, recomputes `tier_values` on the copy and repeats until
they stop changing, three passes at most, then commits; values still changing are an error and
the player is left as it was.
Why: the specials were resolved against the player's old values, so a special conditioned on a
value the tier sets (form, a stat) wrote a player `check_team` then rejected, breaking the quick
actions' promise (Astra I.A1, concern 6). A bounded loop with an error, not an unbounded one,
because a special can switch itself off by its own effect.
Plan: `plans/aatf_rules.md` "The host", the `apply_tier` paragraph.

## 2026-10-14 — save_editor, pes_savefile — strip and seed takes each row from the player's record
Decision: strip and seed builds each `PlayerAppearance.bin` row with a new
`EditFile::appearance_row(player_id)`, the record's own bytes as the save would write them, not
through `PlayerSettings::from_player` and `PlayerSettings::appearance_row`.
Why: SE-STR-01 asks for rows equal to the records' bytes, and real cup saves hold values past a
key's range inside its field's bits (79 players of the PES 18 fixture save, 26 of the PES 19
one) that `from_player` refuses; widening the ranges would need the game to show those values
first, and the settings route would also rewrite bits no field models with the games' values.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Stripped save" (the strip and seed bullet),
`plans/pes_savefile/model.md` "Player settings model" (the new bullet).

## 2026-10-14 — save_editor — a base-copied face is reported by strip and seed, its condition measured in-game first
Decision: a player whose record copies another player's face is stripped and seeded like the
others and reported as a `strip_base_copied_face` warning; which records count (base-copy id
alone, or with the face edit flag) waits for an in-game check, so step 5.4c splits into the
commands (5.4c1) and the warning (5.4c2, SE-STR-07).
Why: the database row has no base-copy id, so the relationship cannot be carried; leaving such
players unstripped would keep their look but break "every appearance id at -1", so every later
compile and `check-stripped` would flag them. A census of 125 Fox saves found 0 to 26 such
players per real PES 21 cup save (face flag set) and 5,037 in the PES 21 fixture save (all
copying 7511, flag clear): testing the id alone could warn about every player of a save.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Stripped save" (the base-copied face bullet), the `strip-and-seed`
CLI bullet, SE-STR-07; `QUESTIONS.md` "Which base-copied faces the game shows".

## 2026-10-14 — pes_savefile, team_compiler — the Fox player tables move to pes_savefile
Decision: `PlayerAppearance.bin`, `BootsList.bin` and `GloveList.bin` are read, edited by player
id and written sorted by player id by one `pes_savefile` type; the Team compiler's
`BootsList`/`GloveList` editing (`bins::player_tables`'s `ItemList`) moves there, the compiler
keeping its row-selection rules (committed tasks, `Remove` rows, `player_table_missing`).
Why: the Save editor's strip and seed (5.4c1) writes the same three tables, and a tool crate
cannot depend on another; a second codec in the Save editor would drift from the compiler's.
`pes_savefile` already builds the appearance row. Sorted by id with each id once is what all
twelve game and cup `PlayerAppearance.bin` files measured hold, as the item lists do.
Plan: `plans/pes_savefile/model.md` "Player settings model" (the Fox player tables bullet).

## 2026-10-14 — pes_savefile — correction: the appearance row holds no unmodeled bits
Decision: the entry "strip and seed takes each row from the player's record" stands on its first
reason alone (the settings route refuses stored values past a key's range); its second, that the
settings route would rewrite bits no field models, is withdrawn.
Why: 5.4c1a found the row's 56 bytes all modeled (packed fields, then the ingame-face run kept
verbatim), so a row written over zeros and one taken from the record are the same bytes on every
fixture player.
Plan: `plans/pes_savefile/model.md` "Player settings model" (the row-from-record bullet).

## 2026-10-14 — aatf — a free_cards option is used when it lowers an over-limit paid count
Decision: a `free_cards` choice option is used when, without it, the player's paid cards are over
the limit and, with it, fewer are paid; this replaces this day's "used when one of its cards is
held and paid". And `apply_tier` writes the tier's name colour before it resolves the values, so
a special conditioned on `name_colors` sees the colour it writes.
Why: the SWE-2 review of the rework (I.S1) found a held card a group covers whose freeing by name
passes the group's allowance to a paid groupmate: "held and paid" left that option unused and
the player over the limit. The plan's general rule for options ("without it, the player exceeds
a limit the option raises") covers it, and gives the same verdicts on every earlier fixture. The
name colour is a value the tier writes, the same class as form and stats.
Plan: `plans/aatf_rules.md` "The ruleset schema" (`Effects::choice`); "The host" (the
`apply_tier` paragraph already says "resolved against what it writes").

## 2026-10-14 — aatf — a choice option is used only when, applied, it raises the limit the player exceeds
Decision (lead, from a review): a choice option is used when, without it, the player exceeds a
limit and the option, applied to him, raises that limit: a per-tier value naming another tier
raises nothing, nor does a replacing effect (`weak_foot`, `max_a_positions`) that a later
special overrides. Each limit's test compares the player's values with and without the option
applied, not the option's keys.
Why: Astra's review I.A2 found both kinds counted as used because the check read only which keys
the option holds: the option took the choice while changing nothing, and a later option that
would have helped (an extra card) was skipped, leaving a `Cards` error the ruleset does not
mean. Comparing the applied values is the plan's existing "a limit the option raises", read for
the player's own tier and the specials' order; the `free_cards` rule is its case for cards freed
by name.
Plan: `plans/aatf_rules.md` "The ruleset schema" (`Effects::choice`).

## 2026-10-14 — music_player — a missed scorer falls back to a fuzzy match at 90, names of 4 characters up; stoppage chants default to 15 %
Decision (maintainer): the feed's scorer name is matched to a player slot case-insensitively
first, then to the slot with the highest `partial_ratio` (`thefuzz`'s, defined in the plan:
the shorter lowercased name against the longer's windows, best indel similarity, 0 to 100) when
it reaches 90 and no other slot ties it, both names having at least 4 characters; otherwise
the standard horn plays and the names are logged. The ratio is a few lines in the player
crate, not a dependency. `autopilot_stoppage_chant_percent` defaults to 15 (Full mode only,
as before).
Why: the maintainer's answers (2026-10-14 and 15). In-game names and `.4ccm` slot names
differ enough that managers will rename most slots to match, so a high bar suffices: 90, not
the Rigdio fork's 70, which would let a near-miss of another player's name take the goal. The
cross-check of the EDIT-file census against the `.4ccm` census (65 slots, 144 saves; plan
"Scorer matching") found no score between 81 and 99, and a name contained in a longer one
scoring 100 either way, wrongly for short in-game names ("sex" in the slot "Sexy Hagcat",
"I", "NO"): the lead proposed the 4-character floor and the maintainer agreed. The Studio
beta's logs check both values. Full mode is for unattended matches, where nobody presses
Random, so the SEN:P-AI rebuild's 15 % is the default; 0 keeps chants manual.
Plan: `plans/music_player.md` "Autopilot" ("Scorer matching", "Stoppage chants"), the
settings table, "Testing", the Rigdio fork's survey row.

## 2026-10-15 — save_editor — a base-copied face is any base-copy id other than 0 and the player's own, whatever the face flag
Decision (lead, from an in-game check): `strip_base_copied_face` reports every player whose
base-copy id is neither 0 nor his own id; the face edit flag plays no part.
Why: PES 21 Edit mode on the maintainer's cup save (2026-10-15, screenshots in
`.tmp/ingame/face_check/`): "MESSI" of /sp/ copies player 7511 with the flag set and shows
Messi's face; the same save with that one flag cleared (`save-editor diff`: EditedFace 1 to 0,
nothing else) shows the same face, so the game reads the id alone. It wins over the player's
own face model too: two /sp/ players with a `face.fpk` each in the download CPKs, face flag
set on one and clear on the other, given base copy 7511, both showed Messi's face; so a
player with a model of his own is not exempt (stripped, he shows his model instead of the copy,
as a stripped player without a base copy did in the same run). Stripped, he and a
teammate copying 114624 show Placeholder, their rows having no base-copy id, so the warning is
needed. Testing the id and the flag would miss flag-clear copies the game shows. The PES 21
fixture save, whose 5,037 players copy 7511 with the flag clear, is no evidence either way:
the installed game refuses it ("data from a different version").
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Stripped save" (the base-copied face bullet), SE-STR-07.

## 2026-10-15 — team_compiler — a gloves subfolder's .mtl names a texture from above by a copy beside it
Decision (lead, from an in-game check): on PES 15-17 a texture that a shared gloves folder's
subfolder `.mtl` resolves in a folder above its own is packed again beside that `.mtl`, which
names it `./<stem>.dds`, instead of `../<stem>.dds`. Model paths in `glove.xml` keep their
subfolders.
Why: PES 17 Edit mode (2026-10-15, /out/ slots 01-03 wearing shared gloves 1684-1686, files in
`.tmp/ingame/gloves_check/`): `glove.xml`'s `./grip/glove_r.model` loads, and so do a `.mtl`'s
`./magenta.dds` beside it and `./sub/magenta.dds` below it; a `grip/` `.mtl` naming
`../magenta.dds` drew the glove white, and so did the game-rooted
`model/character/glove/g1684/magenta.dds` (CPK patched by hand, since the compiler writes a
path into the folder relative). The question's fallback, packing gloves flat, would collide
two subfolders' `glove_r.model`; a copy collides with nothing, since the lookup reaches above
only when the nearer folders lack the stem. PES 15 and 16 are unmeasured (no test slot) and
taken to read as PES 17, one engine.
Plan: `plans/team_compiler/pipeline.md` "3. Per-model-folder parallel steps (rayon)" (Packing),
TC-MOD-93.

## 2026-10-15 — team_compiler — every .mtl of a pre-Fox gloves output is packed at its root
Decision (lead, from an in-game check): amends the entry above. On PES 15-17 a shared gloves
output packs each `.mtl` at its root, named by its path below the folder with `/` written `_`
(`grip_materials.mtl`), `glove.xml` naming it there; models and textures keep their paths, and
the `.mtl` names its textures `./<stem>.dds` or `./<sub>/<stem>.dds`. No texture is copied.
TC-MOD-93 withdraws TC-MOD-74.
Why: a fifth PES 17 run the same day (`.tmp/ingame/gloves_check/r5_slot01.png`) drew the right
glove magenta with its model at `grip/glove_r.model` and its `.mtl` at the root naming
`./magenta.dds`, and the fourth had a root `.mtl` load `./sub/magenta.dds`; so moving the
`.mtl` removes every upward path. A copy beside a subfolder `.mtl` also works (run 2) but needs
the textures task, which emits each texture once, to learn from the `.mtl` files which ones a
subfolder reaches above; the move is a change to the packed names alone.
Plan: `plans/team_compiler/pipeline.md` "3. Per-model-folder parallel steps (rayon)" (Packing),
`plans/team_compiler/README.md` TC-MOD-93.

## 2026-10-15 — team_compiler — a compiled CPK records its shared IDs, and a Midcup keeps them
Decision (maintainer, on the lead's recommendation): every compiled CPK records, per team,
which shared boots or gloves folder took which ID (`4cc_studio/shared_ids/<team_id>.toml`). A
`Midcup` export reads the record from the installed CPKs below its output: a folder named there
keeps its ID, a new one takes the lowest free shared ID, and a team with no record is numbered
alphabetically with a `shared_ids_unrecorded` warning. A `Full` export numbers alphabetically
and records.
Why: the maintainer answered that members' Midcup exports carry only the shared folders that
changed. Numbering those alone alphabetically gives a new folder the ID an absent one holds in
the main CPK, whose rows stay for the players the Midcup does not compile, so those players
would wear the new folder. The record travels in the CPK every member installs, so a Midcup
compiled anywhere reads the same one; requiring Midcups to carry every shared folder would
make members copy folders they did not change.
Plan: `plans/aesthetics_export/player_folders.md` "A `Midcup` export keeps the shared IDs the
team already has"; `plans/team_compiler/messages.md` `shared_ids_unrecorded`;
`plans/team_compiler/README.md` TC-BIN-34 to TC-BIN-36.

## 2026-10-15 — team_compiler — Phase 5's table scenarios compile a Full export unless they say Midcup
Decision (lead): a Phase 5 acceptance scenario naming no coverage tag compiles a `Full` export;
TC-BIN-31 to TC-BIN-33's patch halves are proven with the patch (step 5.3b), their table halves
before it; a new TC-BIN-37 pins the multi-CPK player-table walk.
Why: a code survey before briefing 5.3a found TC-BIN-25, 27 and 29 expect rows (gloves 0) a
`Midcup` export would not write, since a Midcup with no marker keeps a player's installed row
(`settings_toml.md`, the boots/gloves resolution), while the tests they restate compile a
Midcup; and no patch is written before 5.3b. The spec's "Bins accumulation" says a multi-CPK
compile walks the player tables from the bins CPK itself, keeping the seed rows of players no
export compiles, but the code's walk starts below it: unpinned by any scenario, so built
without a test until now.
Plan: `plans/team_compiler/README.md` "Acceptance" (the Phase 5 scope paragraph, TC-BIN-37).

## 2026-10-15 — team_compiler — the compiler does not report `fpc_custom_skin_on_non_fpc`
Decision (lead): the Team compiler passes the folder's `fpc_on` marker to `fpc::check` as
`is_fpc_player` and maps four of its five rules; the fifth, a custom skin on a player the
check is told is not hidden, is not reported.
Why: the catalog plan listed four rules and was silent on the fifth. In a compile the only
way to a custom skin without `fpc_on` is a `settings.toml` setting skin 7 on PES 15 to 17
(the Fox games narrow it to 1), which is the partial-hide setup (a custom body in a stock
jersey) that no marker names; a warning on it would fire on every such player and on nothing
else. A reader of a save, which has no marker, would classify with `ops::fpc::is_fpc_player`
(a custom skin counts as hidden) instead, under which the rule cannot fire either.
Also: `fpc_gloves_checkbox_winter_gloves` checks the gloves ID the boots/gloves resolution
gives; a `Midcup` player whose gloves keep his installed row is not checked, since `check`
reads no installed table and `check` and `compile` report a folder's findings alike.
Plan: `plans/team_compiler/messages.md`, the `fpc_inners_break_hiding` and
`fpc_gloves_checkbox_winter_gloves` rows.

## 2026-10-15 — aesthetics_export — the names marker is `write_names`, not `autopilot`
Decision (maintainer): the valueless root marker that opts an export's players' `name` and
`shirt_name` into the aesthetics patch is named `write_names`. Autopilot teams stay the
motivating case; one whose tactical export already holds the right names leaves it out.
Why: the marker controls what the compile does, not what the team is, and the two do not
coincide (an autopilot team with correct names needs no names written). A name that states
its effect reads right in an export folder and leaves `autopilot` free of a meaning it did
not have. Without the marker the patch is still written, carrying the players' motions.
Plan: `aesthetics_export/{player_folders,object_model,settings_toml}.md`,
`team_compiler/{pipeline,messages,README}.md` (TC-SAV-02, 03), `spec/pes_savefile/operations.md`
"Aesthetics patch", GLOSSARY "Aesthetics patch".

## 2026-10-15 — core — a GUI prototype may use what our planned UI crates can draw
Decision (maintainer): a prototype page is limited to the CSS and HTML elements that egui and
the UI crates of the planned dependency table can represent, not to egui's own widgets alone:
eased transitions (`egui_animation`), Markdown (`egui_commonmark`), native file dialogs and files
dropped on the window are allowed. An element only an unlisted crate can draw (sortable tables
need `egui_extras`) needs that crate added to the table first.
Why: the old list was stricter than the build: it forbade transitions the grid's fades and
`egui_animation` already plan, and left out the file drop the Export upgrader's view is made of.
The rule exists so a draft never promises what the implementation cannot draw; the crates we
will use are what decides that.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Prototypes before implementation".

## 2026-10-15 — team_compiler — Launch PES starts the exe from the game folder, never Steam
Decision (maintainer): the sideload mode's Launch PES button (and Phase 8's single launcher it
shares with `run_pes`) starts `PES20{version}.exe` from `pes_folder_path`; nothing goes through
Steam.
Why: launching through Steam is incompatible with the cup's mods, so every version is run from
its install folder; the "Steam URL, else the exe" wording contradicted the launcher plan.
Plan: `plans/team_compiler/gui.md` "Toolbar".

## 2026-10-15 — core — `egui_extras` joins the UI crates; hover cards, mixed formatting and sortable tables are representable
Decision (maintainer, on the lead's recommendation): `egui_extras` (0.36.2, `default-features =
false`) is added to the planned dependency table for `TableBuilder` (resizable, sortable,
sticky-header tables) and `StripBuilder`; the prototype rule counts as representable hover
cards (`UiBuilder::sense` with a `Frame`), mixed inline formatting (`LayoutJob`) and those
tables. Third-party egui crates (`egui_dnd`, `egui_plot`) wait for the tool that needs them;
free-layout crates (`egui_taffy`, `egui_flex`), toast crates, docking crates and theme crates
are not planned.
Why: the save editor's lists, the comparator and the AATF violations list are tables a member
wants to sort and resize; `egui_extras` is released with egui from its own repository, so it
cannot hold back an egui upgrade, which a third-party crate can. Hover cards and `LayoutJob` need
no crate (checked in egui 0.36.2), so listing them as not representable was stricter than egui.
Toasts would bypass the status bar's notices; free layout would mix two layout systems.
Plan: `plans/core/README.md` "External Dependencies", `plans/core/gui.md` "Prototypes before
implementation".

## 2026-10-15 — core — a light theme beside the dark default, both curated
Decision (maintainer): Studio has a light theme as well as the dark one, dark the default. Both
are curated `Visuals` presets in `studio_core`'s `theme.rs`, chosen by the common `theme`
setting (already `Dark`/`Light` in `CommonSettings`) and applied live; views take colors from
the presets' semantic palette, and prototypes are reviewed in both themes.
Why: the setting and a "dark/light" row existed, but the curated look was described as one
preset and the prototypes' stylesheet as dark only, so light would have been egui's plain
default with colors chosen for dark backgrounds.
Plan: `plans/core/README.md` "Styling is code, not CSS", `plans/core/gui.md` "Other UI
components" and "Prototypes before implementation".

## 2026-10-15 — core — correction: the light theme is second-class
Decision (maintainer), narrowing the entry above: only a small fraction of members use a light
theme, so dark is the one curated preset, the default, and the theme every view and prototype
is designed and reviewed in. Light stays available through the `theme` setting as egui's light
`Visuals` with Studio's accent, rounding and status colors, checked once for legibility; drafts
are not reviewed in it and the prototype stylesheet has no light toggle. Views still take
colors from the semantic palette, which keeps light readable at no per-view cost.
Why: designing and checking two themes per view would spend review time on a theme few
members see.
Plan: `plans/core/README.md` "Styling is code, not CSS", `plans/core/gui.md` "Other UI
components" and "Prototypes before implementation".

## 2026-10-15 — team compiler — the savefile step reports its write and a missing player; test mode skips it
Decision: a successful local savefile update is reported as `savefile_written` (I, the path and
the teams applied), and a patch player the save lacks (his team present) as
`savefile_player_missing` (E, the player id), beside `savefile_team_missing`. The step runs only
when the game loads the run's output: a normal-mode deployment that succeeded, or sideload mode;
test mode skips it with the other non-deploying runs.
Why: a step that changes user data and says nothing when it succeeds leaves the user unsure the
save was touched, while the patch and the CPKs each report themselves; dropping
`PatchSkip::PlayerNotInSave` silently would hide an unapplied player, which the save editor's
`apply-patch` already reports for the same patch (one rule in both tools). Test mode's loose
tree in `output/` is never read by the game, so writing the save would make it point at content
that is not installed, the incoherence the deployed-only rule prevents; sideload's `livecpk\`
tree is what the game loads, and TC-SAV-10 expects its savefile written once PES is closed.
Plan: `plans/team_compiler/messages.md` "Output stage and savefile", `plans/team_compiler/pipeline.md`
"Savefile update".

## 2026-10-15 — team compiler — the deployment transaction: old CPKs kept aside, sideload exempt
Decision: a deployment moves every old CPK aside to `{name}.cpk.old` (a one-CPK run too) and
removes the `.old` files only after the patch is written and the savefile step ends without
`savefile_invalid` or `savefile_write_failed`. Those two findings and `patch_write_failed`
roll the deployment back and are Fatal (`AbortRun`, exit 3); after a savefile failure the
staged CPKs are promoted to `output/` beside the patch, after a patch failure nothing more is
published. A stale `.old` from a killed run is left to the next run's move aside, which
replaces it (std's rename replaces an existing file on Windows too). Sideload
mode has no rollback: its savefile failures stay Errors, the new `livecpk\` tree in place.
Why: the plan makes the CPKs and the savefile one transaction (TC-SAV-05, 08, 09 expect the
previous CPK back and exit 3), and the one-CPK deployment's rename over the old CPK cannot be
undone once the savefile fails; moving it aside first costs one more rename. Keeping
sideload's previous tree would cost a copy of every model on each iteration of a mode that
exists for speed, and its savefile half catches up on the next compile anyway. A cleanup of
stale `.old` files was built and removed in review: only a read-only file or a folder at that
path defeats the rename, and a killed run leaves neither.
Plan: `plans/team_compiler/pipeline.md` "One transaction: CPKs, patch, savefile".

## 2026-10-15 — distribution — the platform floor is Windows 10 x64 and 64-bit Linux
Decision: Studio supports Windows 10 x64 and later, and 64-bit Linux; Windows 7 and 8.1 are not
targets, and the docs say so.
Why: the exe already cannot load on Windows 7 (Rust's standard Windows target imports
Windows 8+ functions, and the GUI stack imports `combase.dll`); reaching it would mean a
tier-3 Rust target (`x86_64-win7-windows-msvc`, built from source on nightly) plus patching
`windows-core`'s DLL name, a cost no member needs, since the cup's last Windows 7 users moved
to Linux, which the Linux build serves.
Plan: `spec/core/distribution.md` "Distribution: portable .7z bundle", the "Platform floor"
paragraph (the floor is a fact of the built exe, so it goes to the spec directly).

## 2026-10-15 — distribution — a static C runtime on Windows, `rhai` with `only_i64`, the release profile kept
Decision: every Windows MSVC build links the C runtime statically (`.cargo/config.toml`
`[target.x86_64-pc-windows-msvc] rustflags`), tests and the Python extension included. `rhai`
gains `only_i64`. The release profile stays the default (no LTO, unwinding kept).
Why: a dynamic CRT makes the exe need the Visual C++ redistributable, which a clean Windows 10
lacks and no doc told members to install; the static one costs 225 KiB. The flag on every
build, not only a release recipe, means the gates test the runtime the release ships. The
size growth (17.1 MiB on 2026-10-02 to 30.8 MiB) is features (`cargo bloat`, measured in the
spec), so the cuts were only those that change nothing observable: `only_i64` drops 627 KiB of
operators for integer types no script can produce, every host value being an `i64`; `no_float`
and the other `rhai` cuts were not taken, since they narrow what a ruleset's custom checks may
write. `panic = "abort"` would break the GUI's report of a panicked compile; LTO lengthens
builds, the opposite of the aim. Clean release builds measured 116 s before and 124 s after,
one run each: no build-time gain, and no difference one run can tell from noise.
Plan: `spec/core/distribution.md` "Platform floor" and "Size budget"; `spec/core/README.md`
"External Dependencies", the `rhai` row.

## 2026-10-15 — save editor — the session wiring only the view drives is built with the view (Phase 8)
Decision: Phase 5 delivers the Save editor's settings, CLI and the `session/` operations its
commands run; the wiring only the view drives (editing with the undo stack, selection, recent
files, tactics, the FPC toggle, AATF quick actions) is built in Phase 8, each piece in the slice
of the view that uses it. The development plan's Phase 5 bullet listed it under Phase 5 and its
verification asked unit tests of "the operations with no command"; both now say the above.
Why: found at the Phase 5 converge audit, with none of it built. Built now, each piece is a
layer with no consumer, its shape (what an undo entry holds, what a selection query returns)
guessed before the view that decides it, and reworked when the view lands; the save editor
plan's Acceptance already gave those operations their scenarios with the view. The lib-level
operations they wrap (`pes_savefile`'s model edits, `ops::fpc`, tactics) exist and are tested.
Plan: `plans/core/development_plan.md` "Phase 5" and "Phase 8"; `plans/save_editor.md` "Build
order and verification".

## 2026-10-15 — aatf — a `stat_bonus` choice option is used when a stat it raises is over its own target (correction)
Decision: corrects the entry of 2026-10-07 "VGL24 and VGL25 checked; optional effects as
one-option choices", which said a `stat_bonus` option is used when the player's rating is above
the expected rating. Since step 5.2i-r4 the interpreter uses it when, without it, a stat the
option raises is over that stat's own target.
Why: the rating comparison missed a stat whose tier override sits below the rate (VGL26's
silver place kicking): the player's rating fit while one stat broke its own target, so the
option a member would take went unused and the stat was reported. Found by SWE-2 review I.S2;
the plan's `Effects::choice` comment kept the old rule until the Phase 5 converge audit.
Plan: `plans/aatf_rules.md` "The ruleset schema", `Effects::choice`.

## 2026-10-15 — save_editor — `export-toml` refuses an `--out` that is the input save
Decision: `export-toml --out` naming the save it reads (the same file) is refused, exit 2,
nothing written (SE-TOML-09).
Why: refused, not backed up: the command's other outputs are Team TOMLs, replaced without a
backup by design, and a save replaced by TOML text is lost, where every command that writes a
save keeps a `.bak`. Found by converge review CE.S1.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "CLI", the `export-toml` bullet.

## 2026-10-15 — save_editor — a relative `aatf_rules` resolves in the data directory
Decision: a relative `aatf_rules` setting resolves in the data directory, as `teams_list_path`
does; `--rules` stays relative to the current directory (SE-AATF-04).
Why: the setting is one value the CLI and the AATF panel share; resolved against the current
directory, the same setting would read a different file depending on where `4cc-studio` was
started. One rule across tools: a user data file a setting names follows the settings file.
Found by converge review CE.S1.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "CLI", the `check-aatf` bullet.

## 2026-10-15 — team_compiler — a recordless Midcup with no shared folder writes no shared-IDs record
Decision: a `Midcup` export over installed CPKs holding no record of its team, with no shared
boots or gloves folder taking an ID, writes no `4cc_studio/shared_ids/<team>.toml` (TC-BIN-39).
A `Full` export still writes its record, empty or not.
Why: the empty record read, to the next Midcup above it, as the team having no shared folders,
so that Midcup's new folders took the main CPK's IDs without `shared_ids_unrecorded`. An empty
`Full` record is true (Studio built every folder), so it stays. Found by converge review CT.A1.
Plan: `plans/aesthetics_export/player_folders.md` "A `Midcup` export keeps the shared IDs the
team already has".

## 2026-10-15 — pes_savefile — a 15-17 texport reads the team and roster records, players in roster order
Decision: a 15-17 texport's team and roster records are read and written at their measured
offsets (the roster right before the tactics record, the team record before it, 17 with the
coach block between), and its player records are taken in the roster's order, each id checked
against its slot; the consecutive-id scan (`team * 100 + 1 + i`) goes.
Why: measured on all 46 15-17 texports of the reference machine; one real PES 16 file lists its
players out of id order, and the scan, our unmeasured rule, read 2 of its 23 players without an
error. Found by the Phase 5 texport census and review CP.S2b.
Plan: `plans/pes_savefile/operations.md` "Texport (read + write)".

## 2026-10-16 — core, music player — the suite absorbs outside tools; the player has no inbound API
Decision (maintainer, answering the QUESTIONS entry "An inbound control API for the music
player"): the suite takes in every tool the community uses, those released after it too, so an
outside program that would drive a Studio tool joins the suite and calls it in-process. The
Music player exposes no inbound control API; rigbot (managers' remote control of their team's
tactics), which drives the Rigdio fork's local HTTP API, becomes an unscheduled Studio tool.
Why: the maintainer's statement of the project's aim (one tool covering every other, new ones
included). An inbound API is a server and a wire contract to keep for a consumer the suite
will absorb, and the fork's handlers show its cost (tkinter driven from server threads). Phase
10 plans no control surface.
Plan: `plans/core/development_plan.md` "Unscheduled tools" (the rule, the rigbot bullet);
`plans/music_player.md` "Autopilot" and "Relationship to the old codebase" (the Rigdio fork
row); `plans/match_tracker/README.md` "Key decisions" (External consumers).

## 2026-10-16 — core, studio — the CLI draws a progress line and a run summary in a terminal
Decision (maintainer, on the lead's recommendation): in Phase 8 the console printer draws a
progress line on stderr from `Progress` and leaves a one-line run summary on `Complete`, only
when stderr is a terminal, with `indicatif` (`default-features = false`; the maintainer allowed it
if very light: measured at four small crates and about 145 KiB). Stdout is unchanged. No terminal
version of the progress grid.
Why: the few CLI users get the run's progress and counts at a glance, and stdout stays the finding
lines the CLI tests and scripts read; stderr in a terminal is the one place a redrawn line cannot
corrupt anything. The grid's value is colours and click-through, which a terminal cannot give
without a TUI library, for a handful of users whose finding lines already name each failing
folder. `indicatif` over a hand-written line because terminal width, the Windows console and the
draw-rate cap are already solved there, for a size cost under 0.5 % of the binary.
Plan: `plans/core/architecture.md` "Event system" (the console's progress line and run summary),
`plans/core/development_plan.md` "Phase 8: GUI", `plans/core/README.md` "External Dependencies".

## 2026-10-16 — pes_savefile — a player table is read as a CPK stores it, WESYS-wrapped or not
Decision: `PlayerTable::read` unwraps WESYS-wrapped bytes before reading rows (a stream that does
not unwrap is an error naming the table); `to_bytes` stays unwrapped.
Why: the census of every player table on the machine (worklog 5.6c1) found every game, PES 15 to
21, shipping its `BootsList.bin` and `GloveList.bin` wrapped; read as rows, PES 2020's wrapped
boots list is a whole number of pairs and reads as garbage with no error, and the Save editor's
`--bins` reads tables with no unwrap of its own (the Team compiler's walk unwraps every bin
first). The unwrap in the lib, not in each tool, because one rule in the reader holds for every
caller, where a per-tool copy is the gap this one was. Written unwrapped because every cup copy
is.
Plan: `plans/pes_savefile/model.md` "The Fox player tables".

## 2026-10-16 — cpk — a table string that is not UTF-8 is read as Latin-1, not refused
Decision: a CPK's @UTF string (an entry's directory or file name) that is not valid UTF-8 is read
