byte for byte as Latin-1, and the archive opens; `CpkError::InvalidUtf8` goes.
Why: the census of every CPK on the machine (worklog 5.6c2) found a cup's PES 2016 stadium pack
(`4cc_30_stadiums.cpk`, VGL7) naming one leftover file `au_seat cópia.dds` in a Windows code
page; refusing the archive stops a whole Team compiler run on such an install
(`installed_bin_unreadable`, Fatal) over a file the game never loads. Latin-1, not U+FFFD
replacement, because it maps each byte to its own character, so two such names never fold into
one path, and it reads the Western code pages' accented letters as they were meant. A CPK the
Save editor rewrites would carry such a name back in UTF-8; the bins CPK it rewrites holds none.
Plan: no plan edit needed: no plan or spec section describes the CPK reader's strings; the
crate's docs carry the rule.

## 2026-10-17 — review process — the Clef scan is retired, and SubQ Snap does not replace it
Decision (maintainer): the Clef scan leaves every review, the phase close's design-health pass
included; `scripts/clef_scan.py`, `scripts/clef_rulings.md` and the `just clef*` recipes stay
for re-measuring a model. No decision model takes its place yet.
Why: 88 ruled flags held two real defects, both scored below every flag at 0.80 or above, and
Phase 5's close pass raised 22 flags, all false; each flag cost the lead a reading. The
successor measured first, SubQ Snap (Subquadratic, public preview from 2026-10-12, 384K-token
window, $0.05 per million input tokens), separates one-line mutation-style slips better than
Clef (AUC 0.92 against 0.84 over 732 pairs; 254 against 150 caught with at most 10 clean
windows flagged) but not real defects: over 111 pairs from 63 of the project's fix commits
(the code before the fix against the code after) its AUC is 0.50 on the window, 0.51 on the
whole file and 0.50 with the spec sections the file cites (0.56 asked whether the code
contradicts those sections, 40 pairs), and Clef's is 0.51 on the window. On a whole-workspace
scan (1,512 windows at 53abc6f) the windows it scores highest were less often ones a later fix
changed (top 50: 10%) than windows overall (13%). A slip of the kind it catches breaks a
test, which the mutation runs already measure. As a pre-ruler of reviewer concerns it reaches
AUC 0.91 on 66 Phase 5 concerns, but the reviewer's own "edge case" mark alone reaches 0.875,
and what Snap adds reads the reviewer's hedging words; the lead still reads every concern, so
it saves nothing.
Plan: `CONTRIBUTING.md` "Clef scan"; `AGENTS.md` (converge's design-health pass, the sweeps).
The evaluation is outside the repository (`SystemOne/jev-eval/round3/RESULTS.md` "Round 4").

## 2026-10-17 — review process — a citation audit by SubQ Snap joins the phase close
Decision (maintainer): `just citation-audit` (`scripts/citation_audit.py`) runs in the phase
close's design-health pass: SubQ Snap is asked of every (scenario, citing test) pair whether
the test proves the scenario, the pairs under P 0.3 are flagged, and the lead rules each in
`scripts/citation_rulings.md` (accepted: widen or add the scenario, or move the citation).
Why: `acceptance.py` checks that a citation names a live scenario, not that the test proves
it, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` reads a citation as that proof; nothing else checked it. Measured on
the 732 citations at 7bd0bba against the same tests paired with the nearest scenario of their
family that they do not cite: AUC 0.995 with the test's same-file helpers attached and a
question that lets a test prove one of a scenario's listed cases (0.989 on the test alone,
which flagged 164, mostly helpers hiding the work and multi-case scenarios); 32 flagged, the
three lowest read in full all real, and both citations a commit had removed as wrong scored
under 0.3 (0.10, 0.15). Snap, not a reviewer model, because the question has its answer in the
two texts given and a decision model returns a calibrated probability for each of 732 pairs in
minutes for about $0.08; Astra reads the same pairs only inside a converge review, at the cost
of a review. Not a gate: it needs the network and a key. Its other measured uses failed (the
Clef scan's decision of 2026-10-17; spec drift, AUC 0.68).
Plan: `CONTRIBUTING.md` "Citation audit"; `AGENTS.md` (converge's design-health pass). The
evaluation is outside the repository (`SystemOne/jev-eval/round3/RESULTS.md` "Round 4b").

## 2026-10-17 — export_upgrader — the Red inventory's four open items settled before the acceptance section
Decision: (1) a kit whose binary config names another kit's back, chest, leg or name texture
gets a copy of it in its own folder (`kit_texture_copied`, I), before the `all/` hoist; (2) an
FMDL texture whose stem is only in `Common/` gets the stem and a `.common` link, whatever
directory the FMDL named; (3) the goalkeeper token `u0???g` is no variant set: a whole-export
upgrade respells its three ID characters as the resolved team's ID in names and paths, and
model-folder mode leaves it as written; (4) a second `gk:` Note entry and player entries past
the ninth are reported as unmigrated content.
Why: each keeps the upgraded export compiling as Red compiled the old one. Without (1) the 59
configs that borrow kit 1's fonts would compile kits with no numbers or names; without (2) a
texture Red found in Common would resolve nowhere. For (3), not a `kitN` rewrite, because Studio
has one kit number for every player and a fixed goalkeeper texture is a plain name; and not a
respelling to `XXX`, because nothing in Studio produces `u0XXX` (`spec/model_format.md`), while
the team's ID is what Red wrote and makes a model and a file that spelled it differently match
again. (4) has no Studio slot to land in.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` steps 5 and 7; its "Open items" section removed.

## 2026-10-17 — export_upgrader — generation, portraits and the CLI settled before the acceptance section
Decision: (1) a stripped Fox save's player is generated from his record like any other and named
in the report (I), his record's IDs resolving his wearers; (2) a version's range no game
measured (the PES 17/18 face caps, PES 19's other caps) is its field's bits, for generation and
the compiler's narrowing alike, so a stored value is written as stored, one past a key's widest
range left out and reported; (3) no `fpc_on` marker is written, FPC players migrating as raw settings and their own
models; (4) old portraits `player_???NN.dds` are renamed `player_NN.dds`; (5) the output's name
starts with the resolved team's key and the coverage tag, a tag already second is kept, and a
name equal to the source's gets ` upgraded`; (6) a team export takes exactly one of `--savefile`
and `--loose`; an existing output folder is refused; exit codes follow the Team compiler's
0/1/2/3; `--convert-to-gltf` is an unknown argument until Phase 7; (7) a Note's `Team:` line
naming no listed team is `team_name_unknown`, not skipped for the folder name; a referee export
is one whose first word is `refs`, and takes neither flag; settings are generated for the
player folders written, a player with no face folder and no custom boots/gloves getting none;
loose mode writes `name = true` alone for a folder with a name part, nothing otherwise;
(8) a prefixed face-folder portrait is renamed `portrait.dds`; a kit file naming no configured
slot, and a loose-mode ID past the inferred block, are unmigrated content; a non-archive input
file or an unreadable savefile is exit 2, an archive that does not extract exit 1; a Note kit
entry without a config becomes a colors-only placeholder kit, reported (W); (9) on a pre-Fox
export a single-wearer boots/gloves folder stays shared with a link; an xml-less folder's
models lose `oral_`/`_win32` and keep the `.mtl` Red chose; a game-directory texture reference
keeps its directory; a generated Common link sits at the model folder's root; (10) a `Kit
Configs/` subfolder is read as its root; a merge whose two folders share a file name of
different bytes stays shared with a link; a second folder of one ID is unmigrated; every
non-Common FMDL texture directory becomes the model's own folder; (11) a face folder's and a
kit config's three ID characters are any three, read by position; a name part is what follows
the ID with leading spaces and hyphens trimmed; a second face folder of one slot is unmigrated;
`Faces/Faces/`-style nesting is flattened; zlib-wrapped text files are written back wrapped;
(12) where Red discarded a whole `Kit Configs/`, `Kit Textures/` or `Logo/` folder for one bad
entry, the other entries migrate and the bad one is reported; (13) a team FMDL texture found
only in `Common/` gets a stem and a Common link, as Red's referee pass gave it, where Red's team
pass pointed it at the model's folder; a repointed stem that resolves nowhere stays the bare
stem, for the compiler's `fmdl_texture_not_found`; (14) a `u0???p0` file or folder becomes
`kitF`, a `u0???p0` path `kitN`; a referee export's `???` becomes 999; the "Other Notes"
header is read in any letter case; (15) a kit config whose slot no Note entry gives becomes
its kit folder, reported (W); (16) a stored boots/gloves ID 0 is written in a Midcup output
only; a `Common/` file a member `face.xml` names keeps its name; hoisting counts the empty
`p1`/`g1` a Full export is given; the upgrader compares a slot's two portraits itself;
(17) a referee's folded subfolders keep their place below the root, one landing as a refused
layout name being reported, and an unreferenced `common/` model is reported rather than folded;
(18) `upgrade`'s `-o` names the directory the output is written into, not the output folder;
an FMDL directory below the game's Fox common directory other than the team's is kept;
model-folder output is validated as if dropped into a Midcup export.
Why: the upgraded player must look as he did. (1) the compiler has never compiled an AET
team, so his rows are still the seed his record's bytes made; skipping him would write default
rows over his look at his next compile (worklog issue, review S5.10). (2) 79 players of the PES
18 fixture save hold values past the assumed caps (`cheek_type` 4 or 5, PES 19's measured
range), so an assumed cap would refuse their generation and reset their compile; a measured
cap stays, being what the game offers; the one known value past even the widest range (PES 16's
`goal_celebration_2` 183) stays refused, as the spec already rules. (3) the cup's FPC
teams give each player a blank boots ID of his own (2023 Winter Cup `/a/`), which the preset
match misses, while the strip fields alone also match dressed players; raw settings reproduce
both. (4) 2,248 of 2,271 old portraits carry the three ID characters, a name the compiler
refuses. (5) the compiler takes the team from the first word and the tag from the second, so
an old name kept whole ("Numbers") would not compile. (6) a silent loose fallback would guess
wearers the user never asked for; replacing an output would lose edits made since. (7) Red
stops on an unknown `Team:` line (`team_id_get.py`), which may say the export is another
team's; `refs` is the compiler's own identity rule; a player with no folder keeps the look the
game reads now, his record or his row, which a Full compile leaves standing. (8) the AET allows
the prefix and Red matches the suffix, while Studio reads the stem `portrait`; content with no
Studio home goes to step 10's report rather than a guessed place; the exit codes are the
compiler's for the same cases (`--export`, `export_extract_failed`); the Note's kit lines told
Red how many kits the team has (the AET page), so dropping one would change the kits offered.
(9) each keeps what Red packed: a member's `face.xml` would drop a merged pre-Fox model; Red
matched `.mtl` files against the unwrapped name (`xml_editing.py`); a stem alone would lose a
game texture's directory; a link mirrors `Common/` from its folder's root. (10) each is what Red
did (`export_check.py`'s flatten, its repeated-ID skip, `fmdl_model_folder_paths_fix`), and a
merge that would put two files on one path cannot keep both. (11) also Red's readings
(`export_check.py`'s positional slot and config grammar, `nested_folders_fix`); 1,034 real
face folders carry a baked ID, so an `XXX`-only reading would drop them. (12) and (13) are the
exceptions to that, where Red's output lost what the author shipped: (12) the real `CIV4XG`
VGL26 export lost every kit config to one `XXX_DEF_GK2nd_realUni.bin`, silently, while a
reported file is one the author can fix; (13) the team pass's repoint left the model without a
texture its export held, and a missing texture is an Error on Fox for every Studio export
(`spec/team_compiler/pipeline.md` "A texture a model names must exist"), which keeping the old
directory would only hide. The rest of the 2026-10-18 pass over the 5.0c Red inventory, re-read
on Red's released `main` (it had been read on the unreleased `dev/pre-studio-format` branch),
adds rules that are Red's:
the referee's own `common/` in reference resolution, the Note's grammar, a left Common path's
team ID, OS artifacts left out. (14) FoxDen's kit swapper keeps a `u0???p0` path whose variant
is missing, so that file was the fallback, `kitF`'s role, while a file named `kitN` is no
member of the set and the compiler would fill the gaps from the lowest variant instead (71 real
`u0???p0` files); Red compiled referees under 999; Red's case-exact `Other Notes:` lost a real
Note's `Other notes:` text, and the color headers are read in any case already. (15) Red packed
such a config and, counting the Note's entries, never offered the kit; dropping it would lose a
kit the author shipped, offering it adds one, and the report lets the author delete it.
(16) an unset ID in a Midcup export keeps the installed one, while an explicit 0 in a Full one
would override the hide preset of an author who adds `fpc_on` later; a member xml's path is
packed as written and PES 16 refuses one without `oral_` (`xml_oral_prefix_missing`), so the
sync Red's `update_xml_for_renamed_common_models` did would drop the folder; an empty kit
inherits `all/`, so hoisting past it hands a keeper a texture he never had; the compiler's
portrait comparison is its deep pass, which the upgrader's structural validation lacks.
(17) Red kept a referee's `common/` in his own common directory, where a model loads only when
named, so folded to the root an unnamed one would become a part of his face; a subfolder named
like the refused layout would be refused again (`player_layout_proto`). (18) the output's name
is its identity to the compiler, so an `-o` naming the folder itself could compile one team's
upgrade as another's, while a directory keeps the name derived and matches `upgrade-models`'
`-o`; Red keeps the whole `/Assets/pes16/model/character/common/` prefix and the compiler does
not look in the game's directories, so repointing `common/sourceimages/zero` would lose a
texture the game supplies; bare model folders are no export the shared validation reads.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` steps 1, 2, 5, 7, 8, 10 and 12, "CLI", "Acceptance";
`plans/aesthetics_export/settings_toml.md` "Player settings in exports".

## 2026-10-18 — export_upgrader — its own input read, and the gaps the first slice meets
Decision: (1) the upgrader reads its input through `archives::Archive::open` and a folder walk
of its own; the Team compiler's reader (`team_compiler/src/reader/`) stays private to the
compiler, no crate-boundary move. (2) The export's root is the input's own, or its one folder
when the root holds nothing an old export holds but that folder (folders and archives alike).
(3) The teams list is the data directory's `teams_list.txt`, else the embedded one; no setting.
(4) An output name equal to the export's own, letter case aside, gets ` upgraded`. (5) The
output is validated for the savefile's version (loose mode: PES 21, PES 16 with a `.model`), in
the compiler's default context. (6) A catalog of the run-level codes (`no_old_export`,
`unmigrated_content`, `migration_clean`, `migration_not_clean`, the compiler's
`export_extract_failed` and `team_name_unknown`); the shared validation's codes keep the
compiler's severities, run-dependent ones taken as for a deploying compile. (7) A migration is
clean when no finding is an Error and none drops anything, and only a clean one exits 0.
Why: (1) what the two share is opening an archive by extension, which `archives` already does,
and a 30-line walk; the rest of the compiler's reader is the compile's own (source revisions
checked mid-run, a memory budget for `.7z` buffers, a lock for parallel readers), and moving it
would make a leaf lib depend on `pipeline` and `aesthetics_export`. (2) EU-IN-01's archives
hold the export inside one main folder, as the AET page packs them, and one rule for both
input kinds gives the three forms one output. (3) a second setting could resolve an export
against another list than the compiler compiles it with, as another team. (4) Windows names
ignore case: `CO Full Spring`'s output would be the input folder. (5) the version decides only
which model names are allowed, and old exports are single-engine. (6) the CLI's exit codes
need a severity for every finding, and the output is judged as its first compile will judge it.
(7) "Verification" already calls a draft with a dropped scope unclean, and a Warning can drop a
folder (`player_unlisted`, `shared_folder_orphaned`): exit 0 there would tell a script the
export migrated whole while its compile loses the folder.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` steps 1 and 6, "CLI", "Message catalog" (new), "Verification".

## 2026-10-18 — team_compiler — the 5.0c Red inventory re-read on released Red: four premises corrected, one deviation added
Decision: the 5.0c inventory read Red's unreleased development branch (`e12aa01`); re-read on
released `main` (6.0c), these earlier entries' premises are corrected, their rules unchanged.
(1) 2026-10-11, the kit-texture path: released Red reports nothing and repoints the
`uniform/texture/` directory to the model's own folder, where the file is not, so its model
loses the texture silently; the Error the entry cites is the development branch's. Studio keeps
the path and warns. (2) 2026-10-11, `refs_txt_ignored`: released Red never opens a referee
export's `players.txt` (no error, no skip). (3) 2026-10-11, `+` splitting the team-name token:
released Red splits on `+` too, so this is parity, not a deviation. (4) 2026-10-04, blank faces:
released Red generates no face folder; the blank face is Studio's own rule (the development
branch's `copy_folder_contents` had it). (5) A deviation the 2026-10-11 list lacks: Studio reads
`refs.txt` with the strict roster grammar (a malformed line, a repeated slot, a slot outside
01-35 are Errors) where released Red skips a malformed line, lets the last of a repeated slot
win and bounds nothing.
Why: a premise taken from a branch no member ran describes no export's compile; the rules stand
on their own reasons ((1) a member is told why the texture is wrong; (5) a silently skipped
line, or a slot no game loads, is what an Error exists to show), so only the record changes.
The spec's attributions were corrected in place (`team_compiler/pipeline.md`, `blue_port.md`,
`libs/teams_list.md`, `libs/dds_convert.md`).
Plan: no plan edit needed: each rule's spec text already states the rule; the attributions are
fixed in the spec files named above.

## 2026-10-18 — export_upgrader — the first slice's review and the face-folder rules of 6.2a
Decision: (1) exit 3 also covers a file of the output that cannot be written mid-run: the error
names it and the incomplete output is left. (2) A file of the input that does not read after
its listing did is the compiler's `source_read_failed` (Error), the run going on without it,
unless it is the Note, which decides the team (nothing is then written); an archive that does
not open stays `export_extract_failed`. (3) A referee export's Note txt is
unmigrated content. (4) The output is validated in a fixed context, named as such, not "the
compiler's default". (5) A face folder's NN must be two digits making 01 to 23, else the folder
is unmigrated content as a whole; a second face folder of a slot is too, as one entry. (6) A
player folder name drops what a folder name cannot hold and trims a trailing `.` or space
(`T.O.M.` → `T.O.M`); a name source left empty counts as absent. (7) The save's roster is read
by player ID, never by position; an empty slot is `roster_slot_empty` (W). (8) The nested top
folder is flattened only when it is the folder's only entry, one level.
Why: (1) the copy steps write hundreds of files after the output folder exists, and a disk
full there is no refusal "before anything is written"; deleting the partial output would
delete what the user may want to inspect, while leaving it unexplained makes the second run's
"already exists" a mystery. (2) the code exists for exactly this in the compiler, and one file
failing should not cost the rest of the migration. (3) step 10 reports anything not migrated;
the Note was consumed and dropped without a word. (4) the compiler's file-type setting is on
by default, so "default context" invited a wrong correction. (5) Red refuses a face folder
outside 01-23 and errors on the repeat; reporting the folder once, not each file, names the
decision the user has to make. (6) the real PES 16 save's /co/ slot 23 is `T.O.M.`, which no
Windows folder name can end in, and `ScopePath` refuses. (7) the PES 16 texport fixture's
roster is out of slot order. (8) a flatten beside other entries would merge two trees with no
rule for their collisions.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` steps 1, 2, 3, 9, 10, "CLI", "Message catalog", "Verification".

## 2026-10-18 — export_upgrader — the boots and gloves folders' rules of 6.2b
Decision: (1) a boots folder's name is `k` and four digits, a gloves folder's `g` and four (or
three alone), then the name part; any other, and a model folder no rostered player wears, is
unmigrated content as a whole. (2) A merge kept shared for a byte clash is `merge_kept_shared`
(Info), the first clashing path in its context. (3) Two shared folders of one kind whose names
match, letter case aside, keep the name for the lowest ID; the others take their IDs. (4) The
name order holds for every player: face folder's name part, the worn boots folder's, the worn
gloves folder's, the save's name, the number. (5) Loose mode leaves the item folders unmigrated
until its wearer inference lands (6.7).
Why: (1) Red refuses any other name (`k####`, its `[1:5]` digits) and a folder nobody wears is
step 10's "unassigned model folder"; one finding per folder names the decision. (2) the step
said "reported (I)" with no code, and the path is what the author has to reconcile. (3) one
`Boots/Crocs/` would hold two models, a wearer of one loading the other's; the ID keeps both
recognizable. (4) a nameless face folder's player wearing `k0430 - Crocs` is the same author's
naming as a player without a face folder; two orders would be a rule nobody remembers. (5)
wearers then come from the IDs, step 11's own rules.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` steps 3 and 4.

## 2026-10-18 — export_upgrader — the kit configs' and kit textures' rules of 6.3a
Decision: (1) a second config of one kit slot (another ID spelling, or one below a `Kit
Configs` subfolder) is one config with the kit's when its bytes match and unmigrated content
otherwise, the kit's being the root's before a subfolder's, then the first by name; a file
deeper than one subfolder is unmigrated. (2) A config that does not decode is unmigrated
content, the decoder's error in the context (`error`). (3) A Kit Textures file is read by
position, as Red reads it (`u`, four characters, `p`/`g` and the digit, a rest empty or
starting with `_`, `.dds`), in any letter case; any other file, and the second by name of two
landing on one name, letter case aside, is unmigrated content. (4) `kit_config`'s `KitSlot`
reads a config entry suffix (`1st` … `GK1st`) itself, beside its `parse` of `p1` … `g1`.
Why: (1) two configs of one slot cannot both reach the game, and the plan already rules the
byte-equal pair one config; deeper files are what Red's one-level flatten left a folder,
which its name check refused. (2) a reported config is one the author can fix, as the
2026-10-17 entry (12) has it for bad entries. (3) Red checks `name[0] == "u"` and `name[5]` in
`p`/`g` and packs only `.dds` from the folder; a rest not starting with `_` would give a
generic name the shared validation refuses (`kit_texture_name_invalid`). (4) the suffix table
is the crate's (`config_name` writes it); a second copy in the upgrader would drift.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 5, "Message catalog".

## 2026-10-18 — export_upgrader — the Note's kit entries' grammar and the two kit Warnings of 6.3b
Decision: (1) a kit entry's colors split at each `-`: two colors, each read as a team color,
and an optional third part, a whole number 0-23 other than 3 giving `icon_<N>`, anything else
there giving no icon; one part, or more than three, does not read. (2) `kit_without_config` and
`config_without_kit_entry` keep what they name (`Keep`), the finding on the Note's file or on
the config's, context `slot`.
Why: (1) Red took the icon as the last number past the colors when it read 0-23 and dropped
it silently otherwise (`bins_update.py`), and the AET template writes no third part; four
parts is no entry the page describes. (2) a placeholder kit and a kit the Note never offered
are both migrated, not lost: a Warning that dropped would make every such run not clean,
against EU-KIT-09 and EU-KIT-13's exit 0.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 5.

## 2026-10-18 — export_upgrader — the kit-texture copy covers every field naming another texture (6.3c)
Decision: (1) a config's back, chest, leg or name field naming anything other than its own
kit's texture of that stem (another kit's, or another stem, the kit's own included) gives the
kit a copy of the named texture under the field's generic name (`kit_leg.dds` from
`p1/kit_back.dds`); `kit_texture_copied` (I) is on the config's file, context `kit`, `stem` (the
field's) and `from` (the source's kit and stem). (2) No copy when the named texture is not in
the output, or when the kit holds its own file of the field's name.
Why: (1) the census of the maintainer's 1,038 distinct old configs found 103 fields naming
another kit's same stem (the case the plan covered) and 59 naming another stem, the shipped
cases in MGGG (every leg field names `p1_back`), HSRG and JP's chest `_front` textures, a stem
the compiler drops: the compiler derives each field from its own stem's file, so without the
copy those numbers compile blank; one rule covers both. (2) a texture the export never shipped
has nothing to copy; a kit that ships its own file of that name was meant to wear it (MGGG's
goalkeeper ships its own back and name textures while its config, copied from kit 1, names
kit 1's), which is the simpler rule too, where letting the copy win would turn the kit's own
file into unmigrated content.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 5.

## 2026-10-18 — export_upgrader — two shared folders of one name and the same files become one
Decision: two shared boots or gloves folders whose names match, letter case aside, and which
hold the same files (the same paths, letter case aside, each byte for byte) become one shared
folder under the lowest ID's spelling, every wearer of either linking it; folders that differ
keep the 6.2b rule (the lowest ID keeps the name, the others take their IDs). The maintainer's
ruling, replacing 6.2b's (3) for identical folders.
Why: identical files are one model under two IDs, which the game already shows alike, so one
folder keeps every wearer's look and spares a copy, where the ID spelling kept a duplicate
named by a number the author never chose.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 4.

## 2026-10-18 — export_upgrader — the logo rule remeasured with the compiler's resampler, and its member grammar
Decision: (1) the logo comparison downscales through `dds_convert::resize`, the compiler's
resampler, so `export_upgrader` depends on `dds_convert`; the 40 % line stays. (2) The scenarios'
two closest real pairs become `/omg/` VGL26 (a downscale, 30 %) and `/vrg/` VGL26 (a variant,
53 %), replacing `/aceg/` (27 % now) and `/fgog/` (63 %). (3) A `Logo/` member is a file
directly in it whose name ends, in any case, in `_r_ll.png`, `_r_l.png` or `_r.png`, usable
when it decodes; other files and a second member of one role are unmigrated content; the
fallback takes `_r_l` before `_r`. (4) The share is reported on the `_r` file rounded to a whole
percent (`share`); the three logo codes and `portrait_conflict` keep both files (no drop), so
only `portrait_conflict`'s Error makes the run not clean.
Why: (1) the plan's numbers came from another resampler; measured with the compiler's own, the
94 distinct pairs on the maintainer's machine split 77 downscales at 0–30 % and 17 variants at
53–97 % (each pair from 30 % to 63 % checked by eye), so the line still sits in an empty band;
a second resampler would be the suite's second raster path, and its scores would drift from
the compile's. (2) the scenarios test the line with the nearest real pair on each side, so a
change to the resampler or tolerance fails a number. (3) the 149 such folders hold the AET
page's three emblems in 148 cases and a `Thumbs.db` beside them in the last; PNG is the only
format seen. (4) a dropped small logo is regenerated by the compile and a fallback logo is
written, so neither loses content.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 7, "Verification", "Dependencies", EU-MDL-02, -03.

## 2026-10-18 — export_upgrader — old `.mtl` references keep their extension, and a Common reference no link can spell is kept
Decision: (1) the upgrader no longer strips `.dds` from `.mtl` texture references: a name in
the model's folder (`./face_srm.dds`) and a game directory other than the team's Common stay
as written; a reference into the team's Common becomes the bare name (`./hair.dds`, or
`./jessie/hair.dds` for a Common subfolder) plus the link named after the `Common/` file. (2) A
Common reference no link can spell is kept as written, its `???` the team's ID, and reported
`common_reference_kept` (W, on the `.mtl`, context `reference`), as a reference whose file
`Common/` lacks already was: when the model's folder holds a texture or link of that stem on
the reference's nearest-first way up, or when a `.mtl` in a subfolder names a Common
subfolder. (3) An `.mtl` that does not parse or needs no change is copied as it is; a
rewritten one is written in `pes_model`'s layout, WESYS-wrapped again when it was (step 1).
Why: (1) the plan's stripping rested on "as required by the Studio format", which the spec
does not require ("Stem-based texture references": a reference's extension is ignored), and
the compiler puts `.dds` back only on a reference it resolves to a file of the export
(`prefox_face.rs` `point_materials`), so `model/character/boots/k0002/ek0062_n` would reach
the game with no extension, where the old path loads the game's own file. (2) a link beside a
local file of its stem is `texture_stem_conflict` (the folder dropped), and a nearer local
file would win the lookup silently: either way the model would change look; a subfolder
`.mtl`'s path below it and a link mirroring `Common/` cannot name the same place; keeping the
game path keeps what the export meant, the warning saying where. (3) a broken `.mtl` is the
compile's to report, as it was before the upgrade; copying untouched files keeps their bytes.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 7, EU-MDL-05.

## 2026-10-18 — export_upgrader — a shared folder's `.mtl` keeps its Common references, and a link needs one texture
Decision: (1) the `.mtl` files of a shared `Boots/` or `Gloves/` folder keep their references
into the team's Common as written, `???` respelled the team's ID, with no finding. (2) A Common
reference is linked only when the directory it names in `Common/` holds exactly one texture of
its stem; none, or two (`hair.dds` beside `hair.png`), keeps it with `common_reference_kept`.
Why: (1) review round 6.4.S2: the pre-Fox compile leaves a shared folder's `.common` links
unread until the cup next plays a pre-Fox version, and `.mtl` is pre-Fox alone, so a link there
would lose the texture the game path gets from the carried `Common/`. (2) a non-texture of the
stem gives a link that claims no texture, and two textures conflict in `Common/` and are both
dropped, so the link would dangle and drop the player folder.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 7.

## 2026-10-18 — export_upgrader — a WESYS-wrapped `face.xml` is written unwrapped
Decision: the upgrader writes every member `face.xml` unwrapped, whether a rewrite touched it
or not; a rewritten `.mtl` keeps its wrapper.
Why: the plan wrote both back wrapped, but the compiler parses a member's `face.xml` as plain
XML and reports a wrapped one `xml_broken` (E, the folder discarded): 48 such files on the
maintainer's machine would each cost a player his face at the first compile of the upgraded
export, where Red unwrapped them. The compiler's `.mtl` reader unwraps, so the `.mtl` keeps the
form its author shipped.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 1, EU-MDL-09.

## 2026-10-18 — export_upgrader — the kit magic's grammar, where it is renamed, and a Common kit set's link
Decision: (1) the legacy token is matched as Red's `path_id_change` matches it: `u0`, three
ASCII letters or digits, `p` and a digit (or `g`), case as written, anywhere and every
occurrence. (2) Names are renamed below player folders, shared folders and `Common/`; a renamed
path another output already takes (letter case aside) is the later input's, reported
`unmigrated_content`. (3) Only paths the export resolves (`./`, the team's Common) are
respelled; a game directory's are kept. (4) A Common reference whose respelled name is a `kitN`
reference links as `<name>.common` when `Common/` holds a member of its set. (5) A `face.xml`
changes only its `path`/`material` values; their `???` stays. (6) A `.mtl` in `Common/` is
treated as a shared folder's: its Common references keep their path, `???` respelled the
team's ID, with no finding.
Why: (1) the plan said "any three characters" without saying where or in what case; Red's
regex is what the exports were checked against. (2) silently overwriting one input with the
other would write a wrong file with no error. (3) a game directory's file is the game's, named
`u0<ID>p1` there (`uniform/texture/u0814p1.dds`, 176 references in one test folder, none in an
export), so a `kit1` spelling would find nothing. (4) /vg/'s Autumn 24 export names
`common/XXX/u0XXXp0.dds` with `Common/u0XXXp1.dds` to `p3`: without the set rule the reference
matches no single texture and is kept unlinked, its `u0XXXp0` gone from the renamed `Common/`.
(5) the compiler replaces any three characters of a `face.xml` Common path with the team ID
already, and a byte-for-byte copy elsewhere keeps the `<dif>` and every attribute the compiler
passes through. (6) the compiler emits a member's `.mtl` as written, so a Common `.mtl`'s `XXX`
would reach the game, where Red respelled it (`txt_id_change`); 343 such references sit in the
maintainer's 1,489 `Common/` `.mtl` files, and a link has no place in `Common/`.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 7, EU-MDL-16, "Dependencies" (`roxmltree`, already the
workspace's XML reader).

## 2026-10-18 — export_upgrader — an FMDL's texture entries, class by class
Decision: per texture entry of a migrated FMDL: a `dummy_` stem is left as written; a `./`
directory has its kit magic respelled only; the game's kit texture folder
(`/Assets/pes16/model/character/uniform/texture/`) is kept; the team's Common
(`common/<3>/[sub/]sourceimages/`) is linked as a `.mtl`'s Common reference; other directories
below `common/` are kept; every other directory becomes `./`, linked to the `Common/` root's
texture when the model's folder holds none of the stem. A shared folder's FMDL links as a
player folder's; a `Common/` FMDL gets the shared `.mtl` rule.
Why: the plan said "every other FMDL texture directory becomes the model's own folder", which
would repoint the 25 real FMDLs naming the game's kit texture folder at a file the folder lacks,
so `fmdl_texture_not_found` would drop the model where the compiler keeps that path on purpose
(`fmdl_texture_kit_path`). `dummy_` stems are game-supplied and never looked up. A census of the
6,053 FMDLs in export folders (`.tmp/6_4/fmdl_dir_census.txt`) found no directory naming a
subfolder of the model's folder outside one test export, Common subfolders spelled with
`sourceimages/` after the subfolder (`common/000/Boots/sourceimages/`, 117 boots FMDLs), and
kit magic in Common subfolders (`common/000/u0XXXp0/sourceimages/`, 45). The Fox compile reads
a shared folder's links (`shared_texture_claim`), unlike the pre-Fox one.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 7.

## 2026-10-18 — export_upgrader — a kept Common reference that clashes is worn as the folder's texture, and `dummy_` stems are no Common files
Decision: (1) a Common reference kept because the folder already holds a texture of its stem
stays kept, and `common_reference_kept`'s text says the folder's texture is the one the model
will wear. (2) A `.mtl`'s `dummy_` stem in a Common path has its `???` respelled alone: no
lookup in `Common/`, no finding.
Why: (1) Astra round M-A1: the compiler looks a game path's file name up in the folder first
(`point_materials`, as `spec/model_format.md` "Stem-based texture references" says), so keeping
the path does not keep its target, as the plan had claimed; changing the compiler's lookup for
a rare layout is not worth a spec change, while a warning that says what happens is enough for
an export that gets a human look anyway. (2) the game supplies `dummy_kit*` textures, so the
lookup reported a false `common_reference_kept` on real files (/jp/ Summer 25 `XXX15 -
Sister`); the compiler emits a member's `.mtl` as written, so the `???` still needs the ID.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 7.

## 2026-10-18 — export_upgrader — a pre-Fox leading type moves only when `_` follows it, `model_type_` names stay, `.mtl.common` links follow their target
Decision: in the type swap of step 7, (1) a leading type is recognized only when `_` and more
of the name follow it (`gloveL_foo` → `foo_gloveL`); a glued one (`eyebrow_x`) is left as
written. (2) A name holding `model_type_` is left as written. (3) A `.mtl.common` link is not
renamed with a model of its folder; it follows its `Common/` target. (4) A `Common/` file that
a link in a folder with a `face.xml` names keeps its name, as one the `face.xml` itself names
does. (5) A shared boots or gloves folder
gets both renames, as an xml-less player folder does.
Why: (1) Red matched the type with no delimiter, so `eyebrow_x` was typed `eye`; moving letters
off a word makes a name nobody wrote, and a census of the maintainer's exports
(`.tmp/6_4/model_names_census.txt`) found 185 delimited leading types and no glued one among the
856 models of xml-less face folders. (2) the plan said the `model_type_` token moves to the end,
but Red and the compiler (`xml_type`) both read everything after it as the type, so it is in
place wherever it stands and a move would change the type (Red read it only when no leading
type matched, the compiler always: `gloveL_model_type_x` changes type either way); the census
found no such name. (3) a link to a name that moved names a missing file: its target is
renamed only when it follows a swap-renamed `Common/` model (one real `.mtl.common`, a test
folder; round 6.4.S6-2). (4) that link is left as written with its folder, so renaming its
target would break it; no real export has one, and the rule costs one set entry. (5) it holds
no `face.xml`, and validation refuses a boots or gloves model whose name does not end in its
type (`model_name_invalid`, the folder dropped with its wearers' links): EU-PLY-08's
`oral_boots_win32.model` failed so. Real old boots folders hold `boots.model` (221) and
`boots_edit.model` (158, mostly in model folders; the Edit-mode model is an open pre-Fox parity
item of the worklog), so the rename rarely fires there.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 7.

## 2026-10-18 — export_upgrader — an author's `kit1` beside a legacy kit token is written `Kit1`
Decision: in a name segment that holds a legacy `u0???pN` token, every Studio kit token already
there (`kit1`-`kit9`, `kitN`, `kitF`, as the kit token grammar reads one) has its `k` written
`K`, in file names and in `.mtl`/`face.xml`/FMDL references alike (`kit1_u0827p0.dds` →
`Kit1_kitN.dds`, `Common/kit1_u0827p1.dds` → `Common/Kit1_kit1.dds`).
Why: Astra round M-A2: five VGL26 exports in the maintainer's lab (`UMAJP`, `ESG`, `1999`, `PG`,
a guest boss export) name kit-dependent textures `kit<K>_u0XXXp<N>`; respelled as they were, a
stem's first token, the author's `kit1`, is its kit token, so the reference read as variant 1,
no set link was planned and the model pointed at nothing. Upper-casing keeps the author's word
and the file names distinct, while the token grammar (spelled exactly) no longer reads it;
dropping or renaming the fragment would lose what it says, and a set token the grammar picks
by position would change a rule the compiler and validation share.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 7 (the kit magic).

## 2026-10-18 — export_upgrader — step 8's codes, the Midcup scope of a missing custom model, and a claimed ID left out
Decision: (1) step 8 reports `custom_model_missing` (E), `settings_value_refused` (W),
`settings_from_stripped_record` (I) and `settings_not_generated` (E), each with the slot and the
player's name. (2) a worn custom ID no migrated folder claims is checked for every rostered
player of a Full output, but in a Midcup output only for a player the output gives a folder.
(3) a boots or gloves ID a migrated folder claims is left out of `settings.toml` whatever its
value, a stock-band one included. (4) `name = true` is written when the player name the
compiler derives from the output folder's name (`aesthetics_export`'s rule) equals the save's
raw name.
Why: (1) the plan named the findings' severities but no codes. (2) a Midcup compile leaves a
player without a folder as installed, his custom content included, so checking him would flag
every Midcup export's other players and exit 1 on content nothing loses; a Full compile
rebuilds the team from the export alone, so there the missing model is lost. (3) the plan kept
a stock ID "which no folder carries", silent on a folder spelled with a stock-band ID; written
beside the folder, the key is ignored at every compile (`settings_model_id_conflict`) and says
nothing. (4) one rule with the compiler's own derivation, not a second reading of the folder
name that could drift from it (a name part with a hyphen, a folder named by its number alone).
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 8.

## 2026-10-18 — pes_savefile — an unmeasured face-type cap is the field's bits in `face_type_cap` itself
Decision: `face_type_cap` returns the field's bit maximum for every version whose cap no game
measured (PES 17 and 18 for all eleven types, PES 19 for all but cheek and forehead), so the
compiler's per-version narrowing, the cross-version conversion and Team TOML's import all keep
a stored value inside the field. The in-game hair half of the same plan rule waits for a real
value past PES 21's range.
Why: Astra round 6.5.A1: the upgrader generated a PES 18 cup player's `cheek_type = 5`
(EU-SET-05) and the compiler's narrowing, on the assumed cap 3, reset it to 0 at his first
compile, against `plans/aesthetics_export/settings_toml.md`. One table changed at its source,
not a second "bits" table beside the narrowing, so the three readers cannot disagree on what a
version accepts (a conversion to PES 18 capping what its compile keeps). The hair keys share one
range over every version and no fixture player exceeds it, so a per-version hair table would
be built for no value seen. Two delivered scenarios built on the assumed caps change with it:
TC-BIN-31's PES 18 run keeps a facial hair type 20 (its PES 21 run now narrows it), and
SE-TOML-05's capped value is a goal celebration, since no document can hold a face type past
PES 18's cap any more.
Plan: `plans/aesthetics_export/settings_toml.md` "Player settings in exports (settings.toml)"
(the hair half); the built half in `spec/pes_savefile/operations.md` "Cross-version player
conversion" and `spec/aesthetics_export/settings_toml.md`; TC-BIN-31
(`spec/team_compiler/README.md`), SE-TOML-05 (`spec/save_editor.md`).

## 2026-10-18 — music_export — the plan's "Model" is the code's copy; items with no planned consumer are crate-private
Decision: `music_player.md` "Model" (and "File resolution") carries every type and signature
the crate exports, copied from the code: the condition and instruction vocabularies,
`parse`/`write` and their result types, `Side`/`TeamState`/`MatchState`, `Verdict` and the
`eval` methods, `Loaded`/`Press`/`PriorityList`, `Resolution` and the two `resolve_*`
functions. `Press<'a>` keeps its lifetime, the crate's one struct lifetime, now named by the
plan. Six items with no consumer in the player's or the editor's plan become `pub(crate)`:
`Comparison::holds`, `SongEntry::is_once`, `TeamState::has_most_goals`, `TeamState::clear`,
`MatchState::lead` and the `Loaded::fallback` field; `write`'s `condition_text` and
`instruction_text` stay `pub(crate)` until the editor's chips need them. `resolve_song` joins
a song's subfolder once, after reading `\` as `/`, so a path anchored by a leading separator
or a drive is used as written (a join's rule), where the split-and-fold it replaces put it
under the export's folder.
Why: the crate was built ahead of its phase from a section naming three shapes, and a
consumer written at Phase 10 against the plan would otherwise be written against what a
session remembered. A press is a one-call parameter bundle: borrowing the button's name is
what a function argument does, and an owned `String` would allocate per press for nothing.
The narrowed items are evaluation and selection internals; `CONTRIBUTING.md` makes `pub`
crate API, and widening one when a consumer appears is one word. The anchored-path rule is
the plan's standard (`os.path.join` does the same) and no export on the machine has one (0 of
1,808 song lines name a subfolder at all), so the simpler form wins over a rooting no file
needs.
Plan: `music_player.md` "Model", "File resolution".

## 2026-10-18 — music_export — a `_normalized` companion is matched by stem, any extension; the entry `advance` skips is not drawn; a root-level anchor holds
Decision: `resolve_song`'s companion is any file of the song's folder whose stem is
`<stem>_normalized`, case-insensitively, whatever its extension, the song's own extension
preferred when there are several, and among equal ranks the smallest name (the listing's
order, which `songCheck` takes, is the filesystem's and differs between NTFS and ext4); names
fold with `to_lowercase`, Unicode included, in both lookups; a path anchored by a leading
separator or a drive is used as written whether or not it names a subfolder (the whole path
is joined for the folder, the name taken as written, so `sub/` resolves nowhere rather than to
the subfolder); under `randomise`, the entry that just ended (`Press::skip`) counts for the
all-entries check and is left out of the draw.
Why: Astra round 10.0e.A1. `songCheck` (the Rigdio fork's `rigparse.py`) compares
`splitext(file)[0]` with `<stem>_normalized` and never the extension, and real exports lean
on it: IZAKAYA's `izakaya.4ccm` names 17 `.mp3` songs each beside an `X_normalized.opus`,
DNG's one, which the extension-bound rule silently resolved to the plain file. The root-level
case was the half of S1-1's rule the first form missed (`/song.mp3` split into an empty
parent). A drawn repeat of the entry that just ended is what `advance` exists to prevent; no
readable export combines the two instructions, so the fix is the smaller one (filter the
draw, keep the check).
Plan: `music_player.md` "File resolution", "Song selection (per button press)" step 3.

## 2026-10-18 — core — the folder watcher and the check cache live in `libs/pipeline`
Decision (side-lead, 8.0): the exports folder watcher (`notify` + debouncing) and the check
cache (the manifest fingerprint and what it keys) are `libs/pipeline`'s, as the spec's crate
tree said; the Team compiler's planned `check/watcher.rs` goes, and its `check/` only decides
what to check when and maps results to rows. Their design stays in `plans/team_compiler/gui.md`
"Live validation".
Why: two plan files named two homes. The Balls compiler's list view watches its folder the
same way (`plans/balls_compiler.md` "GUI"), and tool crates never depend on tool crates, so a
watcher in `team_compiler` would be copied there; `pipeline` is "the scaffolding every
compiling tool runs on" and already names the pair. The design text stays with the grid
because the grid is what the watcher and cache exist for, and a second copy would drift.
Plan: `plans/team_compiler/README.md` "Crate layout"; `plans/team_compiler/gui.md` "Live
validation"; `spec/libs/pipeline.md` (the consumers named); `plans/core/development_plan.md`
"Phase 8".

## 2026-10-18 — core — `ST` is the shell's acceptance code; TC-GUI-02 and -03 are automated
Decision (side-lead, 8.0): the shell's scenarios carry the code `ST` and live in
`plans/core/gui.md` "Acceptance" (the shell is no tool, so no tool plan owns them). TC-GUI-01
is narrowed to what needs a display (the window opening, `run_gui`); TC-GUI-02 (the Compile
click runs the CLI's `compile`, the log shows its lines then the exit code) loses `manual` and
is cited by `team_compiler`'s headless compile-click test, and the new TC-GUI-03 (a sidebar
click shows the tool's view; the settings section, the Compile button and the log) is cited by
the shell's and the view's headless tests. TC-GUI-02's former deployment clause goes: what the
run writes is TC-DEP's and TC-OUT's, through the CLI path the button shares.
Why: CONTRIBUTING's rule is "prefer an automated proof whenever the UI toolkit allows one";
3.z's headless harness proves everything in the two scenarios but the native window, and the
worklog's manual lines were proving by hand what a test proves on every run. The deployment
clause was never what the headless test could or should observe twice.
Plan: `spec/team_compiler/README.md` "Acceptance" (shell slice); `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md`
"Testing" (the `ST` code); `plans/core/gui.md` "Acceptance".

## 2026-10-18 — workspace — `eframe` and `egui` pinned exact; `egui-wgpu` stays undeclared
Decision (side-lead, 8.0): `[workspace.dependencies]` pins `eframe = "=0.36.2"` and
`egui = "=0.36.2"`; `egui-wgpu` is not added. The spec's "egui version discipline" said to pin
all three.
Why: a caret pin already excludes the next minor (where egui renames); what it let through was
a patch release moving on a bare `cargo update`, unreviewed, which the exact pin stops.
`egui-wgpu` is `eframe`'s own dependency and requires `egui = "0.36.2"` (its `Cargo.toml`), as
the crates built on egui require the `egui` of their release, so the exact `egui` pin already
holds it (checked: `cargo tree --locked` resolves unchanged with the exact pins); a third pin
would be a second place to bump for no extra hold. egui's own dependencies (`epaint`, `emath`)
stay caret-required by egui and are not held; nothing here calls them directly.
Plan: `spec/core/gui.md` "egui version discipline"; `Cargo.toml`.

## 2026-10-18 — save editor — a color field is `color_tools`' picker
Decision (side-lead, 8.0): the Save editor's color fields (team colors 1 and 2, skin, iris,
wrist tape) are `color_tools`' color-picker popup, not the "RGB field" the crate's `widgets.rs`
line planned. The picker therefore has a Phase 8 host, and Phase 8's bullets name both
`color_tools` widgets (the picker, and the kit menu icon rendering the grid's kit cells draw).
Why: `color_tools`' plan dated both widgets Phase 8 but named only Phase 12 and 17 consumers
for the picker, which made it a `pub` item with no caller for two phases; the Save editor's
Appearance and Team tabs need a color field in Phase 8, and one picker across the tools is the
"consistent rules across tools" rule applied to a widget.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Crate layout"; `plans/libs/color_tools.md` "Color-picker widget";
`plans/core/development_plan.md` "Phase 8".

## 2026-10-18 — export upgrader — the view is the two commands as drop targets with the report as its product
Decision (side-lead, 8.0): the Export upgrader's view (`plans/export_upgrader.md` "GUI") is two
drop targets (an export; a folder of model folders), the CLI's arguments and nothing more (a
savefile field prefilled from `pes_savefile::discovery` for the selected version, the loose
switch, an output folder field), an Upgrade button running the command through the CLI's own
parser on a thread of its own, and the report: the console's lines in the log panel and an
unmigrated-content list above it. No settings section.
Why: the plan had one sentence ("two drop targets"), and the draft needs a layout to start
from. The CLI path, not a second code path, because the shell slice's rule (the button cannot
do what the command line refuses) already holds for the compiler; the unmigrated list as the
view's centre because that report is the one output a member acts on by hand. The savefile is
prefilled from discovery rather than remembered as a setting because the tool has no settings
and the save of the selected version is what a member means nine times in ten. The draft
review is where the maintainer reshapes it; a handoff to the compiler after a clean upgrade is
not decided here (`QUESTIONS.md`).
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` "GUI", "CLI" (the pointer), "Acceptance" (Phase 8 scope).

## 2026-10-19 — save editor — only the RGB color fields are `color_tools`' picker
Decision: amends 2026-10-18 "a color field is `color_tools`' picker": the picker serves the
Save editor's colors the save stores as RGB (the team colors, the only RGB fields its tabs
draw: the in-game face run's hair, eyebrow and facial-hair colors are outside the Appearance
tab's 4ccEditor contents), the host rounding a picked 8-bit channel to the save's 6 bits
(`c * 63 / 255`) and showing a stored one widened (`v * 255 / 63`); a color stored as a palette
index (skin, iris, wrist tape, spectacles, gloves, hair accessory) is a choice of its palette's
entries.
Why: the rule follows the storage kind, not a list of fields: a palette index cannot hold a
free color from a picker (`settings.toml`'s `skin_color` 0-7, `iris_color` 0-10, the wrist-tape
and gloves colors 0-7), while an RGB field can (Astra 8.0.A1-1, SWE-2 8.0.S7-3, S8-4, S8-5,
S9-1). The picker keeps its Phase 8 host in the team colors, whose channels `write_team`
refuses above 63, so an unconverted #FF0000 would fail to save (Astra 8.0.A2-2).
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Crate layout"; `plans/libs/color_tools.md` "Color-picker widget";
`plans/core/development_plan.md` "Phase 8".

## 2026-10-19 — core — a run's events wake the GUI on emit
Decision: the shell installs a GUI-neutral wake callback in every `ToolContext` it hands out
(taking a delay, calling `egui::Context::request_repaint_after`): `ToolContext::emit` calls it
with no delay after each send, and a tool's own deadlines call it from `tick` through
`ToolContext::request_repaint_after`; a tool's view no longer requests repaints while its run
is in flight. A run's verdict is the last message on its own channel, sent before a wake, not
read from its thread's `JoinHandle`.
Why: egui repaints only on input, and a view not drawn (another tool active, the window
hidden) requests nothing, so a run's last events, or a hidden tool's timer, waited for
unrelated input; waking from the context is the match feed's rule (its wake callback on
publish), one rule for every background source rather than one per view (Astra 8.0.A1-2,
SWE-2 8.0.S7-2). The verdict travels as a message because `is_finished` can still be false
in the frame the last event woke, and a preflight refusal emits no event at all (Astra
8.0.A2-1).
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Event wiring"; ST-TTL-03, TC-GUI-22.

## 2026-10-18 — export_upgrader — steps 9 and 12's gaps: the missing roster's code, the `players.txt` writer, and what a folder left as it was keeps
Decision: (1) a `refs` export without a `refs.txt` is `refs_txt_missing` (E, the export
dropped, nothing written). (2) `players.txt` is written by the upgrader itself: every nonblank
line of `refs.txt`, a line that parses (an all-digit head) as its slot in two digits, one space
and the trimmed rest, any other line as written; a `refs.txt` that is not UTF-8 is
`unmigrated_content` and no `players.txt` is written. (3) a referee folder step 12 leaves as it
was is copied at its old paths and skipped by step 7's renames and rewrites. (4) a `common/`
model is "named" when a `face.xml` anywhere in the referee's folder has a `path` value whose
file name, `*` read as `win32`, is the model's, folded. (5) the stem conflict the fold creates
counts only two files from different locations. (6) in a referee's `.mtl`, `face.xml` or FMDL,
a Common reference whose path the flattened folder holds becomes `./<sub>` with no link and no
finding, wherever the file came from. (7) the respelling takes the export's identity, 999 for
referees, not a `TeamId`.
Why: (1) the plan named the outcome but no code; `no_old_export` is false (the export holds
`Players/`) and `players_txt_missing` is the output validation's. (2) a line the upgrader
cannot parse is not its to interpret: written as it was, the shared validation reports it on
the output with its line, where a dropped line would be silent; `aesthetics_export` has only
the reader, and a three-line writer earns no library function until the Refs arranger is built.
(3) "left as it was" is literal: a folder the author must repair by hand with names moved
under him hides what the report named, and the renames would follow the fold anyway once he
has resolved it. (4) a face.xml `path` is the only reference that names a model; its `*` is
the compiler's reading. (5) two textures of one stem already inside one location are the
compile's `texture_stem_conflict` for any folder; the fold made only the cross-location one.
(6) the compiler looks a folder's own file up before a game path, so a file from `face/` and
one from `common/` resolve the same once at the root; one rule, not a record of where each
file came from. (7) `TeamId` is strictly 701-920 and cannot carry 999 (round 6.4.S3-4).
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` steps 9 and 12.

## 2026-10-18 — export_upgrader — a referee `face.xml`'s `./` reference to a `Common/` file is left as written
Decision: step 12's "a `./x` whose file is only in the export's `Common/` gets step 7's stem and
link" applies to an `.mtl`'s and an FMDL's textures; a referee `face.xml`'s `./x` (a `path` or
a `material`) is left as written. Its Common-path values whose file the flatten moved into the
folder still become `./<rest>`.
Why: the compiler resolves a `face.xml` `path` among the folder's own `.model` files
(`team_compiler/src/user_face_xml.rs` `resolve`: a `.mtl.common` link counts for a `material`,
no link counts for a `path`), so a `.model.common` link would resolve nothing and the plan's
sentence, read for a `face.xml`, names a spelling the compiler does not read; the miss is
reported loudly (`xml_model_not_found`, the folder dropped), and every `./` value of the 69 real
referee xmls names a file of its own face folder (`.tmp/6_6/refs_xml_census.py`: 532 such
values, 64 Common-path ones naming the export's `Common/refkit/`), so machinery for it would
serve no file seen. One rule for the two kinds the link does serve, not a per-attribute table.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 12.

## 2026-10-19 — export_upgrader — the refs-compiler layout (`Refs list.txt`, referee folders at the root) migrates too
Decision: a root `Refs list.txt` (any letter case) is read as the referee roster when there is
no `refs.txt`, and when a referee export has no `Players/` folder, every root folder step 1
does not know (not `Common`, `Other`, the kit, item or image folders) is a referee folder;
step 12's flatten and the rest of step 9 apply unchanged. Step 1 counts `Refs list.txt` among
what an old export holds.
Why: SWE-2 round 6.6.S1 listed four of the eleven real referee exports on the maintainer's
machine (`C:\Data\4cc\Refs\25_{1,2,3,4}-*_refs\exports_to_add\refs for *`, Winter to Summer
25) in that layout, the one the earlier "4cc refs compiler" read, each referee's folder the
same `Face/` + `Common/` the Red layout has; refused as `no_old_export`, a `refs`-named export
with a roster got a false diagnosis, and step 9's purpose is to migrate the maintainer's
referee exports. Two aliases (the file's name, the folders' place) rather than a second layout
rule, since nothing else differs.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` steps 1 and 9.

## 2026-10-19 — core — a tool with unsaved work vetoes the window's close
Decision: closing the window, by the member or by the shell itself (the quick-compile close on
success), asks every tool through a `StudioTool` hook beside `version_change_blocker`; one
holding unsaved work makes the shell cancel the close and switch to it, and its own prompt
decides: save or discard sends a close request back (a `ShellRequest`), which asks every tool
again, so a second tool with unsaved work prompts in turn; cancel keeps the window. A tool
with a run in flight (a compile, an upgrade) reports it through the same hook; its prompt
offers to close once the run has ended, cancelling it first where the tool has a Cancel (the
Team compiler; an upgrade has none and runs to its end), or to keep the window.
Why: the prompt is the tool's view, which the shell draws only for the active tool, so a close
decided by the shell alone dropped the Save editor's edits whenever another tool was in view
(SWE-2 8.0.S7-5). A hook, not a shell-owned prompt, because what "unsaved" means and how it is
saved are the tool's. A run in flight is asked about because an exit cannot discard its
staging as a cancel does, and one killed while deploying can leave a torn output (SWE-2
8.0.S9-3); the real tools each get a scenario of their own (Astra 8.0.A2-3).
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Cancellation" ("Closing the window"); SE-GUI-05, ST-RUN-05,
ST-RUN-06, TC-GUI-23, EU-GUI-07.

## 2026-10-19 — save editor — the GUI's Texport export writes PES 18-21
Decision: Texport export is offered on PES 18-21 saves, from `Texport::new`'s templates; on a
PES 15-17 save it is disabled with a tooltip saying those versions have no template.
Why: `Texport::new` returns `NoTemplate` for 15-17, whose files can only be written over a real
one the game exported; a flow that first asks for such a file is machinery no member has asked
for, and a disabled action with its reason fails loudly rather than late (SWE-2 8.0.S7-6).
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Interchange formats in the UI"; SE-GUI-29.

## 2026-10-19 — dds_convert — the GPU BC7 encoder is built ahead of 0.1.0, unwired, on Vulkan/Metal with bounded submissions
Decision: step 16.x's encoder half is built now in `dds_convert` (native only, behind
`cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))`): `block_compression`'s `wgpu` feature and a workspace `wgpu`
entry (30.0.1, the version eframe already resolves, so no new crate enters the build); the
device is started on its own thread on Vulkan (Metal on macOS) with no DX12 or fallback
adapter, a software one (`DeviceType::Cpu`) refused too; each submission encodes a bounded
slab of rows; a failure, a lost device's panic inside wgpu included, falls back to the CPU from
the mip it hit on and leaves the encoder unavailable with its reason. The Team compiler's wiring
stays after Release 0.1.0, which ships the CPU encoder only.
Why: the probe (`.tmp/16x/findings.md`) measured Vulkan at ~33x the whole CPU's BC7 throughput
at the same quality, a cold pipeline build the driver caches after its first process (16.3 s,
then 27 ms), and DX12 worse on every count, with one unbounded 6 s submission losing the
device; the encoder is independent of the release's features, and building it while the
measurements are fresh costs less than rediscovering them in Phase 16. A cost estimate does
not pick CPU or GPU: the warm start is cheaper than one texture and the cold one cannot be
predicted, so the CPU starts and the GPU joins when ready.
Plan: `plans/libs/README.md` "First-release desktop GPU BC7" ("Measured", "Built ahead").

## 2026-10-19 — export_upgrader — loose mode's block per kind, its pairing line, and the IDs naming nobody
Decision: (1) loose mode infers the boots folders' Red block from the lowest `k` ID and the
gloves folders' from the lowest `g` ID, each kind on its own; (2) each assumed pairing is
reported as `wearer_assumed` (I) on the item folder, its four-digit ID and the slot in the
context (`id=0128, slot=03`); (3) a folder whose ID lands on the block's spare positions
(24-25) or past it is `unmigrated_content` as a whole, the same finding step 3 gives a folder
no rostered player wears.
Why: step 11 said "the lowest boots (or gloves) folder ID", "the report states the assumed
pairings" and "reported" without a code. (1) The two kinds are numbered apart in the old
format, so a shared minimum would let one kind's numbering push the other's folders past their
block; per kind is also how the Pre-Studio upgrader's loose mode computes it. (2) A code of its
own, at Info, so the assumption is visible on every run without making a clean migration not
clean: the author opted into it with `--loose`. (3) One finding for "this folder belongs to no
player" in both modes, so the report and the GUI's unmigrated-content list read the same
whichever mode ran; not paired by the ID modulo 25, because an ID in another block is in
another team's range and its folder may be anyone's (SWE-2 6.7.S1-2: the real GBFG VGL26
export's `g2522`/`g2523` beside `g2301`-`g2320` are reported, for the author or the save to
place).
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 11.

## 2026-10-19 — export_upgrader — model-folder mode's input, names, validation and report line
Decision: (1) `upgrade-models` reads a folder as it is, its top level the model folders: no
archive, no wrapper-folder or same-named-subfolder rule; (2) a top-level folder's kind is its
name's (`Common` in any case; steps 3-4's item grammar for boots and gloves; any other a face
folder), and a model folder holds a file directly in it (OS artifacts aside, `Common` included);
(3) a face folder
without a slot keeps its own name, and in a face folder only `ingame_face` is normalized, the
portrait keeping its name; (4) two folders publishing one name, letter case aside, keep the
first by input name, the later `unmigrated_content` as a whole folder; a root file is
`unmigrated_content`; (5) the validated listing is named `models Midcup` and leaves out
`player_folder_number_invalid`, `player_number_duplicate` and `shared_folder_orphaned`, at
"Verification"'s version; (6) each output folder is reported `model_folder_destination` (I),
`into` = `Players`, `Boots`, `Gloves` or `root`; (7) `-o` is the output folder itself, refused
when it exists.
Why: the plan said what each folder becomes but not how the input is listed, how a kind is told,
what "holds no model files" counts, or how the validation's placement findings and the "where it
goes" line are spelled. (1) Step 1's wrapper rule would read a folder holding one model folder as
that model folder. (2) The item grammar is the one whole-export upgrades already apply, so a
folder is the same kind in both modes; "directly in it" keeps one level, one folder per model,
as the plan wants, and is what tells the converters' `players/<player>/` layout apart. Any file,
not a model file: asking for an `.fmdl` or `.model` refused 5 of the 23 face folders of the real
/jp/ 2024 Winter Cup export, which hold `face_diff.bin` and a portrait only and which `upgrade`
carries (SWE-2 6.8.S1-2). (3) The
plan names the slot rule only; the mode has no `Portraits/`, which step 3's rename serves. (4)
The published folders share one level, so a face and a boots folder can collide where a whole
export's `Players/` and `Boots/` never do; first-wins is step 3's rule for a slot's second face
folder. (5) Those three findings judge where a folder will sit, which only the destination export
knows; kept, every boots or gloves folder would drop (`shared_folder_orphaned` is a `DropFolder`)
and no run holding one could exit 0. (6) A code of its own at Info, so the line shows on every
run without making it not clean. (7) Writing into an existing directory would mix an earlier
run's folders, edited since, with this run's, which is why `upgrade` refuses one too.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` "Model-folder mode" and "CLI".

## 2026-10-19 — export_upgrader — a hair skeleton renamed to pair, `.fpk.xml` left out, an `.ftex` kit texture converted
Decision: in both modes (1) a Fox folder's `fcl_hair_sim.skl` beside an `fcl_hair.fmdl` becomes
`fcl_hair.skl`, unless the folder already holds one; (2) every `*.fpk.xml` is left out of the
output with no finding, as OS artifacts are; (3) a Kit Textures file of the kit grammar's shape
with the extension `.ftex` is converted to its DDS (`ftex::ftex_to_dds`) and migrated as that
`.dds`, one that does not convert being `unmigrated_content` with its error.
Why: the plan was silent on all three, and step 6.9's parity run and census found each on real
exports (`.tmp/6_9/findings.md`). (1) The Studio format pairs a skeleton by its model's stem, so
the upgraded tracer's `fcl_hair_sim.skl` was `file_not_used` at compile and the template
injected in its place; 15 of the 84 such skeletons beside an FMDL on the maintainer's machine are
custom, which the hair would lose. (2) The compiler writes every FPK from the folder's files;
carried, the ~5,400 real ones each made a `file_not_used` Warning at every compile, and Red's
copy in the CPK was read by no game. A finding per file would be the same noise in the upgrade
report. (3) Red's Fox mode packed a member's `.ftex` kit texture as it was, so 13 real exports
(/fgog/'s VGL15-18 ones, INK's VGL26) lost their kits to `unmigrated_content`; the FTEX holds the
DDS data the compiler encodes again, so the conversion loses nothing. A `.dds` and an `.ftex` of
one stem keep the DDS, by the existing first-by-name rule, as Red's Fox mode converted the DDS
over the FTEX.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` steps 1, 3 and 5; EU-IN-04, EU-PLY-13, EU-KIT-15.

## 2026-10-19 — team_compiler — the `.mtl` search reads `oral_X_win32` as `X`
Decision: the pre-Fox `.mtl` search's name match compares a `.mtl`'s stem with the model's stem
read without its `oral_` prefix and `_win32` suffix when it carries both (case-insensitively),
for every caller, `Common/` models included; a stem with one of the two stays literal.
Why: the literal stem, not Red's core name, paired `Common/oral_fbm_u_win32.model` with
`apc.mtl` beside the `fbm.mtl` defining its material in four VG exports (step 6.13a), whose
conversion pre-check then failed and dropped the whole Common folder, which Red packs. Red's
rule closes the 2026-10-17 open issue too (`oral_parts_body_win32.model` getting
`materials.mtl` over `parts_body.mtl`). Red's `face_high_win32` -> `face_neck` reading is not
copied: the game's `face.mtl` name-matches either stem.
Plan: `spec/model_format.md` "Material files", the paragraph "Pre-Fox: the `.mtl` a `.model`
uses".

## 2026-10-19 — pes_model, export_upgrader — the upgrader cleans stray text out of an old `.mtl`
Decision: `MaterialSet::read` keeps refusing non-whitespace text between elements; a second
read, `read_dropping_stray_text`, skips it and says so, and the Export upgrader reads an old
export's `.mtl` with it, writing the set back (the text dropped) and reporting the file.
Why: the Red parity run found a cup export's player (G Autumn 25's `72117 - Lisa/apc.mtl`, a
`\` after a `<sampler/>`) dropped as `mtl_broken`, which Red packs; the census of all 12,755
`.mtl` files on the machine finds three with such text, all typos. Every Studio export is
hand-made or upgraded once, so cleaning in the upgrader fixes the old ones and the compiler
stays strict for a hand-made typo, rather than the compiler tolerating it for good.
Plan: `spec/libs/format_crates.md` "`pes_model::format::mtl`"; `plans/export_upgrader.md`
step 7 and "Message catalog".

## 2026-10-19 — export_upgrader — an upgrade writes a clean export or nothing; a clean one can go straight to the compiler
Decision: the upgrader writes its output only when the migration is clean (no Error, no
finding that drops anything); otherwise nothing is written, exit 1, the report naming what to
fix. A clean run's GUI done line offers Move to exports and compile (the output moved into the
exports folder, the Team compiler made active); the notice keeps Open output folder.
Why: every Studio export is upgraded once, from a clean Red export, so a failure is either an
input to fix first or an upgrader defect to fix; a draft "for manual repair" handed on would be
compiled as if whole and the losses its report named forgotten. With only clean outputs
written, the handoff button has no unclean case to guard against; a notice carries one action,
so the button sits in the done line.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` "Verification", "CLI", "GUI", "Message catalog"; `AGENTS.md`
"Fundamental concepts". The scenarios that assert an output beside exit 1 are rewritten at
worklog step 6.14.

## 2026-10-19 — export_upgrader — a leftover outside the old format is dropped with a Warning, the run clean
Decision: step 10's entries are of two kinds. A leftover, content outside the old format's
layout (a top-level folder the AET does not define, a root file other than the Note, `Other/`'s
files), is dropped with `leftover_dropped` (W) and leaves the run clean; an entry inside the
format's folders that no step migrates stays `unmigrated_content` (E), and nothing is written.
Why: the maintainer's refinement of the clean-or-nothing rule: a leftover the Studio export
does not need (KFG VGL26's `FMDL Boots/` of `.model` copies) should not block a migration that
converts everything that matters, as long as the author is told what was left behind; an
entry inside the format's folders is something the old export compiled, so losing it would
make the compile miss it. The line follows the format's own layout, which a member can check
against the AET page, rather than a list of known junk. A leftover does not decide the
migration's engine either: KFG VGL26's `.model` copies, counted, made the Fox export migrate as
pre-Fox (step 6.13b), whose unmerged boots folders then outran the shared IDs.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 10, "Verification", "CLI", "Message catalog";
`AGENTS.md` "Fundamental concepts".

## 2026-10-19 — team_compiler — a boots or gloves folder one player links takes his own ID
Decision: a shared boots or gloves folder that exactly one roster player links plainly takes
that player's exclusive ID (`block_start + slot - 1`); only folders two or more players link take
the block's 17 shared IDs, in name order as before. A Midcup's folder the installed record names
keeps its recorded ID.
Why: on pre-Fox the upgrader keeps every worn item folder shared (a merged model would sit in
the face folder, where a member's own `face.xml` drops it), so a team with more than 17 custom
boots, such as one ported from Fox when FBMs loaded only as boots models, hit
`boots_id_pool_exhausted` while its 23 exclusive IDs stood unused. A player wears one boots ID
and one gloves ID (a link beside his own model of its kind is already merged into his own
folder), so his exclusive ID is free for a folder only he wears, and with 23 slots at most 11
folders have two wearers: a Full export can no longer run out. We do not lend the unused
exclusive IDs to the shared pool instead, because which ones are unused depends on the whole
roster, and a Midcup, which compiles only some players, could not tell.
Plan: `spec/aesthetics_export/player_folders.md` "Assigns IDs automatically" and "A `Midcup`
export keeps the shared IDs the team already has", edited with the code (worklog 6.15).

## 2026-10-19 — export_upgrader — an upgrade writes into a staging folder, renamed when clean
Decision: `upgrade` and `upgrade-models` write into `<output>.upgrading` beside the output; the
shared validation reads it there; a clean verdict renames it to the output, an unclean one
removes it. An abort leaves it, named in the error, and a run refuses (exit 3) when either
folder exists. The rename and the removal retry for about two seconds on "access denied"
before aborting: on Windows another process (an antivirus scan) can hold a just-written file
for a moment, and the crate's test suite met it in about one run in three.
Why: the clean-or-nothing rule needs the verdict before the output appears, and the
validation reads files from disk, as the compile does; staging and one rename give that
without rebuilding the validation on an in-memory listing, and no reader ever sees a
half-written export under the output's name.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` "CLI".

## 2026-10-19 — export_upgrader — a portrait Red converted or read by its short name migrates
Decision: an old `Portraits/` file named `player_???NN` or `???NN` in a texture format the
compiler converts (`png`, `jpg`, ...) migrates under the `player_NN` stem, as a `.dds` one
does; a name Red misread into one the game never loads stays unmigrated content.
Why: Red converted every portrait to DDS before placing it and read a name not starting
`player_` by its fourth and fifth characters, so BAG VGL18.5's `player_XXX08.jpg` and
`XXX17.jpg` were in game; the upgrader, reading `.dds` names alone, reported them as
unmigrated content (the 2026-10-19 census rerun, worklog 6.14c).
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 7.

## 2026-10-19 — export_upgrader — correction: a portrait not named `player_???NN` never reached the game
Decision: the entry above is half wrong. Red converted a `player_???NN` portrait of another
texture format, so `player_XXX08.jpg` migrates as before; but a name not starting `player_`
(`XXX17.jpg`), or whose two characters before the extension are not a slot 01 to 23, failed
Red's `portraits_check` and was discarded, so it is a leftover (the entry below), not migrated.
Why: the 6.14c reading took Red's `export_move.py` rename for the whole path and missed the
check that runs before it. Red's own output for BAG VGL18.5 (6.12c, 2026-10-19) holds
`78808.dds` and no `78817.dds`; the maintainer asked whether Red really converted those.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 7.

## 2026-10-19 — Studio format — a `Portraits/` file is named `NN`, not `player_NN`
Decision: a portrait in the export's `Portraits/` folder is named by its slot, in the
player folder name's form: `NN` (01 to 23), alone or followed by ` - ` and any text, which
is ignored (`Portraits/08.dds`, `Portraits/17 - Snuffy.png`); the compiler accepts no other
name (`portrait_name_invalid`), and the upgrader writes `NN` alone.
Why: the maintainer's simplification; the folder already says what the file is, and the
`player_` prefix was Red's format, which the upgrader rewrites anyway. The optional name part
(the maintainer, the same day) lets a member paste the player folder's name; taking the
