folder's own form, not any text after `NN`, keeps `081.dds` from reading as slot 08.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 7; the compiler's portrait rows with the code (worklog 6.16).

## 2026-10-19 — export_upgrader — content that never reached a player in game is a leftover
Decision: besides content outside the old layout, a leftover (dropped with `leftover_dropped`,
the run clean) is content inside it that Red never read or the game never loaded: files
directly in `Faces/`, `Boots/` or `Gloves/`; a `Full` export's kit texture no kit row names;
a portrait Red's check refused; a team-color entry's second color; an item folder no save
record names; second and later goalkeeper kits; a Kit Textures file in a subfolder.
Why: the maintainer's answer to QUESTIONS.md "Old content that never reached the game"
("Yes. Those 7z files were only made for sharing the model folders anyway, and would have
been deleted before compiling the exports"): the game never showed them, so an upgrade
without them loses nothing, and refusing it would send members to clean exports that played.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 10, step 2, step 7.

## 2026-10-19 — team_compiler — a `Midcup` kit keeps what it does not resend
Decision: in a `Midcup` export, a kit folder without `config.toml` keeps the slot's installed
config (the template only where nothing is installed), and one holding no texture keeps the
installed textures; a folder holding only `colors.txt` updates the kit's colors alone. The
upgrader migrates a Midcup's texture-only kit update as a kit folder without `config.toml`.
Why: the maintainer's answer to QUESTIONS.md "A Midcup kit that updates its textures only"
("Preferably"), and the 6.12c library run: six Midcups (O 2020 Spring Day 8 Additions, the
Winter 26 Day 0 Midcups of /a/ and /vg/, ...) list kit colors with no textures, Red writes
the colors alone, and ours compiled each to a checkerboard placeholder kit and a template
config, which installed would replace the team's kits.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 2; the compiler's "Bins accumulation" and the
`kit_placeholder`/`kit_config_generated` rows with the code (worklog 6.16).

## 2026-10-19 — Studio format — no second goalkeeper kit slot
Decision: Studio keeps the slots `p1`-`p9` and `g1`; second and later goalkeeper kits are
leftovers when upgraded. A `g2` slot is a new slot in the same naming if a version ever
shows one.
Why: the maintainer's answer: none of the PES versions the cup uses supports goalkeeper kits
past `g1` ("negative but keep the road open for it").
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 2.

## 2026-10-19 — export_upgrader — an empty face folder means no `ingame_face` marker
Decision: an empty old face folder writes nothing of its own; its player folder gets no
`ingame_face` marker, so the compiler writes the blank face, as for any player folder with
no face model.
Why: the maintainer: "Empty face folders are used on players which have an FBM, to remove the
placeholder face, as part of the FPC system." Red packs an empty face package for one; the
upgrader listed face folders from file paths, so an empty one was invisible and its wearer got
`ingame_face`, which would show the default face beside the FBM (6.12c: PMMM VGL26's 18, GIG
VGL26's 10, the 4.2.2 test export `3`'s 2).
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 3.

## 2026-10-19 — export_upgrader — a modelless boots or gloves folder marks its wearer `fpc_on`
Decision: a boots or gloves folder holding no model (nothing, or a `boots.skl` alone) gives
each player wearing it the `fpc_on` marker; its files are leftovers. No empty package is
written.
Why: the maintainer: an empty package is the FPC way to hide a player's boots or hands, but
"an empty folder isn't really needed ... Giving a player a boots/gloves ID for an inexistent
folder will work as fine", which is why members give such players the FPC preset's IDs or
their own unused ones; "the upgrade can indeed mark the player instead of packing an empty
package". Today the upgrade dropped the folder and the player wore stock boots and normal
hands (6.12c: EGG VGL26's `k2176 - EMPTY` and `g2177 - EMPTY`, 9 exports).
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 3.

## 2026-10-19 — team_compiler — a `.mtl` Common path needs the three-character subfolder too
Decision: a `.mtl` sampler path below `model/character/uniform/common/` whose subfolder is not
three characters long (`common/o/env.dds`) is an Error, `mtl_common_path_invalid`, folder
discarded, the rule `xml_common_path_invalid` already applies to a `face.xml`.
Why: the team's Common is written under its three-digit ID, so such a path reaches nothing;
Red's check refuses it in both files ("Files loaded from the Common folder must use a path
with a subfolder whose name is three characters long"), while ours checked only the xml and
packed 8 exports' faces with a texture the game never finds (6.12c D4: /o/ and VG name their
team there). One rule for both files a member can type the path in.
Plan: `plans/team_compiler/messages.md` "XML/MTL content checks".

## 2026-10-19 — export_upgrader — a stray file a folder is refused for is a leftover
Decision: a file in a model folder the Studio format refuses there (a disallowed type,
`face.mtl.backup`; in a boots or gloves folder an FMDL under no name the game loads,
`boots - Copy.fmdl`) is dropped as a leftover with `leftover_dropped`, and the folder migrates.
Why: today the upgrade copies it, and the compile then refuses the whole folder
(`file_type_disallowed`, an Error under the default `strict_file_type_check`) or, for the FMDL,
merges the copy into the wearer's hair (`fmdl_fcl_hair_fallback`): a clean upgrade must end in
a clean Studio export. Red discards the whole folder over such a file; we keep the folder,
the member's content, because the stray copy never belonged to it (6.12c D6: M Winter 18 and
two other exports; D9: the 4.2.3 test export `C-blin`'s `k0326 - IKA-CHAN`).
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 10.

## 2026-10-19 — export_upgrader — a face folder holding the game path migrates its innermost folder
Decision: a face folder holding the game's own path to its face
(`81401/common/character0/model/character/face/real/81401/`) has that innermost folder's
contents moved into the player folder.
Why: Red packs such a folder as it stands, which reproduces the game path, so the face
reached the game; moved as it is, the tree sits below the player folder and the compile
refuses its `face.xml` and drops the player (6.12c D7: FGOG VGL6, FGOG minipatch, /co/'s fetus
export).
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 3.

## 2026-10-19 — export_upgrader — the output's validation runs with the strict file-type check
Decision: the shared validation the upgrader runs on its output has `strict_file_type_check`
on, as the compiler's default has it, so a disallowed file is an Error and nothing is written.
Why: off, a disallowed file was an Info, the output was written, and the compile then refused
the player's folder (6.12c: the nested `face.xml` of the game-path face folders, D7): the
output was not the clean Studio export a clean run promises. Leftovers the upgrader drops
itself (stray backups, D6) never reach the check; any other kind now stops the run by name.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` "Verification"; EU-REP-02 rewritten for it.

## 2026-10-19 — export_upgrader — a Kit Textures file that does not migrate is a leftover
Decision: a file directly in Kit Textures that is not a kit texture of a given slot (`back.dds`,
`u0XXXp2 - Copy.dds`, `u0XXXp1.png`) is a leftover in any export kind; the second of two
landing on one name stays unmigrated content (EU-KIT-18).
Why: none reached the game: Red's `kittextures_check` deletes a name not starting `u` with `p`
or `g` sixth, its `export_move` packs only `.dds` and `.ftex` files, and a copy-named texture
is packed where no kit row names it; the maintainer's answer of 2026-10-19 makes such content
a leftover. (A first reading had `u0XXXp1.png` refused with the whole folder; SWE-2's review
6.16.S1 found `texture_check` passes any non-DDS file.)
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` steps 5 and 10; EU-KIT-08.

## 2026-10-19 — export_upgrader — a modelless item folder names no player
Decision: the name part of a boots or gloves folder holding no model (`k2176 - EMPTY`) is not
a source of its wearer's folder name; the next source in step 3's order is.
Why: the folder's files are leftovers and it migrates to an `fpc_on` marker alone, and its name
describes the folder (`EMPTY`), not the player.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 3; EU-PLY-17.

## 2026-10-19 — Studio format — two `Portraits/` files of one slot conflict
Decision: with `NN` and `NN - <text>` both accepted, two `Portraits/` files of one slot
(`05.dds`, `05 - Bob.png`) are `texture_stem_conflict`, both dropped, the context's `stem`
the slot's `NN`.
Why: grouping by stem alone would let two stems feed one slot, one silently winning; the
existing rule for two files of one stem is the same situation, so it gets the same finding.
Plan: `plans/aesthetics_export/object_model.md` "Validation semantics".

## 2026-10-19 — docs — usability ideas nobody asked for go to `PROPOSALS.md`
Decision: a new working document, `docs/PROPOSALS.md`, holds the usability ideas an agent
thinks of while working (a button, a default, a handoff between tools); the maintainer vetoes
or accepts each, and an unruled one is not built.
Why: the maintainer's ruling: the upgrader's "Move to exports and compile" button, an idea
they had not requested, was rightly asked in `QUESTIONS.md` rather than applied as a
recommendation (it was approved, and needs no new ruling); a file of their own keeps such
ideas from crowding `QUESTIONS.md`, whose entries block work, while still recording each.
Plan: `AGENTS.md` "Working documents" and "When the plan has gaps".

## 2026-10-19 — GUI — usability passes: one before the tools' drafts, one per draft
Decision: after Phase 6 closes and before the first tool's draft page, the lead makes one
usability pass over what Phases 1-6 built for members (export format, message texts, defaults,
the handoffs between tools), and reviews each tool's draft page for usability before refining
it with the maintainer; every idea is a `PROPOSALS.md` entry.
Why: the maintainer asked when such a pass fits. Before the drafts, accepted ideas shape the
pages instead of patching them; on each draft, flow problems show where a spec reading cannot
see them; after implementation, the same idea would cost a view and its GUI scenarios.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Prototypes before implementation"; `plans/core/development_plan.md`
Phase 8's bullets; worklog step 8.4.

## 2026-10-19 — export_upgrader — where "never reached the game" stops being a leftover
Decision: content Red kept out is a leftover when it is a single file under a name Red's
per-file name checks refused (a portrait, a kit texture), a copy or backup, or content outside
the layout;
it stays `unmigrated_content` when the old export holds two candidates for one place (a second
face folder of a slot, a second item folder of an ID, two kit textures landing on one name,
two portraits in one face folder, two old `Portraits/` files of one slot), or a whole model
folder under a name Red refused (a face folder without a valid slot, `K0430`).
Why: SWE-2's review 6.16.S1 found the maintainer's rule, read literally, also covers those
cases, and the line between them was written nowhere. For two candidates only the author
knows the meant one, and Red's pick was a refusal or arbitrary; a misnamed folder is a
player's whole face lost over a typo, which a Warning would let pass unnoticed. A team
color's second color is no such choice: Red always kept the first.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 10.

## 2026-10-19 — export_upgrader — an old portrait's name is read as Red's check read it
Decision: an old `Portraits/` file migrates only when Red's `portraits_check` passed it:
`player_` in that letter case, the two characters before a three-letter extension a slot
01-23 (`file_name[-6:-4]`); `Player_XXX05.dds` and `player_XXX05.jpeg` are leftovers.
Why: what migrates should be what the game showed; Red deleted those names (SWE-2 review
6.16.S1), while the upgrader's earlier reading was case-blind and took any texture extension.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 7; EU-MDL-19.

Decision: after Phase 6 closes, the work runs 20.0d (the DBC ruleset's coverage), 8.4 (the

Decision: DBC participants get the Save editor and the Ruleset editor as a preview build,
0.0.1, cut once the Ruleset editor's phase closes: the Team compiler and the Export upgrader,

## 2026-10-19 — export_upgrader — a player marked `fpc_on` keeps his other category's 0 explicit
Decision: when the upgrader marks a player `fpc_on` for a modelless boots or gloves folder, the
category no folder of his decides keeps a stored 0 as an explicit `boots_id = 0` or
`gloves_id = 0`, in a Full output too.
Why: Astra's review 6.16.A1 found that under the marker an unset key resolves to the hide
preset's blank-model ID, so a player with hidden boots and normal hands (EGG VGL26's EMPTY
boots and gloves folders have different wearers) would lose his hands; an explicit 0 is what
he wore in game.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 8 (the stored-0 sentence), EU-PLY-17.

## 2026-10-19 — team_compiler — a Midcup kit's config names the number textures the game already holds
Decision: a `Midcup` kit's emitted config names a `back`, `chest`, `leg` or `name` texture when the kit
holds it or the installed CPKs before the run's hold that texture of the slot; a `Full` kit's
names still come from its effective set alone.
Why: Astra's review 6.16.BC found the config's five name fields derived from the export alone,
so a `Midcup` resending a config and its main texture zeroed the number font its `Full` export
had installed (JP 2024 Spring Aesthetic Additions for Day 8 resends configs naming
`u0174p1_back`, `_leg`, `_name` with only `u0XXXp1.dds`); Red copied the config as it was, and
the game found the textures installed. The installed entry paths are already read for the
Common texture lookup.
Plan: `spec/team_compiler/pipeline.md` "Bins accumulation"; `spec/aesthetics_export/player_folders.md`
(the texture-name fields); TC-KIT-35.

## 2026-10-20 — model_conversion — a hand split takes stray hand weights as they are
Decision: the hand split keeps selecting every vertex with any positive `skh_` weight, a
residue of 1/255 included; no threshold or special case for a hand part of a few vertices.
Stray hand weights are the model's to fix, and the `model_hand_split` Info already names the
model and the gloves it gave.
Why: 6.16c measured HDG VGL26's `EAT` (`.tmp/6_16/ingame/`): seven loop entries of two
chest-armor vertices carry `sk_chest` 253-254 and 1/255 on `skh_pinky_mcp_l`/`_pip_l`; the
split moves them with their grow ring (20 vertices, 10 `armor` faces) into a `glove_l` that
floats as a speck in game. A threshold would be a second rule for what "weighted to a hand"
means, against the select-grow-separate semantics members reproduce in Blender; the
maintainer ruled it a model issue.
Plan: no plan edit needed: `spec/model_conversion/hand_split.md` "Split" step 1 already says
"any positive weight".

## 2026-10-20 — export_upgrader — a texture the old compile's ID rename replaced is a leftover
Decision: inputs of one folder whose paths differ only in their kit tokens' three characters
(`u0XXXp2.dds` beside `u0731p2.dds` in a /jp/ export) keep the one the old compile's rename
wrote last, the last renamed one in Windows's case-folded name order (an input already spelled
with the team's ID being replaced by any renamed one), and the others are `leftover_dropped`;
every other output-path collision stays `unmigrated_content`, and so does every collision in
model-folder mode, which has no team ID.
Why: the 6.16 census rerun found four real inputs refused for this alone: the JP Genso Cup
exports' `Boots/k0860` (an older `u0731p2.dds` beside the newer `u0XXXp2.dds`) and GBPEN
VGL26's `Gloves/g2336` (identical copies spelled `u0799`, another team's ID, and `u0XXX`).
Red's `filenames_id_replace` renames every token to the team's ID in listing order, deleting
the file under the new name first, so its pick is deterministic and the losers never reached
the game: the maintainer's leftover rule (2026-10-19), not a choice only the author can make.
The plan had listed the pair as unmigrated content, and the upgrade kept the first input,
which for JP was the older texture.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 7 (the collision sentence), step 10's leftover list,
EU-MDL-21.

## 2026-10-20 — team_compiler — the library parity is a measurement rerun at phase closes
Decision: the parity over the maintainer's library of old exports is rerun at each phase close
that changes the Team compiler or the Export upgrader (upgrade census, compile, Red from a fresh
copy, `red_parity`, every line attributed), its scripts committed under
`scripts/library_parity/`; no hash manifest of Red's output is committed as a fixture. The three
tracers stay the committed parity tests.
Why: 6.12b-c's measurements: the inputs are several hundred members' exports on the maintainer's
machine alone, so a manifest-backed test could never run in CI; ours differs from Red's by design
in 28 classes (I1-I28), so a manifest of either tree would be a golden every intentional change
rewrites; and the run's value is the attribution of each new class, which needs judgement. It
costs about 20 minutes of Red (median 3.6 s per export) and 17 of ours over 250 exports.
Plan: `plans/team_compiler/testing.md` "Testing: parity against Red" (the manifest paragraph
replaced); worklog 6.12.

## 2026-10-20 — export_upgrader — correction: Red does not deliver a game-path face folder
Decision: unchanged (2026-10-19 "a face folder holding the game path migrates its innermost
folder"); its reason is corrected. Red's face CPK for such a folder nests the member's tree
below the player's own path (FGOG VGL6: `face/real/79501.cpk` holding
`.../real/79501/common/character0/model/character/face/real/81401/face.mtl` and the rest), and
the `face.xml` Red generates at the player's path, finding none at the folder's top, lists the
models as `./face_high_*.model` and the like, which are not beside it; the member's own
`face.xml` (`arm`, `handL` types in /co/'s fetus export, the member's 944-byte diff) stays
nested. So under Red the face did not load (a CPK listing, not checked in game).
Why: the 6.16 library run classified the two exports' `face.xml` differences against Red's
generated one (every model `parts`, the template 960-byte diff). The rule stays because the
folder is the member's face for the slot, an extracted face CPK of their own (2016-2018
exports), and migrating it gives the face the export was made to show, where
reproducing Red's output would ship a face that does not load. The parity difference is an
intentional class (I30).
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 3 (the game-path sentence).

## 2026-10-20 — team_compiler — a `Midcup` kit without colors keeps its installed menu colors
Decision: in a `Midcup` export, a kit without a usable `colors.txt` emits no `UniColor.bin`
entry, its installed entry standing, whether or not it resends its main texture; a `Full`
export's still derives the pair from the main texture (`kit_colors_derived`).
Why: the 2026-10-19 rule ("a `Midcup` kit keeps what it does not resend") left derivation as it
was, so a texture-only update replaced the installed menu colors with ones derived from the
new texture, where Red keeps them unless the Note lists colors: the 6.16 library run's
`UniColor.bin` records for JP 2024 Spring Aesthetic Additions for Day 5 (team 731, six kits) and
VG Aesthetics Day 0 Midcup differed for that alone (Red's base entry, ours derived). The colors
are what such a folder does not resend.
Plan: `spec/team_compiler/pipeline.md` step 2 (the **Kits** item), `messages.md`
`kit_colors_derived`, TC-KIT-36.

## 2026-10-20 — model_conversion — a face made for the other engine is transformed, not passed through
Decision: a face folder marks the engine its face was made for (`fox`/`pre-fox`, as the kit
layout marker; none means the target), and a face with face weighting compiled for the other
engine gets the transformation the Sopdog pair shows applied to its model and diff; if no rule
reproduces it, the compiler reports the face instead. Lower priority than the Divegrass Before
Christmas work.
Why: the maintainer's answer to QUESTIONS.md "Face diffs are engine-specific" (2026-10-20):
"Apply the same transformation that was done to sopdog's model to any model with face weighting
which has to change format (as indicated by a fox/pre-fox marker like the one used on kits).
This might not be possible but we should attempt it." Options (a) silence, (b) a report on
every pre-Fox face once the cup moves to Fox, and (c) dropping the diff were the alternatives.
Plan: `plans/model_conversion/conversion.md` "A face made for the other engine"; worklog Issues.

## 2026-10-20 — export_upgrader — a Common path spelled with the team's name is the team's Common
Decision: in an old face's `.mtl` and `face.xml`, a Common path whose segment is the team's
name without its slashes (`model/character/uniform/common/o/env.dds` for /o/, `.../common/vg/`
for VG, letter case aside) is read as the team's Common, as `XXX` and a baked-in ID are, and
migrated the same way (the bare name and its `.common` link, or the kept Common path).
Why: the maintainer's answer to QUESTIONS.md "A Common path spelled with the team's name"
(2026-10-20): the question's premise, that no compiler ever resolved that spelling, was wrong:
the first, batch-file compiler (`4cc aet compiler/_old/4cc-aet-compiler`, readme "the contents
of the Common folder will be moved to model/character/uniform/common/---/ (where --- is the team
name)") wrote a pre-Fox export's Common there, so those faces loaded their Common files then;
"if we can easily do (a) let's go with that instead, so we can support even older exports".
Options (b) a leftover and (c) a refusal remain the fallback if (a) proves hard.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 7 (the Common reference sentence); worklog 6.16d.

## 2026-10-20 — export_upgrader — a pre-Fox Common segment of any name is the team's Common
Decision: the rule above widens to any folder name after `model/character/uniform/common/` in
a pre-Fox `.mtl` or `face.xml` (another team's name included), and a segment of another length
than three that stays a game path is written as the team's ID (`XXX` in model-folder mode). The
Fox common directory keeps its three-character rule.
Why: the library run at 6.16 found 15 exports the compile refused over such a segment: 14 are
/o/ and VG faces naming their own team, the 15th is ASP's 4CCC export, whose `Players/08 - asp`
carries a referee kit's `refkit.mtl` naming `common/refs/refkit/`. The upgrade ended clean on
all 15 and the compile failed, against the rule that an upgrade ends in a clean Studio export.
A Studio export names no Common but its own, and the compiler already reads every
three-character segment as the team's, so the narrower rule bought nothing and left ASP's
export to fail; one rule is also less code than comparing against the team's name. Options:
the team's name alone (the answer as given, ASP refused), or ASP's reference a refusal.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` step 7 (the Common reference sentence); worklog 6.16d.

## 2026-10-20 — aatf — DBC7's rules become three schema fields, none a custom check
Decision: the ruleset schema gains `medal_systems` (alternative tier counts), `HeightSystem::
by_quotas` (a system that holds only when the team meets its quotas) and `HeightSystem::
extra_height` (a team-wide pool of centimetres, filled tallest first), with the violation kinds
`MedalSystem` and `ExtraHeight`; DBC7's data block uses all three and no custom check.
Why: the maintainer asked for UI-class support of every DBC rule but niche, complex ones. The
medal systems tie tier counts together, which per-tier counts cannot say; the systems are told
apart by their counts, which no one-player condition can say (a giga team may hold a 195 cm
player); and the pool as a custom check would run after the built-in height checks had already
failed every giga team standing between bracket heights, while the Manlet bonus needs the system
the pool decides. Tallest first draws no more of the pool than any order that fills the quotas,
so it agrees with the organizer's roster-order count on every verdict.
Plan: `plans/aatf_rules.md` "The ruleset schema", "DBC7", "Coverage of the DBC7 rules";
`plans/ruleset_editor.md` "The editor" (Tiers, Heights); worklog 20.0d.

## 2026-10-20 — aatf — DBC7 follows its wiki page where the organizer's editor is stricter
Decision: `dbc7.rhai` checks what the page's "Tactical export Rules" state and nothing else: any
stat above its tier's target is a violation, where DBC7-Editor only warns up to 7 above (5 for a
silver or a Manlet regular); the editor's errors for what the page leaves free (registered
position not A, age, weight, captain, a registered goalkeeper, a 189 cm goalkeeper's second A)
are not in the data block.
Why: the maintainer ruled the page the source of truth and the fork a reference, and the page
says "No tactical export rules for anything else … go crazy". Whether the organizer enforces the
editor's extra errors is cup practice, asked in `QUESTIONS.md`; an answer turns the matching
`universal` flags and one special on, without a schema change.
Plan: `plans/aatf_rules.md` "DBC7" (the differences list).

## 2026-10-20 — aatf — a tier is recognized by its expected rating before its choices
Decision: the interpreter compares a player's rating with each tier's expected rating as the
specials leave it before any `choice` is resolved, and DBC7's Manlet bonus is a one-option
choice.
Why: the page allows the bonus ("silvers can also be buffed"), so a Manlet silver may sit
anywhere from 88 to 93. Read after the choices, a silver at 92 uses the option (a stat over 88),
which lifts his expected rating to 93, past his rating, and he falls to regular: the DBC7 parity
run found three such players on real teams the organizer's editor reads as silvers. An option
only raises targets, so the tier reached without it is the player's; VGL25's optional manlet
bonus had the same gap, unseen for want of a cup save. Every existing fixture passes unchanged.
Plan: `plans/aatf_rules.md` "The ruleset schema" ("Recognition before choices").

## 2026-10-20 — save_editor — Output rosters to TSV keeps 4ccEditor's layout
Decision: the TSV holds, per team, the team's name on its own line, then one tab-separated row
per player (number, name, registered position, rating, captain mark, height, playing style,
skills), then a blank line: 4ccEditor's `roster_data_output`. SE-GUI-27 is reworded to match.
Why: the action is kept for parity ("Feature inventory": "Kept"), and members paste the file
into sheets built around that layout; the scenario's "his team among its columns" described a
different file, written from memory of the plan rather than from the original.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Acceptance" SE-GUI-27.

## 2026-10-20 — save_editor — The comparator panel draws rows in the tabs' terms
Decision: a comparator row shows the field under its tab's label and its value as that tab
shows it (a free-kick motion 15, stored as 14); a field no tab shows keeps the report's name and
value. Export writes the CLI's `diff` report unchanged, stored values included.
Why: `diff` reports stored values (`PlayerDiff::Field`, the compare scripts' output), measured
on team 739 of the maintainer's PES 21 save: hunching dribbling 2 in the report, 3 in the Team
TOML and the Appearance tab. A row jumps to its player's tab, where a value one lower reads as a
wrong row. The plan was silent on the panel's representation.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Comparator (gameplay + aesthetics)".

## 2026-10-20 — save_editor — The import dialog's sections split the file as 4ccEditor's squad load
Decision: names, shirt names and shirt numbers import with the aesthetics section, as 4ccEditor's
squad load has them (`PlayerImport` copies them under `importAes`; the numbers table is read
under the same flag); the Team TOML's `[team]` keys, which no squad file carried, import with
gameplay.
Why: the plan asks for the squad load's section choices, and a member who unticks aesthetics
expects what 4ccEditor did; the comparator's scopes classify differences, not import choices.
The `[team]` keys are the team's identity and settings, closer to gameplay than to the look.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Interchange formats in the UI".

## 2026-10-20 — studio_core — Planned tools are data; a tool's icon is a trait method
Decision: `studio` keeps the full registry as a list of `PlannedTool { id, label, icon }` in the
registry's order and hands it to the shell with the registered tools; the sidebar lists, after
the registered tools, every planned entry whose id no registered tool has, grayed. `StudioTool`
gains `fn icon(&self) -> &'static str`, an `egui-phosphor` glyph, for the collapsed rail.
Why: ST-SIDE-07 lists the planned tools, and a planned tool has no crate to construct, so the
list is data; the icon rail (ST-SIDE-02) needs a glyph per entry and the plan named none. The
0.0.1 preview uses the same list: a build registering the two editors shows the Team compiler
and the Export upgrader grayed, as the maintainer asked.
Plan: `plans/core/architecture.md` "Tool plugin interface".

## 2026-10-20 — studio_core — The CLI probes for `data_dir_read_only`; CLI notices go to stderr
Decision: the CLI raises `data_dir_read_only` at startup from a probe (the settings file opened
for writing, nothing written) and prints it as stderr's first line; the GUI raises it from a
failed save and drops it at the next successful one, with no probe. Notices a tool publishes
during a CLI command print on stderr as they occur.
Why: the CLI never writes settings, so no save of its own can fail and ST-CLI-01 needs another
source; a probe that writes nothing leaves the file's time and contents alone. The GUI's first
tool switch saves anyway, so a probe there adds a second rule for the same condition. Stderr,
not stdout, because stdout carries the findings a script reads.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Status bar", the "CLI equivalence" bullet.

## 2026-10-20 — studio_core — No `pes_install_missing` condition; a settings save edits the file in place
Decision: `ShellCondition::PesInstallMissing` goes: a PES folder that is missing, or holds no
exe or another version's, is the version selector's coloring alone. `Settings::save` edits the
existing file through `toml_edit`, writing only the values that changed, instead of
regenerating it.
Why: the condition and the selector's yellow reported one fact twice, and the selector is in
every tool's sidebar, so a status-bar line adds nothing but a second place to keep in step (the
side-lead's 8.2 note flagged it; the review A1 found the condition raised nowhere). The save:
since 8.6a every tool switch saves `last_tool`, and a regenerated file drops the comments and
order a member wrote by hand, which they do until the settings menu exists (AGENTS.md "User-facing
TOML is edited, never regenerated").
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Settings menu" (the best-effort bullet); `spec/core/gui.md` "Status bar".

## 2026-10-20 — studio_core — `settings_view` takes the context; a tool without settings has no section
Decision: `StudioTool::settings_view` becomes `settings_view(&mut self, ui, ctx: &ToolContext)`
with a default that draws nothing, and the settings menu draws a section only for a tool whose
`default_settings()` table is not empty. The theme applies through `Context::set_theme` from the
setting alone, and the preset is egui's dark `Visuals` until it is curated.
Why: a section has to write the tool's table, and `set_tool_settings` is on the context, which
the old signature did not pass. The draft draws no header for the Export upgrader, which has no
settings, and the default table already lists every key a tool reads, so no second flag is
needed. egui follows the system's theme unless told otherwise, which would override the dark
default on a light desktop; the drafts are drawn in egui's dark colors, so curating the preset
is a design pass over the drafts first, not a step of the shell's build.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Settings menu", "Other UI components"; `spec/core/architecture.md`
"Tool plugin interface" when the step lands.

## 2026-10-20 — studio_core — The first-run dialog keeps itself open on a failed write; no `.bak` rename; `hold_close`
Decision: a first-run choice whose settings file cannot be written keeps the dialog open with the
error, so the member picks the other location. EGG's rename of a shadowing portable file to
`.bak` is not built. The close hook is `StudioTool::hold_close(&mut self) -> bool`, asked in
sidebar order until one tool holds the close, and a tool's prompt answers through
`ToolContext::request_close`.
Why: a choice that never reached the disk is asked again at every start, and the session's
settings vanish with it; an unpacked program folder under `Program Files` is the likely case.
The rename covers a portable file present when the member picks the config dir, which cannot
happen: the dialog shows only when neither file exists, and no later move of the data
location exists. Asking the tools one at a time keeps one prompt on screen, the one whose view
the shell switches to.
Plan: `plans/core/distribution.md` "Data location: asked on first run"; `plans/core/gui.md`
"Cancellation".

## 2026-10-20 — help — The Messages topic's text sits in `messages.rs`'s catalog rows; `help`'s output shape
Decision: each tool's catalog row in `messages.rs` gains two member-facing cells, *When* and
*Effect*, first copied from the spec's catalog table, which stays the design record; the
Export upgrader lists the structure pass's codes it reports with its own severity and the
Team compiler's text, or its own table's where that table describes the code. `4cc-studio help` alone lists the chapters, `help <id> messages` prints
the Messages topic, `--export` writes `<id>.md` per chapter, and the core chapters' ids
(`setting-up`, `first-run`) share the tools' namespace, `help` reserved. The core chapters
"Updates" and "What's new" wait for the update check and `CHANGELOG.md` (Release 0.1.0).
Why: the plan generates the topic from `messages.rs` but its rows held a code and a severity
only. A Markdown table in `help/` would be easier prose to edit but a second list of codes,
which the existing catalog tests do not see; the row beside the code cannot miss one. Copying
the spec's cells gives members a complete topic now, and the wording pass the draft's review
asked for edits them for members (the dispositions and docs pointers they carry) without
losing the maintainer's record. A chapter about a feature not built would describe nothing.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Help window" (the Messages and CLI bullets).

## 2026-10-21 — studio_core — The help window's geometry holds for the session only
Decision: the help window's position and size are egui's own, kept by the window's id while the
program runs, and are not written to the settings file; opening the window closes the settings
menu or the About popup.
Why: remembering them across restarts needs a common-settings field the shell rewrites at the
end of every drag or resize, a settings save per move for a window members open now and then,
and `CommonSettings` has no such field (the draft's review found the gap). A modal left open
would cover the non-modal window it just opened.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Help window" ("Window").

## 2026-10-21 — studio_core — `egui_commonmark` `=0.25.0`, without its image loaders
Decision: the help window renders Markdown with `egui_commonmark` 0.25.0, pinned exactly like
`egui`, with its default features off and `pulldown_cmark` on.
Why: 0.25.0 is the last release built on egui 0.36 (0.26.0 requires 0.37, which the workspace's
exact pin rules out until egui moves). The default `load-images` feature brings `egui_extras`'
image and file loaders, and the help's topics hold no images. The crate was chosen over a
hand-rolled renderer on 2026-09-12; its link hooks are what an in-doc link's click reads.
Plan: `plans/core/README.md` "External Dependencies (Rust crates)".

## 2026-10-21 — save_editor — Live AATF: the open team re-checked after every edit, in a panel docked at the bottom
Decision (maintainer's request): a "Live AATF" toolbar toggle, remembered in the Save editor's
settings, docks a panel at the bottom of the view listing the open team's violations, re-checked
on a worker after every settled edit (undo and redo included) and on a team switch, so the list
empties as the member fixes the team; `No issues: <team> passes <ruleset>` once it is empty. The
floating AATF panel stays for several teams, suggestions and the rules file's tools.
Why: the planned panel was a one-shot check a member had to rerun after each fix. The bottom
over a side because the player list holds the left and the tabs need their width, and the
Team compiler's log already sits there, so the log panel widget's frame serves both. On a worker
because one team's check takes about 50 ms in a release build (measured on a PES 2017 save),
more than a frame, which a stat drag would pay at every frame.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Configurable AATF rules" ("Live AATF"), SE-GUI-30.

## 2026-10-21 — dds_convert — BC7 speed is judged on a cold full-cup compile; BC3 when no BC7 encoder is fast enough
Decision (maintainer): a full-cup compile runs once per set of exports, so its PNG textures are
always encoded cold and no conversion cache shortens it; the encoder's speed is the measure. The
16 s per 4096² chain of the current CPU BC7 encoder is unacceptable: unless a faster CPU encoder
or preset keeps quality above BC3's, a PES 19-21 compile without a GPU writes BC3. The GPU's own
time (0.48 s per chain at `basic`, about 15 s for a team of PNG textures) is to be cut through the
preset, several textures in flight and flat blocks kept out of the search, measured after DBC's
work (worklog 16.x c); our own encoder only if those fall short.
Why: Studio exports are PNG by design (lossless edits, smaller files with flat colors), so nearly
every Fox texture is encoded, a team's being about 30 chains; speed is the suite's first goal.
Plan: `plans/libs/README.md` "First-release desktop GPU BC7" ("The workload the speed is judged on").

## 2026-10-21 — aatf — DBC7 follows the organizer's choice on each of the seven page/editor differences
Decision (the DBC7 organizer, relayed by the maintainer): the stat band is the editor's (a
regular's stat up to 7 above its target, a silver's or a Manlet regular's up to 5, a warning;
past it an error), plus an error when a regular's or a silver's stats added up exceed their
targets' sum; the registered position not rated A is a warning; a 189 cm goalkeeper with a
second A position is an error; age, weight, captain and a registered goalkeeper stay free, as
the page leaves them; and no skill-card cap, the game not holding a player to ten in play.
The schema gains `Tier::stat_warning`, `Tier::total_within_targets` and an effect's
`stat_warning`; the two position rules are specials. The total is read against the player's own
targets over every ability stat until the organizer says otherwise (QUESTIONS.md "DBC7: the stat
total").
Why: the organizer runs the cup and checks its exports; a band in the schema, not one per stat,
because DBC7's band differs by tier and by the Manlet bonus. A flat all-77 total would make the
Manlet bonus unusable beyond trading points, which the page grants.
Plan: `plans/aatf_rules.md` "The ruleset schema" (the band, the total), "DBC7", "Coverage of the
DBC7 rules".

## 2026-10-21 — color_tools — The picker popup's layout, its session-only recent colors, and no suggestions in the Save editor
Decision: the color picker opens from a color button as a popup holding egui's opaque
saturation-value square and hue slider, a hex field (`#RRGGBB`, `#` optional, either case,
committed on Enter or focus loss, an unreadable text put back), R/G/B fields, the host's
suggestion swatches and the recent colors. Recent colors are shared by every picker for the
session, newest first, at most eight, a color joining when the popup closes on a color other
than its opening one; the Save editor passes no suggestions. The widget edits a `[u8; 3]` and
returns whether it changed and the hover candidate; a drag is a candidate until released,
then one change.
Why: the plan named the parts but not when a color counts as recent, nor where recents live.
Joining on close, not on every change, keeps a drag across the square from filling the list
with its path; session-only, not saved, because saving rewrites the settings file per pick, as
the help window's geometry decision weighed. The Save editor has no extraction result to
suggest, and an invented suggestion (the team's other color) offers what is already on screen.
One change per gesture, because the Save editor pushes an undo entry per change and a drag
reported frame by frame would take a hundred undos to revert.
Plan: `plans/libs/color_tools.md` "Color-picker widget (Phase 8)".

## 2026-10-21 — aatf — `card_limits` returns the paid cards the player holds
Decision: the logic's `card_limits` map, and `aatf::CardLimits`, gain `paid`, the player's cards
no free group or free card covers, beside `limit`; a card picker's badge is `limit - paid`. The
logic's version-1 hash is replaced rather than a version 2 added, since no ruleset file has been
released with the old one.
Why: the spec named `card_limits` as behind the badges, but the map held the limit without the
count it is compared with; a widget counting paid cards itself would be a second card economy,
drifting from the checks the first time a free-card rule changes.
Plan: `spec/aatf_rules.md` "The interpreter" (the `card_limits` bullet).

## 2026-10-21 — team_widgets — The violations list words the violations itself, in check order, errors first per group
Decision: `team_widgets::violations` draws each violation as its rule's name and a sentence of
its own, one per `ViolationKind`, for both the Save editor and the Team creator; the name and
fields as a rules file spells them move from the Save editor's `messages.rs` to `aatf` as
`ViolationKind::rule`, which the CLI and the widget share. The groups keep `check_team`'s order
(the players by slot, then the team's rows), each group's errors before its warnings, and
suggestions only on the host's request, after the violations.
Why: the plan named the list but not where its words live. A sentence table in each host would
word one violation two ways the first time one host's table changed; the lib is the one place
both draw from. The rules-file spelling is `aatf`'s knowledge, not a tool's message. Errors first
within a group, not a list sorted by severity, because a member fixes one player at a time and
the slot order is the player list's.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "`libs/team_widgets`" (the `violations` bullet).

## 2026-10-21 — team_widgets — The playing-style combo lists the version's stored order
Decision: `playing_style_picker` lists a version's playing styles in the order the save stores
them, not in the canonical order of `PlayStyle::ALL` that the draft's combo uses.
Why: the stored order is the game's own Edit-mode list (PES 15-18 permute it against the
canonical one), and a member checking a style compares the two lists; the canonical order is
the Team TOML's naming, which nobody reads as a list.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "`libs/team_widgets`" (the `cards` bullet).

## 2026-10-21 — color_tools — The picker's HSV is over sRGB, and a host's rounding of a pick is still the pick
Decision: the picker's square and slider work in HSV over sRGB values (not `ecolor::Hsva`,
which is linear, nor `HsvaGamma`, which re-encodes the value alone), keeping the working hue
across gestures on colors with no hue; a change of the color the frame after the widget's own
commit is that commit's feedback (the Save editor's 6-bit rounding), so the pick joins the
recents; any other host change under the open popup is not a pick; every close but Escape
commits a parseable typed hex or R/G/B value.
Why: Astra's review A1 found the linear `Hsva` gradients showing other colors than the ones a
click picks, a hue lost on white, and every Save editor pick kept out of the recents by the
undo rule, since the host always rounds it.
Plan: `plans/libs/color_tools.md` "Color-picker widget (Phase 8)".

## 2026-10-21 — save_editor — Undo holds whole entries, one per gesture; unsaved means unlike the file
Decision: an undo entry is the before and after of each `PlayerEntry` or `TeamEntry` it changed;
changes from one widget merge into the open entry while a pointer button is held or a widget
has keyboard focus; a player's unsaved-changes dot compares his entry and his roster number
with the file as opened or last saved.
Why: per-field changes need every widget to say which field it changed, while
`team_widgets`' contract reports only that something did; an entry per frame would make a
drag dozens of undo steps; a dot tied to the undo stack would stay after undoing back to the
saved state.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Editing UI", the Undo/redo and Unsaved changes bullets.

## 2026-10-21 — save_editor — A name's color code draws its RGB, and a non-hex code draws nothing
Decision: the player list draws a `\x11c` code's first six bytes as the RGB of the text after
it, ignores the alpha, and leaves the text the normal color when those six are not hex.
Why: the game does not check the bytes are hex (nine PES 21 names carry `\x11ca000c8ON`, an
alpha of `ON`), and what it shows for a non-hex RGB is not measured; the normal color draws
nothing invented.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Editing UI", the Player list bullet.

## 2026-10-21 — save_editor — The Abilities tab shows the game's numbers and never edits a player by drawing him
Decision: the tab's controls use 4ccEditor's ranges at the game's numbers (abilities 40 to 99,
form 1 to 8, injury resistance 1 to 3, weak foot 1 to 4, these four stored one lower; star 0
to 7; playing attitude 0 to 3), and a stored value outside its range is drawn as stored, not
clamped; the Cards left badges use the ruleset `check-aatf` runs.
Why: field-level parity with 4ccEditor is the plan's verification, so a member reads the same
number in both; egui's number control clamps the value it draws by default, which would mark
every out-of-range player unsaved the moment he is selected; one ruleset for the badges and
the check, not one each, or the badges and the check could disagree on the same player.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Editing UI", the Abilities & Skills bullet.

## 2026-10-21 — save_editor — The unsaved-changes prompt lists each changed field, old and new
Decision: the save/discard/cancel prompt shows a table (Item, Old value, New value), one row
per field that differs from the file as opened or last saved, players first, then the teams'
own fields, worded in the tabs' terms as the Comparator panel's rows are; it is computed when
the prompt opens, players through `compare_players` and teams through a team twin of it.
Why: the maintainer asked for it (2026-10-21): a member deciding to discard should see what
goes. Against the baseline, not the undo history, because the history lists edits that undo
or redo cancelled out, which would not be saved or lost; per field, not per player, because
"Snuffy changed" does not say what a discard loses; one wording rule with the Comparator, not
a second one, so a field reads the same in both.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Editing UI", the prompt bullet, and SE-GUI-05.

## 2026-10-21 — gui — Studio opens at half the monitor, and the drafts draw at that size
Decision: the window opens at about half the monitor's width and height, centered; every
draft draws its UI inside a simulated window of that size (from the browser's `screen`),
with a 50/60/75/100% choice and the draft controls outside it.
Why: the maintainer asked for both (2026-10-21): a full-page draft in a maximized browser
shows room the real window will not have, so a layout that fits there can be cramped in the
app, and checking it meant restoring the browser by hand. The size comes from `screen`, not
from fixed pixels, so the draft tracks the monitor it is opened on as the app will.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Shell layout" (The window's size) and "Prototypes before
implementation" (the Size bullet).

## 2026-10-21 — gui — Studio Web draws Studio as a window on the page
Decision: Studio Web draws the desktop shell inside one movable, resizable `egui::Window` at
the desktop window's default size, centered over a plain backdrop, with a maximize button
that pins it to the page; the floating windows stay the context's and float over the page.
Why: the maintainer's idea (2026-10-21): a browser is usually maximized, and views laid out
for a half-monitor window turn sparse across a whole page. One window, not one per tool (the
window-manager idea, ruled not useful for the desktop on 2026-10-20 because the system's
window manager does that job there): the page then shows exactly the desktop's shell, so a
view is laid out once for both.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Browser deployment: Studio Web", the first difference bullet.

## 2026-10-21 — gui — The help window stays inside Studio and opens at 90% of it
Decision: the help stays an in-app window, first opened at 90% of Studio's window and
centered, not a fixed 720 x 480 and not a second OS window.
Why: the maintainer weighed a separate OS window and chose this, after a check of egui's
multi-viewport state at 0.37 (2026-10-21): about 130 open issues mention viewports, child
windows still misbehave per platform, and the headless tests draw only the embedded
fallback. A fixed size is cut off by a small window (a 1080p monitor at 125% scaling gives a
768 x 432 one), and a share of the window fits any size it has.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Help window", the Window bullet.

## 2026-10-21 — pes_savefile, save_editor — Names warn past what every version holds, and apply crops
Decision: the Save editor holds a shirt name to 18 letters on every version (PES 16's field
holds 16) and lets a name use the open save's whole field (61 bytes on PES 20/21), drawing a
name past 46 bytes or an existing shirt name past 18 letters with an amber tint and a hover
that shows the text as the older versions cut it; Team TOML's export notes such texts, and
`apply` crops a name or shirt name to a shorter field (on whole characters and colour codes)
with a note, never refusing. The maintainer asked for a pale yellow field; the tint is of the
theme's warning colour instead, because the theme is dark and its text light.
Why: the maintainer's aim is one tactical export that applies to a save of any version, while
some members want a long name on PES 20/21 that the older versions cut (2026-10-21 census: 12
of 4,830 names in one PES 21 save past 46 bytes, the longest 59, the same names cut at 45 in a
PES 17 save). A warning tells the member where the cut falls; a refusal would block a name the
versions that show it can hold, and editing saves is to stay frictionless. PES 16 is the outlier
the maintainer chose to crop rather than hold every shirt name to 16.
Plan: `plans/pes_savefile/operations.md` "Team TOML" (Portable text limits);
`plans/save_editor.md` "Editing UI", the info strip bullet.

## 2026-10-21 — aesthetics_export, pes_savefile — A Complete export carries its tactical file at the root
Decision: an aesthetics team export may hold `tactics.toml` at its root, a Team TOML from the
Save editor's export, making it a Complete export compiled for any version. The aesthetics half
owns the looks and the tactical file carries none (an appearance table or a kit or colour key
in it is an export-check error); the tactical file owns names, gameplay and tactics; the
aesthetics patch writes names only for an export without one, so autopilot teams keep the
`write_names` route. The bundle is optional, under that one name, which the compiler, the
upgrader and the checks recognize.
Why: the maintainer's aim is one folder per team that compiles for any target version; one
owner per field means a name or a look never has two sources that drift apart, and either half
alone keeps working as today. The maintainer's account of cup practice settles where it is
used: official cups have two deadlines and often two builders, so they keep two exports; a
Complete export is made at a cup's end to collect a team for invitationals, which have one
deadline and one organizer, so the compiler applies `tactics.toml` in its own savefile stage.
By 4cc rule roster slot `NN` holds player `team id × 100 + NN`, so the two halves' player
addressing agrees by definition.
Plan: `plans/aesthetics_export/player_folders.md` "Complete export".

## 2026-10-21 — aatf, pes_savefile, save_editor — The roster order is checked, and drag reorder never breaks it
Decision: the AATF host checks for every ruleset, in Rust before the script, that roster slot
`NN` holds player `team id × 100 + NN`, an error (`RosterOrder`) per slot that does not;
`pes_savefile::roster_order_breaks` holds the rule, also used by Team TOML's export notes and
by the compiler refusing a Complete export's `tactics.toml` onto a breaking team. The Save
editor's drag reorder trades the players' records between the ids, as 4ccEditor's spinner
does, instead of reordering the roster as the plan and the draft had it.
Why: the rule is 4cc's definition and the only link between the aesthetics export (by id) and
a Team TOML (by slot); the maintainer asked for a check because PES lets a roster be
reordered, which a real PES 16 texport of team 804 shows (80401, 80402, 80423, ...). A host
check reaches every ruleset without each one repeating it and leaves the hashed `logic.rhai`
alone. SE-GUI-08 as written reordered the roster, breaking the rule on every drag;
4ccEditor's move (`main.cpp`, `UDN_DELTAPOS`: `PlayerExport`/`PlayerImport` swapped,
`copy_id` traded back to match the slot, numbers untouched) shows the move members know.
Plan: `plans/aatf_rules.md` "The host"; `plans/save_editor.md` "Editing UI", the Player list
bullet, and SE-GUI-08; `plans/aesthetics_export/player_folders.md` "Complete export".

## 2026-10-21 — save_editor — The parity table states each 4ccEditor operation's effect, read from its source
Decision: every 4ccEditor control whose handler does more than store a value has its effect
written in `plans/save_editor.md`'s parity table or "Editing UI", read from `origin/master` of
the official repository: the Set and Bump stats ranges and field scope, Copy/Swap's field set,
the boots and gloves numbering (gloves "like the boots" added), names to positions, the TSV's
columns (COM styles added, Finishing as the rating), Fix database's base-copy and strip-flag
repair, the squad load's section split, "Is a copy?"'s edit flags, and the info strip's rename
flag, upper-cased shirt name and radio Captain. Kept apart on purpose: Bump reads -10 whole,
the boots numbering does not stop at a missing id, a `.bak` at every save, the TSV through a
save dialog, the color rounding, Open's version detection, and the hidden debug shortcuts
dropped. The "Make everyone else Messi" action is the maintainer's local experiment, out of
scope.
Why: SE-GUI-08 was written from a control's name and reversed its effect; a source audit
(2026-10-21) found the same gap, smaller, in twenty other controls. The official repository
merged the Tactics fork the docs had named as the reference, so the reference is now one.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Feature inventory", "Crate layout" (`widgets.rs`), "Editing
UI", "Interchange formats", SE-GUI-24 and 27; `spec/save_editor.md` "Background: 4ccEditor".

## 2026-10-21 — music_export — A `.4ccm` reads as Rigdio reads it wherever that decides the song; strict where Rigdio crashes or guesses
Decision: the 10.0f audit of Rigdio v2.2.0 against the built crate is ruled row by row on one
principle: where Rigdio's reading decides which song plays, Studio matches it; where Rigdio
crashes, drops what the author typed, or loads a typo, Studio refuses the line, naming it.
Matched: an entry's conditions are checked in the written order, stopping at the first that
fails, so a later one neither unloads the entry nor spends a `once` nor asks for the goal
minute; `once` is spent when the check reaches it (`goals >= 2;once` plays on the second goal;
Studio's crate spent it at the first press, so it never played); the `goal` fallback is one list
per team, an unload or a spent `once` holding for every button; `randomise` reached on a
fallback entry draws among the fallback's entries; the random warcry pool takes the
fallback's warcries; a press after `advance` that finds nothing plays the first other
non-warcry entry, else the one that ended; the view asks for the goal minute only when the
walk reaches a `time`; `name` only as the first significant line; flag keywords and values
case-insensitive; a leading byte-order mark dropped; a song path always under the export (a
leading separator dropped, a drive-qualified path missing, superseding 2026-10-18's "a
root-level anchor holds"); `[]` read as no token and never
written, nor a one-word group. An export with no `anthem`, or players and no `goal`, loads with
a warning and the button absent, where Rigdio raises `KeyError`. Kept as departures, now
listed in the plan: the refusals of extra, malformed or unknown arguments, `event` misplaced,
empty names and slots; `not` keeping its bracketed group and holding after a never-again
condition; case-insensitive scorers and `opponent`; subfolder lookups; `advance`'s draw
leaving out the entry that ended (2026-10-18).
Why: a member's file was tested by ear in Rigdio, so a reading that changes which song plays
breaks a file that "worked", silently, on match day; a refusal at load breaks nothing that
played. The `once` divergence was found only by reading Rigdio's `check` against the crate,
which is why the audit exists (the SE-GUI-08 lesson, `AGENTS.md` "Before a tool phase").
The player's controls (part 2 of the audit) are ruled when that tool's Acceptance is written.
Plan: `plans/music_player.md` "Grammar", "Conditions", "File resolution", "Model" (the
selection's `TeamLists`, replacing the per-button `PriorityList`), "Song selection", "GUI
view", "Dropped features and compatibility notes", the fork's row in "Background", "Event
clips revived"; `plans/music_export_editor.md` "What the editor does", "Open questions".

## 2026-10-21 — aesthetics_export, music_player — A Complete export may carry the team's music as `Music/`
Decision: a team export may hold its music export as a root folder `Music/`: one `.4ccm`
(any file name) and its songs, resolved against that folder, so the folder copied out loads
in the Music player or Rigdio unchanged. The Team compiler never reads or packs it, the
Export upgrader carries it over, and the export checks parse it and resolve its songs, every
finding a Warning (none drops the export: no compiled output depends on the music), including
a `Music/` with no `.4ccm` or several and a `.4ccm` naming another team. A referee export has
none. The Music player's library scan also reads `<export>/Music/*.4ccm`, so a folder of
Complete exports, or the organizer's pack of their `Music/` folders, is a library as it is.
The folder is capitalized and files lower case, every export's naming rule. A submission
server that checks, rejects and compiles at the deadline is recorded as unscheduled.
Why: the maintainer (2026-10-21): the streamer is usually not the organizer, but organizers
often gather every team's music into one download for the streamer, and a future server
should hand the organizer one link per group (DLC, savefile, music pack). A team's music is
the one part of its identity a collected Complete export would otherwise leave behind. A
Warning, not an Error, because an Error drops the export from a compile the music never
reaches.
Plan: `plans/aesthetics_export/player_folders.md` "Complete export"; `plans/music_player.md`
"Autopilot" (auto team loading); `plans/core/development_plan.md` "Unscheduled tools".

## 2026-10-21 — core — The submission server's in-game check runs on a Windows GPU worker, not on the server
Decision: the unscheduled submission server may also check its compile in game: install the
DLC and the savefile into the cup's PES version, run the Aesthetics ATF bot over every team and
publish the stills and clips on a page per team. That part runs on a Windows machine with a GPU
and that version installed, which takes the job from the server and uploads the captures; the
server keeps the checks, the compile and the page.
Why: the maintainer asked (2026-10-21) whether the server could run it. PES needs a real GPU on
Windows, the bot's virtual pad a Windows driver (ViGEmBus) and its recording OBS; `bonfire` has
8 virtual cores, 15 GB and a virtual display adapter only (read 2026-10-21), and software
rendering would not play the bot's real-time clips. The in-game harness (`scripts/ingame/`)
already installs a CPK in a test slot, drives the pad and captures through OBS; installing the
savefile beside it is the missing step.
Plan: `plans/core/development_plan.md` "Unscheduled tools".

## 2026-10-21 — tooling — `mutants-diff` runs each crate on its own, and the timeout multiplier is back to 5
Decision: `scripts/mutants_diff.py` runs one cargo-mutants per crate the diff mutates
(`--in-diff <diff> -p <crate>`), one after the other, each split or local by its own estimate,
each crate's results moved to `mutants.diff/<crate>/` and every survivor listed in
`mutants.diff/missed_all.txt`; `.cargo/mutants.toml`'s `timeout_multiplier` goes from 3 back to
cargo-mutants' default 5.
Why: a mutant times out at a multiple of the run's baseline, and one run's baseline tests
every crate it mutates, so a hung mutant of a crate with fast tests waited out the slowest
crate's suite (751 s here at `mutants-diff 95f20eac`, nine timeouts costing about 2.5 h of
job time). Uneven shares by machine speed would gain less: the timeouts, not the machines'
speed, dominated that run. A crate's own baseline costs one build per crate, about a minute,
and makes 5x cheap again, which leaves slow tests in a starved low-priority run room before
they count as hangs (the maintainer, 2026-10-21).
Plan: `RUNBOOK.md` "Mutation runs and the VPS"; `CONTRIBUTING.md` "Mutation runs" (where the
results land).

## 2026-10-21 — music_export — `knockouts` beside other match types is refused
Decision: `match knockouts` expands to the five knockout stages only when `knockouts` is the
line's sole argument; beside other types (`match knockouts final`) the line is refused,
naming the word.
Why: Rigdio expands it only alone and otherwise keeps it as a type no match has, so that line
plays in the final only there, where expanding it played it in every knockout stage. Under
the earlier entry's principle (a reading that changes the song matches Rigdio; what Rigdio
silently drops is refused), a refusal at load breaks nothing that played and tells the author
the word did nothing.
Plan: `plans/music_player.md` "Conditions" (the `match` row).

## 2026-10-21 — aatf — Autumn 26 follows the wiki's written rules where the two 4ccEditor editions differ
Decision: the six places where `autumn26.rhai` (transcribed from the fork's `Autumn_2026_AATF`)
and the official 4ccEditor's Autumn 26 edition differ are ruled against the wiki's
`Appendix:Rules` Chapter III as edited on 2026-10-06 (read 2026-10-21):
- D1, a medal's free COM style is traded for a free extra A position ("Medals may trade the Free
  COM Playing Style for a Double A Position instead"), not given an extra free COM or A on top:
  each tier's free COM styles (gold 2, silver 1, bronze 1) become one choice each, a free COM
  style or a free extra A position (never GK). Gold may trade both, as the official edition does
  (the wiki's singular "the Free COM" was written for the tiers with one).
- D2, bronze gets 2 free trick cards, not 3 ("2 trick cards and 1 COM Playing Style").
- D3, the Red CB allowance goes to a non-medal player registered at CB ("Center Back in both
  Registered and Playable Position"), with no further condition: neither the fork's "fielded
  only at CB" nor the official edition's "CB his only A position".
- D4, the allowance lets that CB stand at 189 and count as 185 ("If GK or CB, increase height to
  189cm", the goalkeepers' wording), and is optional: at 185 he stays tall. Before, it applied at
  every height, so a Red CB at the ordinary 185 fielded at CB was in no bracket, an error on a
  legal team, and 180 to 184 counted as mid.
- D5, a Green silver at 194 is legal with every stat 3 lower, as Studio has it (the official
  edition fails every one, a bug the fork fixed).
- D6, every player on the first preset of the deadline export stands at one of his A positions:
  `universal.fielded_at_a: [1]` set.
Why: the maintainer's standing rule that the wiki is the source of truth; each of the two
editions departs from it somewhere. D3 drops a restriction both editions add (each its own),
which a manager may have relied on as written; the alternative reading is noted here so the
maintainer can reinstate one. Heights 186 to 188 for such a CB ("can go up to 189") stay outside
every bracket, as the goalkeepers' do: nothing is gained by them, and the table's wording is the
goalkeepers'. Not a difference, noted: both editions and Studio take 176 to 179 as mid where the
wiki says "exactly 180", a leniency that gains no one anything.
Plan: `spec/aatf_rules.md` "The official ruleset" (with the change); WORKLOG 20.1.

## 2026-10-21 — aatf — Autumn 26 suggests a medal's untaken trade
Decision: `autumn26.rhai` lists `"choices"` in `suggestions`, so a medal who keeps neither his
free COM style nor an extra A position for a trade is told of it (`UnusedChoice`, the trade's
label).
Why: before D1 a medal's free COM style was unconditional, and one holding none got the
`Unused com` hint; as a trade, the free style exists only once taken, so without the listing the
member who could use it hears nothing. The 20.1 review's S1-2.
Plan: `spec/aatf_rules.md` "The official ruleset" (the block's `suggestions`).

## 2026-10-22 — pes_savefile — The roster-order rule is a method on the team record
Decision: `TeamEntry::roster_order_breaks(&self) -> Vec<(u8, u32)>` (roster slots 0-based as
stored, the player ids they hold), not the plan's `roster_order_breaks(&EditFile, TeamId)`.
Why: the rule reads the team's roster alone; the AATF host (`TeamView::new`, which looks the
entry up) and Team TOML's export (`from_team`, which is handed it) both hold the entry, and a
whole-file signature would make the export reach for a file it is not given.
Plan: `plans/aatf_rules.md` "The host"; `plans/pes_savefile/operations.md` "Team TOML", the
paragraph "Roster order".

## 2026-10-22 — gui — Studio opens at 1440 × 900 points, fitted to a smaller monitor
Decision: the window's default is 1440 × 900 points (16:10), centered, replacing the 2026-10-21
half-monitor default. Points are logical pixels, so the display scaling applies. On a monitor
whose logical size cannot hold it, the window opens at the largest 16:10 size within 90% of
the monitor's logical width and height (1037 × 648 on a 1080p monitor at 150%). The drafts
draw at that default and offer the smallest one.
Why: the maintainer's request (75% of the monitor's width at 16:10, then a fixed width, since a
share of an ultrawide monitor is too wide, with system scaling accounted for). The 90% fit is
the lead's: a fixed size alone opens past the screen on a laptop or a scaled 1080p monitor,
and 90% leaves the taskbar and the title bar room.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Shell layout", "The window's size", and "Prototypes before
implementation", the Size bullet.

## 2026-10-22 — ruleset_editor — The data block preview is behind a "Show preview" toggle
Decision: the Ruleset editor's data block pane shows only while a "Show preview" toggle at the
top right of the tool's bar is on, off at every start.
Why: the maintainer's request: open beside the form, the pane left the sections a third of the
window.
Plan: `plans/ruleset_editor.md` "The editor".

## 2026-10-22 — aatf — Autumn 26 takes the 4cc organizer's answers
Decision: on the seven points where the wiki's Appendix:Rules and the official 4ccEditor
(`82879a7`, Autumn 26 Version B) differ, the organizer chose (2026-10-22, the answer line "1.
gold-trades=editor 2.red-cb-who=wiki 3.red-cb-185=wiki 4.green-silver-194=wiki 5.mid-176-179=wiki
6.gold-gk-194=wiki 7.red-manlet-bonus=wiki"): a gold trades both free COM styles; any non-medal
registered at CB may be 189 under Red, and may stay at 185; a Green silver at 194 is legal at
every stat 3 lower; heights 176 to 179 are in no bracket (mid is exactly 180); a gold or a
goalkeeper at 194 cm is an error, not a warning; the Red 175 cm bonus is optional (a one-option
`choice`), the tier's base rating legal too, and names the tiers it has an amount for (regular,
goalkeeper, bronze, silver), so a gold at 175 is offered no bonus he cannot take. The first four confirm the 2026-10-21 rulings
(D1, D3, D4, D5); the last three change `autumn26.rhai`.
Why: the organizer sets the cup's rules; the page asked each point against the wiki and the
editor alone (`.tmp/20_au26/autumn26_rule_choices.html`).
Plan: `spec/aatf_rules.md` "The official ruleset" (its block and prose); WORKLOG 20.2.

## 2026-10-22 — save_editor — 4ccEditor's hidden team trim (Ctrl+Shift+T) is dropped
Decision: the Save editor has no counterpart of 4ccEditor's Ctrl+Shift+T on the team selector,
which empties a team's roster slots past 23.
Why: the maintainer's answer: cups no longer need it. It is in 4ccEditor's first public commit
(`49926fa`, 2019-08-16) and was last widened to PES 19's 40-slot rosters (`8d78775`).
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Feature inventory", the hidden shortcut's row.

## 2026-10-22 — save_editor — A drag reorder leaves each slot its face and hairstyle
Decision: the move keeps on each slot, besides its id, appearance id and base copy, the in-game
face run's face structure and hairstyle; the four fields of that run the spinner's record holds
(skin colour, iris colour, player gloves and their colour) move with the rest of the record.
Why: 4ccEditor's spinner moves exactly its `player_export` record (`editor.h`, `PlayerExport`/
`PlayerImport`), which ends at `iris_col` and has no face or hair; the 8.9c2 audit compared
every `PlayerEntry` field with it and found no other difference.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Editing UI", the Player list bullet, and SE-GUI-08.

## 2026-10-22 — mutants — The VPS keeps this project under 30 GiB and 20 GiB free, cleaned at each phase's close
Decision: every run that uses the mutation host first empties its tests' temp folder
(`~/studio-mutants/tmp`), then refuses when `~/studio-mutants` holds over 30 GiB or the host's
disk has under 20 GiB free; at each phase's close the lead removes the clone's build cache
(`scripts/remote_clean_target.sh`).
Why: the maintainer affords about 40 GB on a disk the host's production services share, and
asked for the free-space check as well. Between phase closes the clone's cache reached 22 GB
and a run's build copies take about 8 GiB more, so a phase-close cleanup alone fits the 40;
but one new leaking test filled 27 GB in two days, so only a check at every run catches it in
time. The 20 GiB floor leaves the host about 10 GiB while a run's copies stand.
Plan: RUNBOOK "The scratch folder"; `scripts/mutants.py` `REMOTE_DISK_BUDGET`, `REMOTE_FREE_FLOOR`.

## 2026-10-22 — tooling — The hot dependencies build optimized in dev, and the two all-teams CLI tests check fewer teams
Decision: `rhai`, `zlib-rs`, `md-5` and `sha2` build at `opt-level = 3` in the dev profile
(as `block_compression` does), and two of the Save editor's CLI tests stop doing their work 220
times: SE-AATF-05's test checks five cup teams (the fixture's others renumbered below the cup
range) and asserts exactly those print, in id order; SE-TOML-02's test checks every exported
file's version and team id lines as text and parses three back whole (its THEN says so).
Why: the save editor's 49 CLI tests took 417 s run one by one, 179 of them in those two
tests: the AATF check runs the rules interpreter unoptimized (0.5 s a team; 19 s for 220 with
`rhai` optimized), and the export test parsed 220 files of 5,143 lines each in debug code (the
export itself took 2.5 s). The four crates cut a one-team test from 5.6 to 2.5 s at no build
cost measured; optimizing every dependency (`"*"`) cut the workspace's tests from 351 to 209 s
but cost 88 s per cold build, which every mutation run's copy of the tree pays, so it is not
done. The maintainer: "don't be afraid of reducing the fixtures". SE-TOML-02's library half in
`pes_savefile` (49 s) samples its text pass the same way, as its round-trip siblings already
did; the exhaustive model passes over every fixture team and player (11 to 17 s each) stay,
since the fixtures' records are not placeholders: every team is distinct (220 of 220; 200 of
202 on PES 18) and each version has 415 to 2,509 distinct players.
Plan: `Cargo.toml` `[profile.dev.package.*]`; `spec/save_editor.md` SE-TOML-02.

## 2026-10-22 — aatf — A loaded ruleset is shared across threads, and the whole-save check runs its teams in parallel
Decision: `rhai` builds with its `sync` feature, so `aatf::Rules` is `Send + Sync`;
`check-aatf` checks its teams in parallel (rayon) on the one loaded file and reports them in id
order as before. The Live AATF worker and the AATF panel's whole-save check will use the
window's `Rules` the same way. `sync` brings two small crates, `no-std-compat` and `spin` 0.5
(rhai's lock), both through `cargo deny`. The script's own work is not cut here: a rewrite of
`logic.rhai`'s per-tier reading is a worklog step of its own.
Why: measured where one team's check spends its 56 ms (release, the official ruleset, a PES
2017 save's 220 cup teams): building the team's view 0.03 ms, copying it under 0.001 ms, an
empty script 0.03 ms, so there was nothing outside the script to cut; `read_player`'s profile
of each tier is 50 of the 56 ms (rhai copies every map argument per call). Checking teams on
16 threads takes the command from 13.2 s to 2.0 s with identical output, and `sync` costs about
3% per team. Loading one `Rules` per thread instead would pay the ~70 ms load and its sample
check per thread, and the Live worker could not take the window's ruleset at all.
Plan: `spec/aatf_rules.md` "The host"; `plans/save_editor.md` "Configurable AATF rules" (Live
AATF); the root `Cargo.toml`'s `rhai` line.

## 2026-10-22 — save_editor — With ALL picked, Live AATF checks the selected player's team
Decision: Live AATF's "open team" is the team selector's; with ALL picked, it is the selected
player's team, the one the info strip and the tabs are editing.
Why: under ALL no team is open, and the edits Live AATF follows are the selected player's, so
his team is the one whose list should shrink; checking every team instead would be the AATF
panel's whole-save run on every edit, and checking nothing would switch the panel off in the
list's default view of the PES 21 sample.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Configurable AATF rules" (Live AATF); the draft's `liveTeam`.

## 2026-10-22 — save_editor — Randomize motion draws within each version's measured ranges
Decision: the Appearance tab's Randomize sets every motion but the dribbling motion to a value
from 1 to the version's measured top (`pes_savefile::schema::limits::motion_top`, shown scale),
one undoable edit; the motion fields' ranges are the same tops.
Why: 4ccEditor's button (`main.cpp` `IDB_MOTI_RAND`) draws from 1 and skips the dribbling
motion, which we keep, but its two fixed sets of maxima, not the version's: on PES 15 it can
write arm movements 6 to 8 and celebrations 113 to 122, which that game does not have, and on
PES 18 and 19 it never reaches celebrations 123 to 127 and 123 to 140. The measured table
already decides the Team TOML's and the conversions' ranges, so the tab agrees with them.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Editing UI" (Tabs, Appearance).

## 2026-10-22 — save_editor — Team operations act on the selected player's team alone
Decision: every Team menu operation acts on the selected player's team (under ALL too), on
every filled roster slot, as one undoable edit.
Why: 4ccEditor's team operations do so (`team_vis_clear`, `team_created_set`, `team_fpc_on`
take the selected player's `team_ind`), but its `player_names_to_positions` renames every row
its list shows, which under ALL is every player of the save. One scope for every item of one
menu, not a menu whose fourth item reaches the whole save because its list happened to be ALL.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Feature inventory", Team operations.

## 2026-10-22 — save_editor — FPC keeps a model's own IDs, and is two actions, not a checkbox
Decision: hiding writes the hide preset's boots or gloves ID only where the record holds 0 (or
already the hide ID), showing writes 0 only where it holds the hide ID; any other ID is kept.
The Appearance tab reads `is_fpc_player` as a line and offers Hide body and Show body; Ctrl+I
shows a player read as hidden and hides any other. The hide IDs stay `libs/fpc`'s constants for
the editor and the compiler alike until the suite-common setting is built for both.
Why: the wiki's hide list allows "your FBM's custom boots", the compiler keeps a
`settings.toml`'s own ID over the marker's (TC-BIN-29), and 4ccEditor's enable and disable
functions swap only 0 and the hide IDs: writing 55 over an FBM's own boots ID would unlink his
body model. A checkbox drawn from `is_fpc_player` would then stay unticked after hiding such a
player, and a second click would hide him again rather than show him. A setting in one tool
only would let the two tools' hide IDs differ.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Full Player Customization (FPC)"; SE-GUI-11 reworded.

## 2026-10-22 — aatf (DBC7) — The stat total: the player's own targets, over every ability stat
Decision: the DBC7 organizer confirmed both readings `dbc7.rhai` already took: a regular's or a
silver's ability stats, added up, may not exceed the sum of his own targets (so a Manlet regular
who takes the +5 is held to an all-82 sum), and the sum runs over every ability stat the
version has, an outfielder's goalkeeping stats included.
Why: a flat all-77 cap would leave the Manlet bonus nothing but points to trade between stats,
and a per-role list of stats would be a second rule to maintain for no gain the organizer wants.
Plan: `plans/aatf_rules.md` "DBC7" (the stat-total bullet); `QUESTIONS.md` entry removed.

## 2026-10-22 — releases — 0.x are test releases; compatibility contracts start at 1.0.0
Decision: 0.1.0 is an early test release for a restricted group of testers, told in person of
every change: no released surface is a compatibility contract before 1.0.0, and the
maintenance-mode section of `AGENTS.md` is written for 1.0.0 (Phase 16) rather than at 0.1.0.
0.1.0 ships the bundle and `CHANGELOG.md` only; the help chapters beyond the views' own topics,
the update check and notice, and the teams-list merge move to Release 0.2.0 or later.
