Why: holding the export layout, the settings keys and the finding codes to a contract while a
handful of testers use them would make every early correction an upgrader migration; told in
person, a tester can take the change by hand. What a tester would notice still gets its
`CHANGELOG.md` line (the rule `AGENTS.md` already sets once a release exists), since the notice
is written from it. Without the teams-list merge a new build keeps a tester's old working list,
which a tester can replace by hand when told.
Plan: `plans/core/development_plan.md` "Releases", "Release 0.1.0", the new "Release 0.2.0",
Phase 16; `plans/core/distribution.md` (the updater's steps ship at 0.2.0);
`spec/core/distribution.md` (the compatibility rule binds from 1.0.0).

## 2026-10-22 — save_editor — Set and Bump stats set no edit flag; Copy and Swap pick the other player by team, then slot
Decision: Set all stats and Bump all stats write the ability values and no edit flag. Copy and
Swap stats pick the other player with two combo boxes, the team (the selected player's first)
and then one of its filled roster slots, rather than 4ccEditor's typed player ids or the
draft's one list of every player; Copy writes the picked player's stats onto the selected one.
Why: 4ccEditor's two dialogs only fill the Abilities tab's fields, as typing does, and neither
it nor Studio's Abilities tab sets a flag for that, so a flag here would make one write path
differ from the other. A cup save holds about 4,600 players: one list of them all cannot be
browsed, and a typed id is the number a member has to look up first.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Feature inventory", the Player operations rows.

## 2026-10-22 — save_editor — The FPC interference findings are message-catalog codes
Decision: the Appearance tab draws `fpc::check`'s findings through the tool's message catalog,
five codes with member-facing text, rather than text of its own in the view.
Why: a finding's text written in the view would be a second copy of what the help's Messages
topic lists, and the two would drift; through the catalog the tab and the topic read one row.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Full Player Customization (FPC)", the bullet on the findings.

## 2026-10-22 — save_editor — Fix database: base copies only where the flag exists, no PES 17 table write, under the lock
Decision: Fix database repairs base copies only on PES 15 to 18, where the record has the
base-copy flag; it does not write PES 17's strip table; and it sits under the aesthetics lock,
one undo step. The rest is 4ccEditor's: the four visual flags cleared on every player, the
teams' strip flag cleared, the kit slots reset to Kit 1, Kit 2 and the goalkeeper's bound to
the team and the rest to the nonexistent team id.
Why: on PES 19 to 21 4ccEditor's rule reads `b_base_copy`, which its readers never set and its
constructor leaves uninitialized, so what it clears there is chance; a copy id is the player's
look on those versions. Its PES 17 repair steps 131 bytes (`write_dataOld` advances the cursor
by reference) over 132-byte entries and writes 0xFFFFC0 from bit 0, so it puts 0xC0 in the
strip-number byte and, past the first entry, writes into entries' bodies. Clear visual flags
is locked because it writes what a team's export owns; Fix database writes the same flags, and
one guard is one rule.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Feature inventory", the Database operations table.

## 2026-10-22 — fpc, studio_core, save_editor, team_compiler — The FPC hide IDs are two common settings bounded to the stock band
Decision: `fpc_hide_boots_id` (55) and `fpc_hide_gloves_id` (11) are common settings, carried
to `libs/fpc`'s hide preset as an `fpc::HideIds` argument that replaces the two constants; the
save editor's FPC actions and classifier and the compiler's `fpc_on` marker read them. A valid
ID is in the stock band, boots 1 to 100 and gloves 11 to 100; the settings menu bounds its rows
there, and a compile with a hand-set value outside is refused (exit code 2). Changing the
setting rewrites no save: a player hidden with the old ID reads "body shown".
Why: the plan made the IDs a suite-common setting (any nonexistent ID hides; 55 and 11 are the
4cc convention). One setting for both tools, since a compiler writing one ID and an editor
classifying by another would read every compiled FPC player as shown. Above 100 the compiler
allocates its per-team blocks (101 to 8900, `plan/ids.rs`), so a hide ID there would be a real
model of another player; gloves 1 to 10 are goalkeepers' real gloves. Keeping the constants
beside the setting would leave a second source every caller could reach for. Recognizing the
old ID as well after a change would be machinery for a setting changed once, if ever.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Full Player Customization (FPC)", `plans/libs/fpc.md`,
`plans/core/gui.md` "Settings menu", `plans/team_compiler/settings.md` "Common settings";
SE-GUI-31, TC-BIN-43.

## 2026-10-22 — save_editor, team_widgets, pes_savefile — The Tactics tab's edits where the draft and 4ccEditor differ
Decision: the instruction list is the version's stored table less Tight Marking, a held one
still shown; the target pick is enabled for Counter Target and Defensive only
(`Instruction::takes_player` in `pes_savefile`), and a pick that takes none sets the target to
255. Players to join the attack stay packed. The goalkeeper's slot is not dragged or edited;
Make GK swaps two starting-eleven entries. A preset copy or swap moves the whole preset, man
marking included. PES 20/21's instructions use the measured table (Anchoring at 0x0A), not
4ccEditor's, which numbers them as on 18/19.
Why: Tight Marking marks an opponent, set in a match; Edit mode does not offer it and 4ccEditor
leaves it out. One home for the target rule, so the editor and the Team creator cannot drift;
clearing a stale target keeps the record saying only what the tab shows. A gap in the join list
is a state 4ccEditor never writes. The keeper's lock is 4ccEditor's, and its drawing ignores
the stored keeper coordinates. Members bring a match's man marking into a team through the
game's own copy preset (2026-10-12), so a copy that dropped it would undo that. The PES 21
table was measured in game (`spec/pes_savefile/model.md`).
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Tactics editor".

## 2026-10-22 — save_editor — Slice 2's parity with 4ccEditor: four differences kept
Decision: run on the PES 16, 17 and 21 fixture saves, every batch operation and Fix database
gives 4ccEditor's fields but for four differences, kept: (1) Set player names to positions is
written (4ccEditor's never reaches the file); (2) Hide body on PES 15 to 17 sets no Custom skin
(4ccEditor sets it); (3) a rewritten name keeps the bytes after its terminator where 4ccEditor
zeroes them; (4) the rosters TSV ends lines with LF where 4ccEditor writes CRLF. Fix database's
two differences are the earlier entry's (base copies only where the flag exists, no PES 17
strip-table write).
Why: (1) the operation's effect is the one 4ccEditor's code means, and its Save drops it only
because the records are never marked changed; (2) the wiki, the source of truth, sets no skin
for the full hide and Custom is its partial hide's, and both tools' Show body converge on the
Light skin; (3) the game reads a name up to its terminator, and keeping the rest is what keeps
an opened-and-saved file byte-identical (both tools' were, on all three saves); (4) a
spreadsheet reads either, and the content is identical line for line.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Team operations", "Full Player Customization (FPC)"; the run's
outputs in `.tmp/8_9/parity/RESULT.md`.

## 2026-10-22 — team_widgets — A pitch player dropped on another exchanges the two starters
Decision: on the Tactics tab's pitch, a player dropped on another player exchanges the two
starters, their formation slots staying; one released on the grass moves to the snapped point;
one released off the pitch stays.
Why: the game's own formation screen swaps two players dropped on each other, and the marker's
drag carries the same payload as a starting-eleven row, whose drop on a marker already exchanges
them. Writing the drop point instead (the draft's first version) stacked two players on one spot,
a formation no member means; a release off the pitch clamped to the edge moved a player nobody
aimed at the edge.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Tactics editor", "What the controls write".

## 2026-10-23 — release — 0.0.1 also carries the Team compiler and the Export upgrader through their CLI, for VGL 27
Decision: the 0.0.1 preview build also ships the Team compiler and the Export upgrader, run
through their CLI, for the /vg/ League 27 (PES 2019 with FoxDen, from late November): managers
send old-format exports; the maintainer and the organizer upgrade and compile them, with Red as
the fallback. The window stays as planned, the two tools greyed out. The bundle's
`quick_compile.bat` runs the CLI compile until the Team compiler's view lands, and an interim
`quick_upgrade.bat` upgrades every export in `old_exports/` into `exports/` against the savefile
dropped onto it, stopping with a how-to when none is dropped. The console's progress line and run
summary move from 8.10 into 0.0.1. Two checks join the release: an interrupted run leaves no
half-written file the game reads, and a rehearsal on PES 2019 with VGL26's old exports. 0.0.1 has
no `CHANGELOG.md`; the file starts with 0.1.0.
Why: the maintainer's choice (one build rather than a separate compiler preview; "CLI-only"
meaning no GUI needed yet, not a binary without one; the progress line wanted; no changelog at
0.0.1; launchers like Red's, which runs its CLI from a bat). The lead's parts: the upgrader's
bat takes the save by drag-and-drop and never falls back to `--loose`, because loose mode is an
assumption the user opts into (`spec/export_upgrader.md` "CLI"), and a silent loose run on a
league's exports would write teams from guesses; `old_exports/` beside `exports/` keeps the two
formats apart, so the compiler never sees an old export; the interruption check and the
rehearsal come from the answer given before the choice (an interrupted compile was unchecked,
and no release had run the two tools end to end from a bundle).
Plan: `plans/core/development_plan.md` "Releases" (the DBC paragraph and "The /vg/ League 27
(VGL)"), `plans/core/architecture.md` "Launch modes", `plans/core/distribution.md`
"Distribution: portable .7z bundle".

## 2026-10-23 — save_editor, team_widgets — the Tactics pitch reproduces PES 2021's formation screen, with portraits
Decision: the Tactics tab's pitch is drawn as close as possible to PES 2021's own formation
screen (turf, lines, each starter as the game shows him), every starter by his portrait read from
the selected game's `download/` CPKs when that folder is found and holds one, the plain chip
otherwise; every version's save gets the same pitch.
Why: the maintainer's request: members read a formation the way the game shows it, and a pitch
that looks like the game's needs no translating. One look for every version rather than one per
game, because the look is the editor's, not data the version gates, and one reproduction is
what can be made exact.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Tactics editor" (the pitch's look); worklog 8.9g.

## 2026-10-23 — scripts — the citation audit spends its keys in order, the next when one is refused
Decision: `citation_audit.py` reads every key line of `STUDIO_SNAP_KEY_FILE` (after
`SUBQ_API_KEY`) and, when the service refuses the current key (HTTP 401-403, or a 429 still
returned after the retries), moves to the next for the rest of the run; the last key's refusal
is the run's error, the key never printed.
Why: the maintainer added a second SubQ key, to be used once the first runs out. The service's
answer to a spent key is not documented, so any refusal counts, rather than one code that might
be the wrong one and leave the run failing on a usable second key; a request error (400) does
not switch, since another key would fail it too.
Plan: `CONTRIBUTING.md` "Citation audit".

## 2026-10-23 — release, studio — every release before 1.0.0 is named Unlimited Tool Works
Decision: the pre-1.0.0 releases carry the codename Unlimited Tool Works on everything a user
sees (window title, About box, first-run prompt, `--help` header and usage examples, help
pages, readme, the executable
`UnlimitedToolWorks.exe`, the bundle's name), through one display-name constant; crates, docs and
the settings folder keep "4cc Studio"; nothing in the preview names 4cc Studio.
Why: the maintainer's choice: DBC7's and VGL 27's testers meet the suite at its least finished,
and a codename keeps that impression off the name it keeps; the maintainer announces the change
of name at 1.0.0. The settings folder keeps its name so testers' setups carry over with no
migration, which a renamed folder would need.
Plan: `plans/core/development_plan.md` "The preview's codename: Unlimited Tool Works";
`plans/core/distribution.md` bundle list; worklog 0.0.1d.

## 2026-10-23 — release — the 0.0.1 launchers name the bundle's `exports/` and count each upgrade
Decision: both bats live in `resources/bundle/`, checked out CRLF; `quick_compile.bat` passes
the bundle's `exports/` as the compile's root rather than relying on `exports_folder_path`;
`quick_upgrade.bat` runs one `export-upgrader upgrade` per folder, `.zip` and `.7z` in
`old_exports/`, counts exit code 0 as upgraded and any other as not, prints
`Upgraded: N. Not upgraded: M.`, and with no savefile dropped prints how to drop one and writes
nothing.
Why: the upgrade writes into the bundle's `exports/`, so a compile reading the setting's folder
instead would miss what was just upgraded once a tester points the setting elsewhere; one call
per export keeps a refused export (its output already there, a team the save lacks) from
stopping the rest. cmd misreads a batch file's labels with LF line ends.
Plan: `plans/core/development_plan.md` "The /vg/ League 27 (VGL)"; `plans/core/distribution.md`
bundle list; worklog 0.0.1b.

## 2026-10-23 — studio, team_compiler — the console's progress line counts exports from their events and the manifest's tasks as "parts"
Decision: the progress line's exports counter is the printer's count of `ExportStarted` (total)
and `ExportProcessed` (done) events; its second counter is `Progress`, which the Team compiler
emits as each build-manifest task commits, labelled "parts"; `Progress` keeps its one pair; the
line draws from the first export, and a stream that ends with no `Complete` (a `check`, an
upgrade) clears it.
Why: every export starts in the validation pass before any is compiled, so the events already
carry the total and no new event or field is needed; a task is not always a folder (a kit, the
logo, a Common directory), so "folders" would not add up to an export's folders, and the
manifest's tasks are the unit that commits whole. The printer is tool-neutral and cannot know
a `Complete` is coming until the stream ends, and a count left behind by a run that sends none
would read as unfinished.
Plan: `plans/core/architecture.md` "The console's progress line and run summary"; worklog 0.0.1a.

## 2026-10-23 — studio, team_compiler — the run summary counts exports skipped, and distinct folders
Decision: `Complete` gains `skipped_exports`, the distinct exports a `DropExport` finding
refused, and the console's summary reads `Done: 1,284 files written, 1 export skipped,
2 folders skipped, 1 folder with errors, 0:42`; `skipped_folders` counts distinct folders (a
file's finding counting its folder), not findings.
Why: a review found that an export refused whole shows in no folder count, so a run that left
a team out ended on "0 folders skipped", and that a player folder with two broken files was
counted twice; the plan's four items were silent on both.
Plan: `plans/core/architecture.md` "The console's progress line and run summary"; worklog 0.0.1a.

## 2026-10-23 — team_compiler — an unfinished upgrade's staging folder is skipped with a Warning
Decision: the compiler's discovery skips a folder whose name ends in `.upgrading` with the
Warning `export_upgrade_unfinished` naming it; the folder takes no part in duplicate detection
or planning. The upgrader keeps refusing while it exists (EU-CLI-05), and the member removes it.
Why: 0.0.1c's kill measurement left `<output>.upgrading` in `exports/` after every upgrade
killed mid-write (10 of 10 fired kills); `quick_upgrade.bat` upgrades into `exports/`, so the
next `quick_compile.bat` compiled the half-migrated folder as an export of the same team. A
skip with a Warning rather than an upgrader that sweeps its dead staging: a sweep needs a lock
the upgrader does not hold today, and the compile must not take the folder in either case.
Plan: `plans/team_compiler/pipeline.md` "1. Reader"; worklog 0.0.1c.

## 2026-10-23 — studio_core, release — the codename's reach: two constants, spelled pages, name-free file text
Decision: the code reads Unlimited Tool Works from two `studio_core` constants (display name,
executable name); the help pages and launchers spell `UnlimitedToolWorks` as text, checked by
a test over the help export and `--help` that fails on any "4cc Studio"; text a file format
keeps (ruleset headers and logic banner, the shared-IDs comment) names no product; a CPK's
`Tvers` field and the settings folder keep "4cc Studio", and the data-location help page
names that folder's path.
Why: a Markdown page and a batch file cannot read a Rust constant, so "one line" holds for the
code only, and the test lists the rest for 1.0.0. Name-free file text, not the codename, because
the logic banner is hashed into a ruleset's identity: a name there makes each switch a new logic
version. The folder path stays because a tester's setup must carry over to 1.0.0 and a member
may need to find it.
Plan: `plans/core/development_plan.md` "The preview's codename: Unlimited Tool Works".

## 2026-10-23 — release — the bundle's layout and the recipe's refusals
Decision: `just release <version>` packs `target/dist/UnlimitedToolWorks-<version>-windows.7z`
with one top folder, `UnlimitedToolWorks-<version>/`, beside a `sha256sum`-format checksum; the
readme is `README.txt`; the recipe refuses a dirty tree, a mismatched version, an existing
archive and a stale readme, checks the archive's listing against the staged files, and reads the
executable's name from the built exe's `--help`.
Why: one top folder, not loose files, because "Extract here" into Downloads otherwise scatters
the exe among the member's files; `.txt`, not `.md`, because a double-click opens Notepad on any
Windows; the exe's name from the exe, not a second constant in the script, so the codename has
one home in code.
Plan: `plans/core/distribution.md` "Distribution: portable .7z bundle".

## 2026-10-23 — release — the workspace version is 0.0.1 until the preview is cut
Decision: the workspace version goes from 0.1.0 to 0.0.1, and `just release` finds the target
directory through `cargo metadata` (the archive in its `dist/`) rather than `target/`.
Why: the spec makes the workspace version the next release's, and 0.0.1 now comes before 0.1.0;
with 0.1.0 left, `just release 0.0.1` refused at its version check and `just release 0.1.0` at
its readme check, so no version could be released (the sidekick's report on 0.0.1d2). Asked of
cargo, not assumed, because CONTRIBUTING's recipes never hardcode `target/`.
Plan: `spec/core/distribution.md` "Versioning: one workspace version, one exception";
`plans/core/distribution.md` "Distribution: portable .7z bundle".

## 2026-10-23 — studio, studio_core — a CLI-only tool: registered, drawn as its planned entry
Decision: in the 0.0.1 preview the registry in `studio` marks the Team compiler and the Export
upgrader CLI-only; the sidebar draws each as its planned entry (grayed, not clickable, a tooltip
saying it runs from the command line in this version) and never makes it active, while it stays
registered for its CLI, its help chapter and its settings section (ST-SIDE-08).
Why: the plan wants them "greyed out on the sidebar as the planned tools are", and nothing did
it: a registered tool was always drawn live (0.0.1d's review S1-1). Registered and marked, not
left out of the window's tool list, because the help window's chapters and the settings menu
come from that list, and the readme sends members to the help for every finding's code. The
mark is the build's, not a `StudioTool` method, since which tools a build shows is its choice.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Sidebar" item 3 and ST-SIDE-08.

## 2026-10-23 — bundle — the upgrade launcher's rerun: the readme moves upgraded exports out
Decision: the bundle's readme tells the member to move the upgraded old exports out of
`old_exports/` after a run; the launcher and the upgrader stay as they are, a second run
refusing each export already upgraded ("the output folder already exists") and counting it as
not upgraded.
Why: the 0.0.1e rehearsal's second pass printed 22 such refusals; VGL's organizer receives
exports over several days and reruns the launcher. The refusal is right (replacing the folder
would lose edits made since), and the launcher cannot tell it from another abort (both exit 3)
nor predict the output's name (the upgrader names it from the resolved team), so a skip in the
bat would need the upgrader to grow a new exit code for one launcher that goes when the view
lands. One readme step costs nothing.
Plan: `plans/core/development_plan.md` "The /vg/ League 27 (VGL)", the `quick_upgrade.bat` item.

## 2026-10-23 — save_editor, team_widgets — the Tactics pitch is painted from the game's measured screen
Decision: the Tactics pitch is painted from measurements of PES 2021's formation screen (its own
pitch texture, decoded from `gamePlan.bin` in `dt11_x64.cpk`, and a capture of the screen): the
turf's eleven bands and grain, the lines at 20% white, the screen's slot-to-badge mapping fitted
within half a pixel, the keeper at the screen's own spot, and each marker as portrait, badge and
name with the game's colours. The badge leaves out the overall rating; the screen's selection
corners mark the editor's open popover and armed mode.
Why: the maintainer asked for the game's own look (DECISIONS 2026-10-23, the pitch with
portraits). Painted rather than the texture drawn: the texture is Konami's, the program does
not ship it, and a member with only an older game has no PES 2021 install to read it from,
while every version's save draws the same pitch. The rating is the game's computation, which
the suite does not have; a number of ours beside the game's own position badge would read as
the game's. The editor's states reuse the screen's marks so the pitch introduces no look of its
own.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Tactics editor" (the pitch's look); worklog 8.9g.

## 2026-10-23 — save_editor, team_widgets — the pitch's long names scroll on one clock from the tab's opening
Decision: a starter's name wider than his badge scrolls as the game's formation screen scrolls
it (13.5 s period, 40 px/s, a 16 px gap before its start follows), every name's period starting
when the pitch first shows it, still first; the editor does not reproduce the game's stagger
between names.
Why: the maintainer asked for the game's scrolling (an idea, to be dropped if costly; it is one
offset function and a repaint request while a name moves). Four names measured over 30 s
captures share the period and the speed, but two started 2.1 s apart by a rule the captures do
not establish; an invented stagger would be a guess dressed as the game's, and names that start
together read the same way.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Tactics editor" (the pitch's look, "A marker"); worklog 8.9g.

## 2026-10-23 — cpk, pes_savefile, team_compiler — the DpFileList reader and the portrait path move to the libs
Decision: the Team compiler's DpFileList reader (`bins/dpfl.rs`, with its fixtures and tests)
moves to `cpk`, its errors a `thiserror` enum with the same texts; the portrait's CPK path
(`paths::portrait`) moves to `pes_savefile` beside the player tables' paths. The compiler calls
both from there; the Save editor reads portraits through them.
Why: the Save editor's pitch shows each starter's portrait from the selected game's
`download/` CPKs, which needs the list's load order and the path the compiler writes portraits
to. A copy in the editor would be two rules for one path, and the day one changed, compiled
portraits would stop showing in the editor with no test failing. `cpk` is the CPK family's
crate and has no other home for a list of CPKs; `pes_savefile` already holds the CPK paths the
compiler and the editor share (the player tables).
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Tactics editor" (the pitch's look, "Portraits"); worklog 8.9g
slice 2.

## 2026-10-23 — save_editor — a listed CPK that is missing leaves the pitch without portraits
Decision: when `download/DpFileList.bin` lists a CPK that is not in the folder, the Tactics
pitch shows no portraits (logged), as for a CPK it cannot read; it does not skip the missing
one and show the others' portraits.
Why: the game itself rejects the whole `download/` folder when a listed CPK is absent (the Team
compiler warns of it as `dpfilelist_cpk_missing`); portraits taken from the remaining CPKs
would show the tester faces the game will not, and a missing file would hide behind a pitch
that looks right. The first build skipped it, on a premise the review found false.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Tactics editor", "Portraits".

## 2026-10-23 — ruleset_editor — DBC7 is a template while DBC is the editors' test ground
Decision: the Ruleset editor's start page offers DBC7 after the six embedded rulesets of the
4cc, VGL and VTL, until Divegrass Before Christmas ends; Blank is defined field by field in the
plan (one regular tier, rate 75, the universal rules on).
Why: DBC is where members first use the editor (0.0.1); its organizers start from DBC7, and a
manager gets the rules file the Save editor checks with by saving that template, which no other
route offers before the Save editor's "save a copy". The "latest two of each kind" rule would
leave it out as a minor invitational, which is right once the cup is over, not during it.
Plan: `plans/ruleset_editor.md` "The editor" (the start page).

## 2026-10-23 — aatf — logic version 1 is frozen at the 0.0.1 cut
Decision: for logic identity, "the first release" is the 0.0.1 preview: from its cut, a changed
logic is version 2, version 1's hash staying in `LOGIC_VERSIONS`. The older-official path's
scenarios are written with version 2, a file the preview saved as their fixture; Phase 20
builds the path and proves it in `libs/aatf`'s tests.
Why: the preview's Ruleset editor saves files DBC's organizers and managers keep. Freezing only
at 0.1.0 would make each of them *modified* at the next logic edit, so the editor would stop
offering the update and keep their old logic on every save. No file of an older official logic
can exist before then, so a Phase 20 scenario for it would have no real input.
Plan: `plans/aatf_rules.md` "Loading and validation"; `plans/ruleset_editor.md` "Acceptance"
(the paragraph after "Opening and saving").

## 2026-10-23 — ruleset_editor — a file that breaks a load rule is refused at open
Decision: the Ruleset editor refuses a rules file that reads but breaks a load rule (two tiers
sharing an id) the way it refuses a parse or schema error: the findings listed with their key
paths, the forms not opened.
Why: it is the file the Save editor refuses too, so both tools agree on what a rules file is,
and `libs/aatf`'s load already refuses it; opening it in the forms with rail marks would need a
second, unchecked load path for a file only a hand edit produces.
Plan: `plans/ruleset_editor.md` "Opening and saving" (*Unreadable*), RE-FILE-03.

## 2026-10-23 — save_editor — a starter without a shown portrait gets the game's placeholder, bundled
Decision (maintainer): a starter whose portrait the Tactics pitch cannot show, for any reason,
gets the game's own placeholder portrait (`common/render/symbol/blank/player-dummy.png`, three
versions: PES 2015, 2016-2018, 2019-2021), drawn as a portrait, instead of the badge and name
alone. The three PNGs are bundled in `resources/portraits/` and embedded, not read from the
install.
Why: it is what the game draws for a player with no portrait, so the pitch keeps looking like
the game's screen; bundled, it shows with no PES folder set, which is when every portrait is
missing.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Tactics editor" (a marker; "Portraits"); worklog 8.9i.

## 2026-10-23 — studio_core — the shell's icons are a single-colour icon font of our own
Decision (maintainer): the shell's icons become a single-colour icon font built from our own
SVGs (each tool's drawn to say what it does; the general ones copied from Phosphor, MIT),
registered through `FontDefinitions`; `egui-phosphor` leaves the workspace at the egui 0.37
migration, its regular font bundled until ours replaces it. Multi-colour icons wait until after
1.0.0.
Why: `egui-phosphor`'s only tie to egui is a font-registration helper, and it held the egui
0.37 upgrade (no release three weeks on); its stock glyphs ("users three" for the Team
compiler) say little about a tool. A font keeps `icon() -> &'static str` and the text-colour
hover and selection, with no runtime dependency; SVG drawn at run time would add resvg's crates
for colour the pre-1.0 releases do not need.
Plan: `plans/core/README.md` "GUI framework choice: egui", "External Dependencies";
`plans/core/architecture.md`; `plans/core/gui.md`; worklog 8.11, 8.14.

## 2026-10-23 — studio — the version is shown with its release stage, derived from the version
Decision (maintainer's idea; the stages after 0.0.x the lead's, reversible): the shown version
string gains the release stage, `v0.0.1 pre-alpha`: pre-alpha for 0.0.x, alpha from 0.1.0,
none from 1.0.0, derived in one function from the version's major and minor numbers. The
semver carries no pre-release suffix.
Why: the previews and test releases are incomplete by design, and the word tells a member so
where every bug report starts (the status bar's version). Derived rather than written, a
version bump cannot leave a stale stage; a semver suffix would change the release tags and the
updater's comparison for a label. 0.1.0 and on are test releases for a restricted group, which
is what alpha means; a public beta, if any, is a later ruling.
Plan: `plans/core/distribution.md` "Changelog and version display"; worklog 8.13.

## 2026-10-23 — fmdl, pes_model — the algorithms both crates carry stay mirrored, never merged
Decision (maintainer, on the lead's recommendation against a merge): the split, its combine,
the split vertex encoding and the `check` limits stay written once per crate, also when the
algorithm itself changes. Each mirrored file names its twin in its header, a change to one goes
to the other in the same commit, and the duplication check's keep list holds each pair.
Why: the duplication audit found about 400 mirrored lines; the copies differ where the formats
do (weights, bone positions, mesh fields, errors, bone-group sets), so one shared version needs
a new crate and a trait carrying every difference, splitting one algorithm across three files
and giving both crates (and their Python bindings) a new shared dependency. The real risk, a fix
landing in one copy only, happened once (2026-09-28, fmdl's split fixes ported a day later) and
is covered by the header and the keep list at a fraction of the cost.
Plan: `spec/libs/format_crates.md`, "`ops/` are format-native transformations"; worklog issue
"repetition in the code".

## 2026-10-23 — ruleset_editor — an undo snapshot is the ruleset and the logic status together
Decision (lead, where the plan said "whole-ruleset snapshots"): each undo entry holds the
ruleset and the file's logic status; the saved state is one such snapshot, and the document is
dirty when it differs. **Update logic** records a snapshot like any form edit.
Why: Update logic changes the logic, not the ruleset, so a ruleset-only snapshot made its undo
restore an identical ruleset and leave the new logic in place (20.6a1's first delivery, found
in review); a separate dirty flag for the logic could not be undone either.
Plan: `plans/ruleset_editor.md` "The editor", the undo paragraph.

## 2026-10-23 — 0.0.1 — VGL 27's organizer moves to the official DpFileList and compiles in multi-CPK mode
Decision (maintainer): the organizer's PES 2019 install takes the official DpFileList
(`upgrade-dpfl`), and the initial DLC compiles into the `teams` slot run, as many slots as its
size needs (multi-CPK mode: `4cc_41_teams` on, the official list's run counting from 1, the
bins in `4cc_08_bins`). No default changes for the preview.
Why: the 4cc PES 2019 patch's 31-entry list has neither `4cc_99_test` nor the `teams` run, so
a compile with the defaults refused to install (worklog 0.0.1e); the official list is the one
every install is meant to carry, and the league's whole content (3.7 GiB at the rehearsal)
is past one part's 3 GiB cap, which the size split handles. The five CPKs the rehearsal's
upgrade would have dropped (`4cc_03_base`, `4cc_10_scoreboard` and three more) were that
machine's own older 4cc PES 2019 patch (its list dated 2024-01-19), not VGL's: the last VGL
ran on PES 21, so VGL 27's install is set up anew.
Plan: `plans/core/development_plan.md` "The /vg/ League 27 (VGL)"; worklog 0.0.1f.

## 2026-10-23 — 8.11 — The Tactics tab's pitch keeps its width; the lists take the rest
Decision (lead, found by the egui 0.37 migration): the Tactics tab lays the pitch canvas out
at its fixed 320 px and gives the starting eleven and bench lists the rest of the pane,
through two child uis, replacing `ui.columns(2)`.
Why: `ui.columns` halves the pane, and at a narrow window the pitch overflowed its half; egui
then widened the pane's layout bound (856 px in a 792 px window), and the formation settings'
wrapped rows below drew past the window's edge (a test caught it once 0.37's roomier buttons
pushed one over). The draft's `taccols` is a fixed pitch beside flexible lists, so this is the
draft's layout, not a new one.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Tactics editor", "The pitch is the editor".

## 2026-10-23 — 8.9i — A portrait still being read shows the placeholder meanwhile
Decision (lead): while the reading thread has not answered for a starter, his marker draws the
selected game's placeholder portrait, then his portrait once it is decoded.
Why: the maintainer asked for the placeholder wherever the portrait cannot be shown, to get
rid of the empty space above a badge; drawing nothing until the answer lands would keep that
space for the read's duration, then pop the portrait in. The placeholder then the portrait is
one change instead of two.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Tactics editor", "A marker".

## 2026-10-24 — ruleset_editor — A tier's per-stat target is a checkbox and a number; a free-card count of 0 is no entry
Decision (lead): in a tier's expander each ability stat has an "own target" checkbox with its
number beside it; unticked, the stat has no `stats` entry and follows the rate. A group's free
cards set to 0 remove the group's `free` entry.
Why: the draft shows "the rate" as an empty number field, and egui's number field cannot be
empty; a target of 0 cannot stand for "the rate" either, since 0 is a target a ruleset may set.
A free count of 0 and no entry give a player the same cards, so dropping the entry keeps the
written file to what the ruleset sets, as the writer does for every field at its default.
Plan: `plans/ruleset_editor.md` "The editor", the Tiers bullet.

## 2026-10-24 — development plan — The Ruleset editor leaves 0.0.1; the bundle carries DBC7's rules file
Decision: the maintainer's directive: the Ruleset editor is not in the 0.0.1 preview and runs
after Release 0.1.0; for now a working Save editor with a rock-solid AATF check is what matters
most. The Ruleset editor's work in flight (20.6a2a, the Tiers section) is reviewed and landed,
then the phase waits; the build keeps it CLI-only. The lead's follow-up, applied: the 0.0.1
bundle carries DBC7 as an assembled rules file (`rules/dbc7.rhai`) and its settings name it as
the Save editor's `aatf_rules`.
Why: the plan's only route for a DBC manager to get DBC7's rules file was saving the template
in the Ruleset editor; the Save editor's "save a copy" writes the official ruleset only. A file
in the bundle, already selected, gives the window's testers (DBC's managers) the cup's check
with no step of their own; the setting stays a member's to change. Not "save a copy" offering
every embedded ruleset: that is a new control nobody asked for (a `PROPOSALS.md` matter).
Plan: `plans/core/development_plan.md` "Divegrass Before Christmas", "Phase 20";
`plans/ruleset_editor.md` "The editor", the start page paragraph.

## 2026-10-24 — save_editor, studio_core — the rules file's settings row and the quick actions' edges
Decision: the Save editor's settings section is one path row for `aatf_rules` with a Browse
button picking a `.rhai` file, and `studio_core` owns the path row (text edit committing on Enter
or focus loss, plus Browse) for every section, the common folder rows gaining their Browse with
it. The quick actions row sits under the info strip: one Make button per tier, then Set stats
(the Player menu's Set all stats in one click); a rules file that does not load leaves Set stats
and the load error on the row; a failed `apply_tier` changes nothing and shows the refusal
dialog.
Why: the shell draft draws every path row with a Browse button and the 8.6c1 settings menu
left them out only until `rfd` was in the workspace; one row in `studio_core`, not a copy per
tool, so a tool's path row cannot commit differently from the common ones. The error states
follow the Cards left badges' (the error in the controls' place) rather than hiding the row,
which would leave a member with no hint why the tier buttons went.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Settings menu"; `plans/save_editor.md` "Configurable AATF rules"
(the rules file's row, Quick actions), SE-GUI-32.

## 2026-10-24 — ruleset_editor — A tier's id commits on Enter or focus loss; the Tiers numbers draw as stored
Decision: the Tiers table's id field commits on Enter or focus loss, as a settings path row
does, and the commit carries the tier's key in the medal systems from the id it had to the one
committed, only while no other tier carries the old id and no system holds the new one. Every
number in the section draws its value as stored (egui's `clamp_existing_to_range` off), and the
paid and minimum cards run to 48.
Why: the draft renames per keystroke, and an id typed through another tier's id moved that
tier's medal counts (Silver typed to `gold2` passed through `gold`; the keystroke after it moved
Gold's counts to `gold2`, Astra A1 on 20.6a2a); one carry per commit, refused while ambiguous,
cannot. A clamped draw rewrote DBC7's 48 paid cards to 20 on opening the section, marking the
file unsaved; 48 is every card the game has (DBC7's own comment).
Plan: `plans/ruleset_editor.md` "The editor", the Tiers bullet.

## 2026-10-24 — aesthetics_export — `ingame_face.toml` replaces the marker and takes the face, hair and iris keys
Decision: the `ingame_face` marker becomes `ingame_face.toml` (an empty file is the old marker),
holding `iris_color` and the `[face]` and `[hair]` tables that leave `settings.toml`; a player
without it gets the game's default face values. The old spellings are an Error naming the new
file (`ingame_face_marker_renamed`), recognized only to say so; an unparsable file is
`ingame_face_toml_invalid`, the player keeping the in-game face at the defaults. The Export
upgrader fills the file from the record wherever it wrote the marker; the Save editor generates
it through its own action, "Generate in-game face", apart from `settings.toml`.
Why: measured in PES 21 and PES 17 Edit mode (WORKLOG 0.0.1h's `manual: checked` lines): beside a face model
the game draws neither the in-game hair nor the record's iris, so 90 keys did nothing for the 19
players in 20 who wear one, in the file members read first. Moving the iris with them, not
keeping it in `settings.toml`, because both samples drew the model's own eyes whatever it was
set to. One Save editor action for both files was not chosen because the save cannot tell which
players wear the in-game face (the cup keeps every "modified face" flag off), and a generated
`ingame_face.toml` beside a face model drops the folder (`ingame_face_explicit_face_model`). The
old marker is refused rather than read as an empty file because the compiler stays strict: the
upgrader carries Red's marker over, and the change lands before members write Studio exports by
hand (0.0.1).
Plan: `plans/aesthetics_export/player_folders.md` "`ingame_face.toml` (new; step 0.0.1h)", with
pointers in its `settings_toml.md` and `object_model.md` and in `plans/save_editor.md`'s
`settings.toml` generation bullet.

## 2026-10-24 — save_editor — the AATF panel's current team, jump, recheck and rules file
Decision: the floating AATF panel opens from a Panels menu and the quick actions' "AATF…", as
the draft shows; Current team is the selector's team, or with ALL the selected player's team; a
click on a row selects the player and switches the selector to his team unless it is at ALL;
the teams are re-checked on a save, team-pick or rules-file change, the previous result shown
as checking meanwhile, on a worker; Validate rules runs on the active rules file, and Save a
copy writes the file `Rules::official()` loads, under its file name.
Why: the selected player's team, not the draft's first team, because the panel checks what the
strip and tabs are editing, as Live AATF already reads ALL; switching the selector, because a
selected player the list does not show is a selection the member cannot see; validating the
active file, not a second file chosen in the panel, because two file choices would let the
panel validate one file and check with another; the assembled file, not the data block alone,
because the data block does not load as a rules file.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Configurable AATF rules", the AATF panel, Validate rules and
"save a copy" bullets.

## 2026-10-24 — save_editor — The comparator's direction, Export's scope and where the tabs' terms live
Decision: the picked save is the `diff` report's first and the open save its second; Export
writes the report of the toggled scope over the whole save (`save-editor diff <picked> <open>`
with `--gameplay` or `--aesthetics`, All neither), the team filter narrowing the screen only;
the tabs' terms are read from the tabs' own label and transform tables.
Why: picked → open, not the reverse, because a member compares his edited save against a
reference and reads a row as what his edits changed (the draft's direction); the whole save's
report, not the rows shown as the draft exported them, because the plan and SE-GUI-13 ask for
the CLI's text and the command has no team filter, so a filtered Export could not be checked
against it; the tabs' tables, not a second one for the panel, because two label tables drift.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Comparator (gameplay + aesthetics)".

## 2026-10-24 — save_editor — The comparator's groups, its worker and a kept pick
Decision: the comparator's rows of the players both saves hold group per team, a player
under the first team in the open save's order whose roster holds him (`No team` when none does), the players only in one save
last under `Only in the picked save` and `Only in the open save`; the comparison runs on a
worker thread with the held list marked `Comparing…`, a frame drawing only the rows in view;
another save opened keeps the pick and compares it again.
Why: one group per player, not one per roster, because a player on a club and a national team
would read twice (the Strip again list already names a player's first team); a worker because
two real PES 2021 saves differ in 34,379 rows and the command takes about half a second, a
hitch after every edit on the UI thread; the pick kept because a member compares several saves
against one reference, and the version check runs again on the new save.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Comparator (gameplay + aesthetics)".

## 2026-10-24 — save_editor — The second draft arrangement is the base
Decision: `docs/prototypes/save_editor_v2.html` is the Save editor's draft; the built tabs of
8.9's slices 1-3, which follow the first draft, are ported to it as a step of their own (8.9f
slice 4), and the maintainer's fine tweaks land on it.
Why: the maintainer's ruling ("V2 is a much better base"): it fixes the first draft's badly
arranged elements (the team's name in view on every tab, the positions grid in the
collaborator's order, the cutscene-only stats outside Appearance's lock); the panels are the same in both,
so the AATF and comparator work goes on unchanged.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Build order and verification" (the draft paragraph).

## 2026-10-24 — save_editor — The comparator's groups in the open save's team order
Decision: the comparator draws one group per team, in the open save's team order, each
group's players in the report's order, `No team` after the teams and before the only-in
sections.
Why: a heading at each change of team along the report's order (the picked save's record
order) heads a team once per run of its players, and a real save's teams hold player ids far
apart, so one team's rows would be scattered under many headings; the team selector's order is
the one a member reads the teams in everywhere else.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Comparator (gameplay + aesthetics)".

## 2026-10-24 — save_editor — Porting the built tabs to the second draft, in five slices
Decision: 8.9f slice 4 ports the built tabs to `save_editor_v2.html` in five slices, each its
own commit and review: (a) the frame: the team bar above every tab, the tab strip in Player /
Team groups, the player header on the Player tabs only, the quick actions into Abilities' top
row; (b) Abilities' top row and stats columns, with star and playing attitude moved to
Appearance's Cutscenes group; (c) Appearance's aligned groups and Tactics in three columns; (d)
the one cards badge, through a tier recognition `libs/aatf` exposes; (e) the regular-weight
body font, the shell's.
Why: each slice stays one review's size; (d) adds a `pub` API to the crate the 0.0.1 work wants
rock-solid, so it lands alone with its own checkpoint (b) review; (e) changes every tool's
text, not the Save editor's, and adds a bundled font file.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Editing UI", SE-GUI-01, 06, 07, 10, 32.

## 2026-10-24 — save_editor — The player header's two rows, two grids
Decision: the player header draws v2's two rows (Name, Shirt, Number, Captain; ID, Nation, Age,
Height, Weight) as one grid per row, each label in its own cell, not as one grid whose columns
both rows share; the Name and Shirt fields take the draft's 190 and 110 points, not the first
slice's 240 and 140.
Why: the header must fit the 877-point pane of the shell's smallest default window. An egui
grid unions each column's width across its rows, so in one grid the Name field's width widens
row 2's ID column and Height and Weight are cut off; at 240 and 140, row 1 alone (Number and
Captain now beside Name and Shirt) widens the tab's content past that pane (measured in 8.9f
slice 4a: a checkbox below it ended at 908).
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Editing UI", the player header bullet.

## 2026-10-24 — save_editor — Rows picked by width, and stats columns that shrink before they clip
Decision: the team bar and the Abilities tab's top row pick their arrangement from the pane's
width against a constant (the one-row width, measured once with the default font): the bar one
row, else the names row over the colours row; the top row's three blocks (Profile, Playable
positions, Quick actions) on one line, else Profile over the other two. A pair or a block is
never split. The ability stats take four columns, fewer when the pane cannot hold four, filled
column by column.
Why: egui's wrapped row breaks between single widgets, so it split Colour 2's hex from its
swatch at 1037 x 648, and a nested horizontal or vertical claims the line's whole rest and
never wraps (tried at 8.9f4a: the bar stopped wrapping and widened the tab past the 877-point
pane). Wrapping units by their measured widths failed twice in 8.9f4b: a unit boxed at its
remembered width re-fits its grids to the box and needed more egui passes than the default, set
globally from a Save editor helper; lines grouped by the previous frame's widths settled over
several passes and drove the scroll area's offset negative, hiding the tab's labels. A width
constant needs no measurement and no extra pass, as `pairs_per_row` already does in this crate;
a wrong estimate wraps a little early or late, never splits a unit. Four fixed columns of stats
would clip on the smallest default window's pane if the labels outgrow it, where the old row
fill wrapped.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Editing UI", the team bar bullet and the Abilities & Skills bullet.

## 2026-10-24 — save_editor — The draft's pair counts as caps, and the Tactics settings column below on a narrow pane
Decision: Appearance's grids take the draft's pairs per row as a cap, fewer where the pane
cannot hold them: physique two, the strip style's ids, enums and checkboxes four, the motions
four (the draft's 4 / 4 / 2); the strip's wrist-taping, spectacles and player-gloves rows are a
grid of their own, label and contents. The Tactics tab's formation settings take up to two
pairs per row, one where the settings column cannot hold two; the settings column sits beside
the pitch and the lists where the pane holds it at the draft's 360 points, else whole below
them.
Why: the ability stats' rule (the entry above): a fixed count clips the smallest default
window's pane where the old row fill wrapped. An egui grid has no column span, so the draft's
colspan rows inside the strip's table would widen one field column to a palette's width and
push the table off the pane; a separate grid keeps their labels aligned among themselves, not
with the table's first column, which would need the table's width from a previous frame.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Editing UI", the Appearance bullet; "Tactics editor", the
three-columns sentence.

## 2026-10-25 — gui — Studio opens at 1280 × 800 points
Decision: the window's default is 1280 × 800 points (16:10), replacing 1440 × 900; the 90% fit
on a smaller monitor stays, so the smallest default a member meets is still 1037 × 648 (a
1080p monitor at 150%). The Tactics tab's lists narrow from 240 to 200 points, so its three
columns (the pitch 320, the lists, the settings 360, two gaps: 896) fit the 904-point tab area
this window leaves; their names are cut at the column's edge, the full name on hover.
Why: the maintainer, seeing 1440 × 900 on the desktop monitor rather than over remote
desktop, found it too large; the reference editor opens at 1248 × 640. At 240 the lists would
need 936 points and push the settings below the pitch at the new default.

ST-WIN-01, ST-HELP-05; `plans/save_editor.md` "Tactics editor".

## 2026-10-25 — gui — The drafts are one host page and a script per tool
Decision: `docs/prototypes/index.html` holds the simulated window, the shell's elements, the
shared stylesheet and the drawing helpers once; each tool's draft is `tools/<tool>.js`, a script
the host loads with a `<script>` tag that registers the tool and draws only its view, its
images under `assets/`; `scripts/bundle_drafts.py` inlines everything into one HTML file when a
draft must travel as an attachment. Replaces one self-contained file per tool.
Why: the maintainer's request: easy prototyping comes before a single attachment now that the
GUI is being built; the window size, the sidebar and the theme were copied into every draft
and changed in each. Not an HTML page per tool fetched by the host (a page opened from disk
cannot fetch another file), and not an iframe (it would hold a tool's menus and dialogs inside
the tool area, where egui's span the window).
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Prototypes before implementation".

## 2026-10-25 — gui — The drafts' host gets a layout edit toggle
Decision: the host page's draft controls carry a "Layout edit" toggle: every panel a tool
script names with `data-panel` can be moved (an offset that pushes nothing) and resized (its
neighbours reflow), and "Copy layout" copies one line per changed panel, with the tool, screen,
window size, zoom and each panel's rectangle before and after, for the maintainer to paste to
the lead; the tweaks persist across reloads until "Reset". Built once in the host, so every
tool's draft has it.
Why: the maintainer's request: tuning an arrangement by hand and pasting the result is faster
and less ambiguous than describing it in words. The string is evidence, not a layout file
the views load, because the views lay out by width rules rather than coordinates: the lead
turns a tweak into constants and rules, and reports one no rule expresses instead of placing
panels by coordinates.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Prototypes before implementation" ("Layout edit").

## 2026-10-25 — gui — The drafts' host gets remarks, links, longest values, the app's font, an overlay and draft shots
Decision: the six review aids of `plans/core/gui.md` "Prototypes before implementation" ("The
host's other review aids"), proposed as P26-P31 and accepted by the maintainer: remarks pinned
to an element with "Copy remarks"; the tool, screen and draft state in the URL's fragment;
a "Longest values" control fed by `assets/longest.json`; the app's bundled fonts by
`@font-face`; an overlay of the built window's capture; `scripts/draft_shots.py` listing the
screens a host edit changed. Each lives in the host, so every tool's draft gets it once.
Why: remarks in prose and screens reached by described clicks cost the lead guesses and
repeated work; short sample names and the browser's font hide clipping the app then shows
(the Tactics combos at the default window); two captures compared by eye miss small shifts;
a shared host changes every draft at once, and only the tool being worked on is looked at.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Prototypes before implementation"; worklog 8.19, 8.20, 8.21.

Decision: at the default window the Tactics tab keeps its three columns, and the settings

## 2026-10-25 — aesthetics_export, team_compiler — Edits made in PES come back to the export
Decision: PES stays the previewer for the motions and the in-game face; Studio finds the edits
a member made in Edit mode by comparing the save with a compile record the compiler leaves
beside its aesthetics patch (each compiled player's resolved keys and the save's fingerprint),
at start, when the tools' views open, before every compile and on the save's change, so edits
made while Studio was not running are found too; it brings them into `settings.toml` and
`ingame_face.toml` on one click, and writes the save (the re-strip of restored ids, a pending
patch) only once PES is closed. Replaces P15's Part B (a skipped save step applied when PES
closes), which it contains; P15's Part A (two findings opening the Save editor at their fix)
is accepted as proposed.
Why: the maintainer's ruling, with "Studio picks up the changes even if it was not running"
first. A previewer outside PES (the motions, the face) is a research project whose result
would still be judged against the game; the round trip costs a record, a comparison and a
notice. Watching for the write alone would miss edits made with Studio closed, and PES writes
the save only on leaving Edit mode, from its memory, so a write by Studio while it runs is lost.
Plan: `plans/aesthetics_export/settings_toml.md` ("Edits made in PES come back to the export");
worklog 8.23.

layer over the view's left edge, which closes when the pointer leaves it unless one of its
popups is open. The collapse button and its state go.

only for a moment, and reserving their width cost every tool about 104 points all the time
(a tab's area at the default window grows from 904 to about 1008). The view is never pushed
or resized by the overlay, so nothing under the pointer moves while it opens.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Sidebar" (item 4), ST-SIDE-02; worklog 8.25.

Decision: the tool icons, the help `?` and the settings gear are drawn at 24 points, on the

## 2026-10-25 — tooling — The test gate runs four test binaries at once, and a changed-packages mode exists
Decision: `just test` builds the workspace's tests once (`cargo test --workspace --no-run`) and
runs the test binaries four at once, each whole, through the same per-process memory-cap wrapper
`cargo test` uses on Windows, then the doc-tests (`scripts/run_tests.py`). `just gates-changed
[base]` runs the gates with the test gate over the packages changed since `base` and their
dependents; every commit still runs the full `just gates`.
Why: the maintainer asked to shorten the gates as tools are added. Measured in a worktree at
8e67928d under the side-leads' load: `cargo test --workspace` 371-373 s, `cargo nextest` 391-500 s
(a process and a Python wrapper per test), the binaries four at once 176 s against 277 s for
`cargo test` right after (eight at once 180 s: the cores are full). Building with `--workspace`
before selecting keeps every binary's features the gates' (a `-p` build lacks egui's fonts).
Plan: `CONTRIBUTING.md` "Testing and verification".

## 2026-10-25 — gui — The body font is Ubuntu Regular, bundled; every view test draws with the app's fonts
Decision: the suite's body text is the Ubuntu family's regular weight, 0.83, bundled as
`resources/fonts/Ubuntu-Regular.ttf` (the Google Fonts copy, Ubuntu Font Licence 1.0 beside it)
and first in the proportional family, replacing egui's built-in `Ubuntu-Light`; the icon font
stays second. `theme::install_fonts` becomes public and is the one font set the window and
every view test's context install, `team_widgets` reaching it through a dev-dependency on
`studio_core`.
Why: the second Save editor draft, the GUI's base, is drawn at weight 400, and egui ships only
the light weight. A test context left on egui's defaults measured different text per build: a
lone `cargo test -p team_widgets` (and its mutation runs) has no fonts at all, since egui's
`default_fonts` arrives only through eframe, so every glyph was a 9-point box. A copy of
`install_fonts` in `team_widgets` would drift from the window's; the dev-dependency adds no
cycle (`studio_core` depends on no widget lib) and builds nothing the workspace does not build
already.

## 2026-10-25 — save_editor — The aesthetics transplant writes the team's export, after 0.1.0; the save-to-save transplant goes
Decision: the transplant copies a donor save's team's looks into that team's own export (each
checked roster slot's player folder, `settings.toml` and `ingame_face.toml` updated in place,
created if missing, a preview first, the whole run refused when the export or a slot's folder is
missing), picked by team name and roster-slot checkboxes, never ids; cross-team copies are out of
scope; it is built after Release 0.1.0. The save-writing transplant (the panel committed as
8.9j5a, the CLI `transplant` command, `pes_savefile`'s operation) is removed.
Why: the maintainer's ruling: aesthetics live in the exports now, so a look written into a save is
overwritten by the next compile or not read at all on a stripped Fox save; the one use left for a
save-to-save copy, a team with no export, is served by generating the export from the save. Roster
slots, not shirt numbers or ids, because the slot names the player's folder and shirt numbers are
free text. Out of 0.0.1 and 0.1.0 because neither cup needs it.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Aesthetics transplant", "Read-only aesthetics", SE-GUI-14.

## 2026-10-25 — aatf — The player's own tier is a fourth logic function
Decision: the logic gains `player_tier(player, team)`, returning the id of the tier
`check_team` reads the player as (the team's height system, then recognition) or `()`, and
`Rules::player_tier(&TeamView, &PlayerView) -> Result<Option<&Tier>, CheckError>` calls it;
`Rules::load` requires it with two parameters. Behind the Save editor's one cards badge
(8.9f4d).
Why: the badge must read the tier "as `check-aatf` recognizes it", and only the file's logic
does that: a recognition in Rust would copy `read_player` (recognition before choices, the
height system by quotas, a special moving a threshold) and drift from it, and would ignore a
file's own logic. `check_team`'s violations carry no tier, so the host cannot read one from
them. Required rather than optional, because a file without it would leave the badge with
nothing to show; added now, since logic version 1 freezes at the 0.0.1 cut and no released
file exists yet.
Plan: `plans/aatf_rules.md` "The interpreter", "The player's own tier".

## 2026-10-25 — export_upgrader — The view's arguments and report, where the plan was silent
Decision: in the Export upgrader's view, the loose switch on disables the savefile field and

discovered save until the member edits or picks one; after Move to exports and compile the

## 2026-10-25 — save_editor — Generate settings.toml and Generate in-game face: a picked folder, an update in place, a whole face file
Decision: the two Player-menu actions each open a dialog on the selected player: the player
folder typed or picked (never prefilled), the file's text as Write will put it down, Write
enabled only for an existing folder. An existing `settings.toml` is updated in place through
`update_toml` (its comments and layout kept) and one that does not parse is shown as the error
with Write disabled; `ingame_face.toml` is written whole. The success line is the shell's notice
(the tool's first; `SaveView.notice`, forwarded by `Tool::view`).
Why: the plan was silent (0.0.1h slice 3). A prefilled path would be a guess: the save knows no
export or folder name. Updating keeps what a member wrote into a file the project documents with
comments; a file that does not parse may be the member's half-done edit, so it is shown, not
overwritten. The face file holds only values the record supplies and the template's comments, so
replacing it loses nothing of the member's.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Interchange formats in the UI", the `settings.toml` generation bullet.

Decision: the Save editor edits a player's aesthetics as 4ccEditor did, with no ownership line and

## 2026-10-25 — all tools — Text a member reads flows naturally, and every existing line is swept once
Decision: CONTRIBUTING's rule for text a member reads gains a second bullet: the text flows as a
person would say it (whole sentences in ordinary word order, causes joined with because, so or
although, no code shorthand such as "gating" or "targets"), with the maintainer's example pair.
Every member-facing line already written (the view strings, tooltips and notices, the message
catalogs, the help chapters, the injected TOML comments, the CLI's output, and the drafts) is

("This save is PES 17; the selector targets PES 2019. ..."); a member rereads such a line and

reads), and the sweep is a worklog step.

## 2026-10-25 — save_editor — A failed tier check shows its error in the Cards left badge's place
Decision: when the active rules file loads but `player_tier` or `card_limits` fails on the

rules could not read this player: <error>" where the badge stands, as it already does a file that

Decision: the native window gets a minimum inner size of 960 × 600 points; worklog step 8.9h

320-point pitch beside its 200-point lists); the tab strip clips below 738. Every default the
window opens at is 1037 × 648 or larger, which the plan already names as the size views are laid
out for; wrapping each fixed-part row would rework four layouts for sizes no default reaches,
while the minimum costs one builder call and still fits the smallest default with room.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Shell layout", the paragraph "The window's size."; ST-WIN-01.

## 2026-10-25 — aatf — `read_player`'s speed rewrite lands before logic version 1 freezes
Decision: the rewrite of `logic.rhai`'s `read_player` that copies less (one card summary per
choice, the specials' conditions read once per player) is done before the 0.0.1 cut freezes
logic version 1's hash, not after it.
Why: the maintainer's ruling, on the lead's recommendation. After the freeze the same
speedup changes the hash, so it would be logic version 2, and the bundle would keep two logic
copies that differ only in speed; before it, the change is still version 1 and costs only the
fixtures' violations staying identical, which the rewrite must prove anyway.
Plan: `plans/aatf_rules.md` "Loading and validation", its last paragraph.

## 2026-10-25 — studio_core — The update check's settings rows wait for the updater
Decision: the settings menu does not draw "Check for updates" and "Check interval (hours)"
until the release whose updater reads them (Release 0.2.0, `core/distribution.md` step 1); the
two keys stay in the settings file with their defaults.
Why: found by the default-settings audit before 0.0.1 (worklog 0.0.1j): no code reads either
key, and 0.0.1 and 0.1.0 ship no updater, so a member who switches the check off, or on,
changes nothing while the row says it does. Dropping the keys instead would lose them from the
file and re-add them at 0.2.0 for no gain.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Settings menu", the Common settings bullet.

## 2026-10-25 — save_editor, team_compiler — A save is written while its game runs once Edit mode is closed
Decision: the Save editor's Save no longer refuses while the save's own PES runs: it asks the
member to make sure the game's Edit mode is closed, then writes; Edit mode's Load reads the
file in. The CLI's writing commands, which cannot ask, write only with `--edit-mode-closed`
and otherwise refuse naming the flag; the Team compiler's savefile step takes the same flag and
otherwise skips as before, its warning naming the flag.
Why: the maintainer's ruling for the window: the refusal rested on the belief that the game
writes its save back on exit, but PES writes it when the member leaves Edit mode, and Edit
mode's Load reloads an edited save
without a restart, so refusing made a member close the game for every edit. The CLI and the
compiler follow the one rule (two tools guarding the same file keep one rule); a flag rather
than a warning after the write, because a write made while Edit mode is open would be lost
without a word. The flag is the lead's choice for the two commands, open to the maintainer's
reversal.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Writing a save while its game runs", SE-GUI-21, SE-CLI-03;
`plans/team_compiler/pipeline.md` "6. Post-processing", the bullet "Savefile step while the
game runs"; TC-SAV-17.

## 2026-10-25 — studio — 0.0.1 opens no console window, and keeps a diagnostic log
Decision: the 0.0.1 preview's exe is built for the Windows GUI subsystem, calling
`AttachConsole(ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS)` (an `unsafe` Windows call, approved) when given command
arguments so their output reaches the terminal or launcher that started it; and the window's
`studio.log` with its panic hook lands in the same release. No console-subsystem shim is
shipped, then or later: the bundle keeps one exe, and no command reads the keyboard (an answer
is a flag).
Why: the maintainer wants no console beside the window in the preview. Without a console a
panic's message would go nowhere, so the log that catches it comes with the change. A second
exe would confuse members who only double-click, and the command line is second-class to the
window (the maintainer); the cost of going without is small, since the launchers are batch
files, which wait for the exe and see its exit code, and a command typed at an interactive
prompt only prints after the prompt returns.
Plan: `plans/core/development_plan.md` "Divegrass Before Christmas", `plans/core/
architecture.md` "Windows subsystem" and "Diagnostic logging"; ST-RUN-04.

## 2026-10-26 — studio — The window's log: no file on a first run, a dialog for the panic that ends the window
Decision: `studio.log` logs at `info` with no level switch, flushing each line; a first run,
which has no data location until its dialog's choice, writes no log; the panic hook logs every
panic, and the dialog naming the file and repeating the panic's message shows only for the
panic that ends the window, caught around the GUI run, after which the process exits with 101.
Why: a double-click passes no `-v`; a log written outside the chosen location would leave a
folder the portable choice promised not to; a panic on another thread may be recovered (the
GPU encoder's falls back to the CPU encoder), and the hook cannot tell, so a dialog there could
ask for a report of a run that went fine. 101 is the code an unguarded panic exits with.
Plan: `plans/core/architecture.md` "Diagnostic logging"; ST-RUN-07, ST-RUN-08.

## 2026-10-26 — studio — Every Windows build is GUI-subsystem; the window mode's startup failures show in a dialog
Decision: debug builds take `windows_subsystem = "windows"` as releases do; and the window
mode's two printed failures (the settings file that does not load, the window that cannot
open) show in a message dialog with the same text and exit code.
Why: with the subsystem on releases only, no gate would run a GUI-subsystem binary, and a
redirected command losing its output would first show in the bundle; the gates' CLI tests run
the debug binary with piped output, so they test what ships. A double-clicked window has no
console to attach to, so a printed failure would reach nobody. Development loses the console
beside the window, which `studio.log` replaces.
Plan: `plans/core/architecture.md` "Windows subsystem", its second paragraph.

## 2026-10-26 — studio — The log's backtrace is offsets; the release's symbols stay out of the bundle
Decision: the panic hook writes each backtrace frame as its module base and offset (the
`backtrace` crate, a new dependency), the release recipe keeps the exe and its `.pdb` beside
the archive as `-symbols.7z` and never in the bundle, the release profile builds with
`debug = "line-tables-only"`, and `scripts/symbolize_log.py` names a posted log's frames
through `llvm-symbolizer`.
Why: a release exe names its frames only with its `.pdb` beside it (measured on a probe crate:
every frame `<unknown>` without it), shipping it costs every member's download 3.8 MB for a
file only the maintainer reads, and appending it to the exe also has the crash write 17 MB and
point the backtrace at it at run time. Offsets plus the kept `.pdb` name function, file and
line (the probe's offsets, run without its `.pdb`, symbolized to
`bt_probe::main::closure$0 at src\main.rs:12`), and line tables grew the probe's `.pdb` alone.
No crate does better at this size: `human-panic` and `crashlog` print resolved names, which the
missing `.pdb` blanks; Embark's minidump crates cover native crashes too, at the cost of a
monitor process (PROPOSALS P38). The maintainer chose this among the three options.
Plan: `plans/core/architecture.md` "Diagnostic logging"; `plans/core/distribution.md`, the
release recipe's paragraph.

## 2026-10-26 — studio — The next start reports a session that did not close normally
Decision: the window's log ends with a closing line on a normal close and after a crash's
dialog; at the next start a previous log without one shows a dialog, before the window,
naming `studio.old.log` and asking for it if the session crashed, in neutral words.
Why: the maintainer asked for a popup when or after a crash; the panic hook's dialog misses
a stack overflow, a failed allocation and a native crash, which a closing line catches with no
monitor process. Neutral words, chosen by the maintainer over a boot-time check that would
miss a crash followed by a restart: winit 0.30.13 and eframe 0.37 handle neither
`WM_QUERYENDSESSION` nor `WM_ENDSESSION` (their sources hold neither), so a Windows shutdown
with the window open also ends without the line.
Plan: `plans/core/architecture.md` "Diagnostic logging"; ST-RUN-09.

## 2026-10-26 — studio_core — The window keeps 1280 wide, scales down under it, and special tools keep their own size
Decision: the first frame fits only the window's height (to 90% of the monitor's), keeping
1280 points wide wherever the window fits; under a tool's design width (1280 for the main
tools) the shell scales the whole UI down with the width, and at or above it, and at any
height, the views reflow at scale 1. The main tools share one window size; a special tool
(today only the Music player) declares its own, and switching between the two classes
restores each class's last size and position for the session.
Why: the maintainer's UI review: 1280 × 720 screens are rare now, so the 16:10 fit that
shrank the width too is dropped; a horizontal shrink should keep the elements' arrangement and
shrink them, a vertical one or any growth keep their size and reflow; the music player must be
compact beside the PES window while streaming, while the other tools need room. Scaling on the
width alone because the views' fixed-width rows are what clips, while height only needs a
scroll. The size classes wait for the Music player's view, their first special tool.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Shell layout" ("The window's size", "Scaling with the width",
"Window size classes"), ST-WIN-01 to 03; `plans/core/architecture.md` "Tool plugin interface";
`plans/music_player.md` "GUI view".

## 2026-10-26 — save_editor — The version warning offers the switch and a close
Decision: the warning shown when a save's version differs from the sidebar's selector carries
"Switch to PES 20xx" (the selector's own change, blockers included) and a close button that
hides it until another save opens.
Why: the maintainer's UI review asked for either action on the warning. The switch is never
made on open, since the selector also sets what the other tools target.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Editing UI", the bullet starting "A save of another version";
SE-GUI-28.

## 2026-10-26 — drafts — Layout edit pins a moved panel; a columned panel narrows into fewer columns
Decision: a moved panel is pinned at its dropped position in window points, its slot kept, so
no neighbour's resize moves it; a panel laid out in columns can be narrowed past its columns
and reflows into fewer; the simulated window scales under the design width as Studio does.
Why: the maintainer's review: resizing `profile` moved the quick-actions panel after it had
been moved elsewhere (the move was an offset from the layout's position), and a columned
panel stopped at its widest row.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Layout edit", the "Size:" bullet.

## 2026-10-26 — export_upgrader, team_compiler, color_tools, core, save_editor — Usability proposals P17-P24 and P32-P38 accepted
Decision: the maintainer accepted P17-P24 and P32-P36 of `PROPOSALS.md` as proposed, with
these changes. P19's Warning becomes a dialog before a loose upgrade, saying the save is where
the players' looks live and holding its Upgrade button until the member ticks that they
understand the loss; the CLI asks nothing, `--loose` being the opt-in already. P24 remembers
both window size classes' places across runs, in two settings the shell writes (not eframe's
`persistence`, which writes its own file outside the data location and knows one size), a
place on no monitor dropped for the fit. P38 is accepted on a measured condition: its three
crates go in only while the release exe grows by at most 10 MB with them. P20's several
exports refuse one export alone for its own missing path or a save lacking its team, the
whole run for an argument shared by all.
Why: each spares a member a step or a lost team the proposals name (`PROPOSALS.md` as of
2026-10-26, now removed from it); a loose upgrade loses every player's look silently, which a
tooltip and a kept Warning would not stop; a window brought back onto an unplugged monitor
would open out of reach.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` "What it does" (P17), "CLI" (P18, P20, P21), "GUI" (P18's
pair, P19, P32-P36), "Message catalog"; `plans/team_compiler/messages.md` "Message structure"
(P22); `plans/libs/color_tools.md` "Color-picker widget" (P23); `plans/core/gui.md` "Window size
classes", ST-WIN-04 (P24); `plans/core/architecture.md` "Diagnostic logging", `plans/core/gui.md`
ST-RUN-10 (P38).

## 2026-10-26 — team_compiler — Red's settings are not imported on first run (P16 vetoed)
Decision: no first-run import of Red's `settings.ini`. Why: only the PES folder would be worth
carrying, and picking it again is easier than picking Red's folder. Plan: no plan edit needed.

## 2026-10-26 — save_editor — Live AATF stays off by default (P37 vetoed); its toggle and marks become visible
Decision: Live AATF stays off by default. Its toolbar toggle is drawn as a framed button with

Error-severity violation) or a check mark, and the field a selected player's violation is about
gets a cross whose tooltip is the AATF panel's line for it (one kind-to-field match, the kinds
about no single field marking the list alone).
Why: the maintainer's ruling: the docked panel takes room, and the editor is also used to build
teams before making them legal; but the toggle read as a label, and a manager should see what

code counts them.

## 2026-10-26 — core — A folder per PES version (P25 accepted, with an override per version)
Decision: the PES folder stays one main row whose Browse stores a picked folder ending in the
selected version's year with `**` in its place; a view-only toggle, A folder per version,
shows one row per version, a filled row overriding the main row for that version
(`[common.pes_folders]`), an empty one falling back to it; the toggle stays on while any
override exists. Fix PES path writes the running version's own row when it has one.
Why: the maintainer's ruling, choosing both over the lead's one-row-per-selected-version
alternative: the `**` rule serves installs sharing a pattern in one pick, the overrides those
that do not; a toggle a member could switch off over a filled row would hide the folder in use.
