## 2026-10-26 — export_upgrader — `--coverage` does not overrule a tag the old name already holds
Decision: an old name whose second word is already `Full` or `Midcup` keeps it (the built
naming rule), reported with source `name`; `--coverage` naming the other tag is refused
(exit 2), the same tag accepted. A removal of a leftover staging folder that fails aborts as
before (exit 3).
Why: the plan was silent on a flag against a tag the member wrote; renaming that word under
them would surprise more than a refusal naming it. A staging folder that will not go is held
open, most likely by a second upgrade of the same export running at that moment, and only
that run can lose by the abort.
Plan: `plans/export_upgrader.md` "CLI", the first and third additions.

## 2026-10-26 — studio_core — the zoom factor is the shell's alone: egui's keyboard zoom off
Decision: with the width scaling (0.0.1m), egui's keyboard zoom (Ctrl with plus, minus or 0)
is turned off; the shell sets the zoom from the window's width and nothing else does.
Why: the plan was silent on the keyboard zoom egui enables by default. The width rule sets the
zoom every frame, so a keyboard zoom would last one frame; folding it into the rule (a member's
factor times the width's) adds a setting nobody asked for, and the system's display scaling
already gives a member larger text, which points follow.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Shell layout", the paragraph "Scaling with the width".

## 2026-10-26 — core — correction: Fix PES path writes an override row whenever any exists
Decision: "A folder per PES version" (above) said Fix PES path writes the running version's
row "when it has one"; the rule is whenever any override exists, the running version's row
then gaining the folder, else the main row as before.
Why: a member keeping folders per version would otherwise see the main row rewritten, moving
every version that falls back to it; the plan text was refined in review and the entry not.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Settings menu", the "PES folder" bullet; ST-SET-04.

## 2026-10-26 — save_editor — `aatf_violation` names `RosterOrder`'s two players
Decision: the `player` context field (id, name and shirt number) is printed for `RosterOrder`
too, in place of the rule's own `player` field holding the same id, and `expected` gains the

Why: the code skips the context field for `RosterOrder` because the rule's field repeats the
id; with the name and number added it no longer repeats, and `RosterOrder` is the violation
whose fix needs both players found, so two bare ids would be its worst line.

## 2026-10-26 — save_editor — The view drops its tabs: a team row per team, the player's fields in three columns
Decision: the Save editor's view is the third draft's (step 0.0.1s1, approved by the
maintainer): a team row heads each team's players and selects the team view (its name, short

in the second, Ability stats in the third, and Appearance a section closed by default; the

Why: tabs split one player's fields over pages a member flicked between to check a build, and
the page not shown hid what an edit depended on (the card budget counts the extra A ratings);
a team bar above every tab took a row from every player for what a team row gives one click

program needs to be as usable as possible before it's unveiled").
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Editing UI" rewritten, the other sections' tab wording, "Build

SE-GUI-37 added.

## 2026-10-26 — save_editor — Name and Shirt count against their limits; 4ccEditor's Edited/created checkbox is not kept
Decision: the Name and Shirt labels carry an `nn/NN` count that follows the field as typed (the

Decision: the list's team row is drawn over the theme's faint fill with its name in the strong

## 2026-10-26 — save_editor — The quick actions' columns take their content's width when it fits

## 2026-10-26 — save_editor — Live AATF's marks: where they sit and their glyphs
Decision: a list row's mark sits at the row's right end after its unsaved-changes dot, a cross

Decision: the maintainer asked for the field labels in the checkboxes' lighter grey, the counts

## 2026-10-26 — aatf — A rules file a member handles ends in `.4ccrules`
Decision (the maintainer's proposal, with the lead's scope): the rules file a member or an
organizer handles is `<name>.4ccrules`: the bundle's `rules/dbc7.4ccrules`, the only ending
every picker offers, the name Save a copy suggests, the CLI's examples. The content stays
plain Rhai, its first line saying so; the loader ignores the ending; the repository's sources
in `libs/aatf` keep `.rhai`.
Why: a member only loads the file, and `.rhai` tells them nothing, where `.4ccrules` names it
and sits beside the suite's `.4ccm`; the pickers offer no `.rhai` beside it since no Studio
has shipped and no such file exists outside the repository. The sources stay `.rhai` because
they are code, edited with an editor's Rhai highlighting, which the first line also points an
organizer's editor at. `.4ccrules` rather than `.aatf`: the file drives the quick actions'
tiers and the card limits as well as the check, and the prefix ties it to the suite.
Plan: `plans/aatf_rules.md` "The rules file" (new); `plans/save_editor.md` the rules file's
row and SE-GUI-15; `plans/ruleset_editor.md` "CLI", RE-FILE-05, RE-CLI-04;
`plans/core/development_plan.md` "Divegrass Before Christmas".

## 2026-10-26 — music_player — a button owns every sound it starts; hand-offs run in `tick()`
Decision: each soundboard button holds one playback state (stopped, playing, fading out) and
every sound it starts; a warcry's hand-off, song end and `advance` are transitions of that
state taken in `tick()`, and a warcry hands off only while its button is still playing it.
Why: a streamer reported that in Rigdio, turning a goalhorn button off at the moment its
warcry ends leaves the goalhorn playing for good: its end-checker thread starts the horn
while the GUI thread's pause clears the button's only reference to it. The plan's frame-driven
engine removes the threads, but an end check reading the sound's state rather than the
button's would still start the horn after the press (a warcry ending during the press's
fade-out), so the rule is the button's state, not the threading.
Plan: `plans/music_player.md` "Playback behavior" (the "A button owns what it plays" bullet)
and "Testing" (the button-state line).

## 2026-10-26 — studio_core — eframe 0.37 gives the shell the monitor list only once the window exists
Decision (the finding step 0.0.1q asked for): before the window exists, eframe 0.37 reaches
winit's monitors only inside its own `viewport_builder` (`event_loop.available_monitors()`,
which its persistence's `WindowSettings::clamp_position_to_monitors` uses), with the
`ActiveEventLoop` no public hook hands out: the `event_loop_builder` hook sees the builder
before it is built, the `window_builder` hook only the `ViewportBuilder`, and winit 0.30
refuses a second event loop in a process (`EVENT_LOOP_CREATED`, `RecreationAttempt`), so a
probe loop before eframe's would make eframe's creation fail. Once the window exists, the
native `Frame` carries it (`Frame::winit_window`), and winit's `Window::available_monitors`
lists every monitor's position and size in physical pixels, a safe call. So the window is
created at the remembered place unchecked, and the first frame checks the place's title bar
against that list: on a monitor, it resends the position; on none (a monitor unplugged since),
it sends the fit a first start sends. The window then sits off every monitor, out of sight, so
the member does not see it move, unless the desk's scales changed with the unplugging (a place
on a 200% monitor, a 100% primary left), where winit's conversion of the creation position
lands it on a monitor for that one frame. `ViewportInfo::monitor_size` alone could not do it: it names
the window's own monitor without its origin, and the nearest monitor's when the window is on
none. Not an OS call of the shell's own (`EnumDisplayMonitors` on Windows, an `unsafe` block,
first planned on the belief that eframe offered no list at all). Not eframe's persistence
(`persist_window`), which would clamp through winit for us: its `WindowGeometry::from_window`
stores the inner size in the shell's zoomed points and restores it at the zoom egui's memory
holds (1 unless the whole egui memory is persisted too), so a window closed under the design
width would reopen wider by the zoom; it also knows one window, not two classes, and writes a
second file. The record itself is `[x, y, width, height, scale]`: the outer position in
physical pixels, since a point is a different number of pixels on each monitor and Windows and
X11 place windows in pixels (egui-winit converts `OuterPosition` with the window's current zoom
times scale); the inner size in points at zoom 1, the size a window keeps when the OS moves it
to a monitor of another scale, never in the shell's zoomed points; and the monitor's scale
factor when recorded, because winit converts a creation position with the scale of the monitor
it creates the window on (the primary), so the record's own scale turns the pixels into the
number winit expects wherever the two scales agree, which is every single-scale desk. The first
frame's resent position is a no-op where creation landed right and the fix on a mixed-scale
desk (a window on a 100% monitor beside a 200% primary): not a move from a centered creation,
because eframe shows the window after the first frame's paint and applies that frame's
viewport commands after the show, so the member would see the jump.
Why: the plan said winit's list "as eframe reaches it at start" and left the how to this step;
reading eframe 0.37, egui-winit 0.37 and winit 0.30 shows no route before the window exists,
the two ways around that (eframe's persistence, a probe event loop) each break something the
shell needs, and the route after it costs one frame the member does not see on a desk of one
scale.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Window size classes", ST-WIN-04.

## 2026-10-26 — studio — The crash dump's crates fit P38's condition; its hook waits on one `unsafe` block
Decision: `crash-handler` 0.8.1, `minidumper` 0.11.0 and `minidump-writer` 0.13.0 (with
`minidump` 0.27.0 for the tests) meet the 10 MB condition P38 was accepted on, at 221 KiB. The
hook's attach is an `unsafe` call of ours, so nothing of the dump is built until the
maintainer rules on it (`QUESTIONS.md`); `minidumper-child`, which would hide that block, is
not taken.
Why: a probe built with the project's release profile, with and without the monitor, the hook
and a stack-overflow trigger wired, measured 243,200 B without and 469,504 B with (`.tmp/0_0_1k4/probe/`),
and its overflow left a dump the `minidump` crate reads as five threads and exception
`0xC00000FD`. `make_crash_event` is an `unsafe fn` and `CrashEvent` an `unsafe trait`, since
the closure runs in the crashed process; there is no safe way to attach. Building the rest
without the hook would start a monitor beside every window that never writes a dump.
`minidumper-child` marks its monitor by an environment variable rather than the plan's
argument, always starts the running exe (so the start's failure cannot be tested on a program
that is not an exe), and pins `crash-handler` 0.7 and `minidumper` 0.10.
Plan: `plans/core/architecture.md` "Diagnostic logging", the "crash dump" bullet.

## 2026-10-27 — studio — The crash dump's hook is one `unsafe` block of ours
Decision: the crash dump attaches its hook through `crash-handler`'s `make_crash_event` in one
`unsafe` block in `studio`, its `// SAFETY:` comment saying why the closure is sound in a
crashed process (it allocates and locks nothing and only sends the dump request).
Why: the maintainer's yes to `QUESTIONS.md` "May the crash dump's hook use one `unsafe`
block?": no safe route exists (the function and the trait are `unsafe`), and the crate that
hides the block, `minidumper-child`, does not fit the plan (an environment variable instead
of the monitor's argument, no testable failed start, older crate versions).
Plan: `plans/core/architecture.md` "Diagnostic logging", the crash dump bullet.

## 2026-10-27 — studio — The preview's icon and its build dependency
Decision: the preview's icon is the maintainer's picture of Archer, the whole picture at 32
pixels and up and a tight square on the head at 24 and 16 (the maintainer's split): an `.ico`

`icon_data::from_png_bytes`, no new dependency) the tight crop on Windows, where winit sets it

2026-10-19), named in the turn report.

## 2026-10-27 — studio — The crash dump's dialog asks for both files, and the monitor appends to an append-mode log
Decision: the next start's dialog after a dumped crash asks for the old log and `studio.dmp`
together, saying the dump may still show the member's user name; the monitor's line counts
anywhere in an old log that did not end with a closing line, not only last, and an empty
old log counts as not closed; the
window opens `studio.log` for appending, as the monitor does, and a monitor that cannot bind
or serve appends its error there; the monitor's hidden argument carries the data location
before the socket's path; the window waits at most two seconds for it.
Why: the dump's module list holds the exe's full path, often under the user's folder, which no
redaction reaches, so the member is told rather than promised a clean file; a window thread
writing at its own offset after the monitor's line would overwrite it, and append mode puts
every write at the end, and the window's other threads keep running (and may log) while the
crashed one waits for the monitor's reply, so a last-line check would lose the dump, while a
second window's monitor can append into a log whose session then closes, so the closing
line wins; passing
the folder, not resolving it again, keeps the monitor writing where the window's log is.
Plan: `plans/core/architecture.md` "Diagnostic logging", the session bullet and the crash dump bullet.

Why: `winresource` writes a version block with every icon, its file description and product
name defaulting to the package's name, `studio`, and Task Manager lists a running program by

uses (without the block, Task Manager shows the file name). A text spelling, not
`studio_core`'s `app_name!`: a build script runs before the crate is compiled, and making
`studio_core` a build dependency would compile eframe twice for one string.
Plan: `plans/core/development_plan.md` "The preview's icon" (`icon.ico`'s bullet) and "The
preview's codename: Unlimited Tool Works" (the text spellings).

## 2026-10-27 — gui — Selawik replaces Ubuntu; the drafts load the app's own font files
Decision: the body font is Selawik (Microsoft's open metric twin of Segoe UI, SIL Open Font
License 1.1), bundled in `resources/fonts/` in place of Ubuntu Regular; monospace stays Hack.
Every glyph the suite draws comes from a bundled file: proportional Selawik, the icon font,
`egui-icons`, Hack, `NotoEmoji-Regular`, `emoji-icon-font` (egui's `monochrome_emoji_fonts`
feature); eframe's system fallback is left for what members type. The drafts load the same
files by `@font-face` in the same order, name no system font or generic family, draw no bold,
and set egui's line height (1.2 times the size) explicitly; `scripts/draft_fonts.py` fails on any other font a draft really draws in. The
drafts' approval is withdrawn until the maintainer's close look at them in these fonts.
Why: the drafts named Ubuntu, installed on no machine they were opened on, so the browsers drew
Segoe UI and every layout was reviewed and calibrated in its metrics, about 3.5% narrower than
the Ubuntu the app draws (Steam's PES 2019 path: 425.7 points in egui with Segoe UI, 438.4 with
Ubuntu). Selawik keeps those widths (426.1) and may be bundled, which Segoe UI may not, so the
calibrated layouts stand, the maintainer's choice over redrawing them in Ubuntu. The same probe
found the drafts' symbols drawn from Cambria Math, Segoe UI Symbol and Arial, their ids in
Consolas, the pitch canvas in Arial Bold, and a line 16 points high where egui's is 15; and the
app itself drew → ↓ ≡ ▸ ▾ ● ▶ ⚠ ✔ ✕ ✖ ⠇ through the system fallback (none in its bundled
fonts), a different glyph per machine and a missing one in every test context.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Prototypes before implementation" (the Fonts bullet) and "Other UI
components" (the Dark/light theme row).

the like) is drawn as an SVG and built into the suite's icon font at its own Unicode codepoint,
by the icons' fontTools build; the font chains are proportional Selawik, the icon font,
`egui-icons`, monospace Hack, Selawik, the icon font, `egui-icons`. This replaces the same
day's chain through egui's `NotoEmoji-Regular`, `emoji-icon-font` and Hack, and its swaps of
✕ for the icon X and ⠇ for ≡, which the drafts undo.
Why: the maintainer's suggestion. One hand draws every symbol at the text's size and weight,
where three fallback fonts gave mismatched shapes (NotoEmoji's scaled 0.81, emoji-icon-font's
0.90, Hack's monospace arrows); a string keeps its character, so no call site changes; it is
the single-colour icon font the plan already builds from SVGs ("GUI framework choice: egui"),
with no new dependency, where SVGs drawn at run time need `egui_extras`' `svg` feature, which
the plan leaves until after 1.0.0.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Other UI components" (the Dark/light theme row).

## 2026-10-27 — gui — The symbols are a font of their own, on the body font's metrics
Decision: the symbols of the entry above are built into a file of their own,
`resources/fonts/symbols.ttf` (`scripts/make_symbols.py`, from `resources/symbols/*.svg`),
whose units per em and vertical metrics are read from the body font's file; the chains are
proportional Selawik, the symbols font, the icon font, `egui-icons`, monospace Hack, Selawik,
the symbols font, the icon font, `egui-icons`. Each symbol keeps the advance and ink box of the
glyph the drafts were reviewed with (Segoe UI's or Segoe UI Symbol's, measured, no outline
copied). The census adds ↻ ∉ ⏷ to the list. The build needs fontTools and picosvg (a
development tool, like `draft_fonts.py`), so CI never runs it; `make_symbols_test.py`, run by
hand, checks the committed files are its output, and 0.0.1w2's Rust test guards the glyphs.
Why: egui places a glyph from a later font of the chain by centring that font's line height on
the body font's (epaint's `text_layout.rs`), where the browser aligns baselines; in the icon
font's metrics (1.0 em high, Selawik's 1.2) a symbol sits 0.6 point below the text's baseline
at 12.5 in the app and on it in the drafts. A file of its own keeps the icon font's metrics,
and so the rail's icons, untouched; reading the metrics from the body font's file makes a
later body font a rebuild (the maintainer, 2026-10-27, keeps alternatives to Selawik open).
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Other UI components" (the Dark/light theme row).

## 2026-10-27 — gui — Menu buttons end in ⏷, as the drafts draw them
Decision: every menu button's label ends in ` ⏷` (U+23F7, the symbols font's), as the drafts'

Why: the drafts are the approved layout and the arrow is in every menu button's width there;

Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Other UI components" (the Menu buttons row).

## 2026-10-27 — gui — The drafts draw the status bar's icons from the icon font, as the app does
Decision: the drafts' status-bar conditions draw the icon font's warning and download glyphs
and the notice's dismiss its X, as `studio_core` does (`ShellCondition::icon`, the status bar's
`icons::X`), not ⚠, ⬇ and ×; the simulated title bar's maximize box is drawn in CSS, not typed;
`scripts/draft_fonts.py` lets the sample saves' member characters (♂, fullwidth letters) fall

## 2026-10-27 — save_editor — Formation pictures, the formation's name and the nation names: the maintainer's answers
Decision (maintainer, answering Track D's drafts' questions):

- Nation names (8.30): PES 2016's table includes 4cc's own nations of the VGL database
  (OFFSIDE 249, EQUESTRIA 251); PES 2020 uses PES 2021's table.

never uses; the save dialog lets a member name a picture they share.

0.0.1x, 8.33, 8.34; the proposals in `side/drafts2`'s `.tmp/<step>/look.md`).

## 2026-10-27 — save_editor — A pitch player dropped on another swaps the two slots in the shown formation, as the game's drag
Decision: on the Tactics pitch, a player dropped on another exchanges the two slots' position, X
and Y in the shown formation of the shown preset alone, each player staying in his slot; the
keeper is never a target. The starting-eleven exchange (2026-10-22's drop) stays the XI list's,
a row dropped on another row or on a pitch marker. Supersedes 2026-10-22's "A pitch player
dropped on another exchanges the two starters" for the pitch drop.
Why: the maintainer pointed out that the game swaps two ways, one reaching every preset, and
asked that the editor's drag behave as the game's and, if easy, offer the other way too. In
game (PES 2021, 2026-10-27), a save written after a drag on /f/'s Kick-off changed only that
formation's two slots; one written after selecting one starter and then the other on /o/
changed only the starting eleven. The editor's drop wrote the second, so a drag meant for one
formation moved the two players in all nine; the XI list already offers the second.

bullet), SE-GUI-12.

## 2026-10-27 — save_editor — The formation's name counts the positions grid's rows, in Selawik Semibold
Decision: the Tactics pitch writes the shown formation's name in its bottom-left corner: the ten
outfield slots counted by the playable positions grid's row their position belongs to, back to
front (LB CB RB, DMF CMF, LMF AMF RMF, LWF CF SS RWF), an empty row left out; the grid's rows
and the name are one table. Set in Selawik Semibold at 21 pt, white, where the game's screen
places it; the drafts name the face through `--font-label`/`FONT_LABEL`.
Why: PES 2021's screen gave that rule on all eight formations captured (four teams), where the
drafted rule (LMF and RMF with the CMF) read /f/'s `3-3-2-2` and `3-4-2-1` as `3-5-2` and
`3-6-1`; the position counts, not the spot (an AMF given CMF at his own spot turns `3-3-1-3`
into `3-4-3`). Semibold, not Bold: egui's dark-mode text alpha thickens strokes, and drawn so
Semibold's verticals measure 2.97 px against the game's 3.01, Bold's 3.41 (the maintainer: the
stroke thickness must match, the typeface need not).
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Tactics editor" ("The formation's name"), SE-GUI-39;
`plans/core/gui.md` "Prototypes before implementation" (the Fonts bullet).

## 2026-10-27 — core — The app pins the drafts' text sizes
Decision: `theme::install` sets egui's text styles to the sizes the drafts draw: `Small` 11,
`Body` and `Button` 12.5, `Monospace` 12, `Heading` 15 (the host stylesheet's `.small`, body,

through an egui upgrade too; matching the drafts to egui's 13 instead would re-open every
approved width.

## 2026-10-27 — save_editor — The changes table's colours draw a swatch; the list has no footer line
Decision: in the table of changes (the toolbar's changes list, 8.31, and the close prompt,

## 2026-10-27 — save_editor — A pitch drop keeps the position: the game's rule is not a map of areas
Decision: a starter dropped on the Tactics pitch's grass keeps his position, as before; the
editor does not try to change it as PES 2021's drag does. Worklog 0.0.1y3 asked to map the
position areas instead, and measured that there are none to map.
Why: in game, the same spot gives different positions by who is dragged (at (24.7, 26) a
dragged LMF reads AMF, a dragged CMF reads LMF), and the switch moves with the teammates (an
LMF turns CMF about 11.5 short of the nearest CMF, at x 41.3 or 31.7 as that CMF stands at 53
or 43); the area the screen lights while a player is held is not where his position changes
(`.tmp/0_0_1y3/findings.md`). A rule fitted to these scans has three unknown parts, and a
wrong guess sets a position silently, where today the member sets it in the player's box and
sees what he set.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Tactics editor", the bullet "A pitch player dropped on another".
## 2026-10-27 — team_compiler — `--edit-mode-closed` reaches the line as `flag`; the tests set the tool's probe
Decision: `savefile_skipped_pes_running`'s line carries the flag as a context entry,
`flag=--edit-mode-closed`, after `path` and `version`; the flag has no settings counterpart;
the words the compiler shares with the Save editor's writing commands (the flag's `--help`
line, the message's "Close the game's Edit mode, then <run> again with `--edit-mode-closed`.
The save is then written, and Edit mode's Load reads it in without restarting the game.") are
written in the spec. The running-PES probe is a field of the tool (`fn() -> Vec<RunningPes>`):
`Tool::new()` takes the real process list (a unit test's build, none), and a new `pub fn
Tool::with_running_probe` lets the in-process command-line tests set it, the default sandbox
reporting no game. The flag is accepted in a run that writes no save (`--no-deploy`,
`--mode test`) and changes nothing there.
Why: a console line prints a finding's code and context, never the catalog's text, so a flag
named only in the catalog is not on the line TC-SAV-17 reads; `savefile_missing` already
carries its command the same way. A setting would be a standing "yes" to a question about the
game's state at each compile, answered before it is asked. Accepted where unused rather
than refused as `--no-deploy` is with the loose-file modes: the member's word about Edit
mode is not wrong in any mode, and a refusal would break a launcher line that always passes
it. The probe on the tool, not a
`#[cfg(test)]` stub alone: an integration test links the crate without `cfg(test)`, and the
live probe made nine savefile tests fail while PES 2021 ran on the developer's machine.
Plan: `spec/team_compiler/pipeline.md` "6. Post-processing" (the plan's "Savefile step while
the game runs" moved there), `spec/team_compiler/settings.md` "CLI", `spec/team_compiler/README.md`
TC-SAV-17 (replacing TC-SAV-10), `plans/team_compiler/gui.md` the save findings' bullet.

## 2026-10-27 — development plan — The bundle's `data/` holds its settings and DBC7's rules file; `just release` assembles the file
Decision: the 0.0.1 bundle ships `data/settings.toml` (the Save editor's `aatf_rules =
"rules/dbc7.4ccrules"`, and the Team compiler's `multicpk_mode` and `cpk_name` at their
defaults) and `data/rules/dbc7.4ccrules`. `scripts/release.py` writes the rules file by joining
`rulesets/dbc7.rhai`, `logic/logic.rhai` and the empty CUSTOM CHECKS section, the layout the
Ruleset editor writes, and refuses unless the staged exe's `ruleset-editor validate` passes it
and its `update-logic` reports the logic current.
Why: the plan's "its settings name it" can only be a settings file in the bundle, and the only
place one is read without a first-run choice is `data/` beside the exe, which makes the bundle
portable, so its first start asks nothing (a preview's testers lose the location choice; DBC's
managers get DBC's check from the first open, the 2026-10-24 entry's aim). The rules file sits
in `data/` because a relative `aatf_rules` resolves there, where one beside the exe would show
`../rules/...` in the settings row. No command of the build writes a template, and a new
`ruleset-editor` command for one build-time use is CLI surface no member needs; the exe's own
checks catch a join that drifts from the format. The two Team compiler lines let the readme
tell VGL's organizer which value to change instead of what to type in.
Plan: `plans/core/development_plan.md` "Divegrass Before Christmas".
## 2026-10-27 — save_editor — The dragged player's position rule is read from PES 2016's executable
Decision: the game's rule for the position a dragged starter takes is read from PES 2016's
executable (worklog 0.0.1y4), not fitted to more in-game scans; the reading is then checked
against the PES 2021 scans of 0.0.1y3, and a rule that reproduces them replaces the kept
position for the versions it holds in. Until then a pitch drop keeps the position.
Why: the maintainer's answer to the question 0.0.1y3 parked. The scans showed a rule with
three unknown parts (what counts as a teammate's line, each position's allowed region, the
defaults where it is not allowed), each a series of scans of its own, where the code states
it whole; PES 2016's is the last executable that is not packed, so its code reads directly
(PES 2021's is the version the scans measured, so they are the check).
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Tactics editor", the bullet "A pitch player dropped on another".
## 2026-10-27 — core — A CLI-only tool has no settings section
Decision: the settings menu draws no section for a tool the registry marks CLI-only, whatever
its `default_settings()` table holds; its keys are edited in the settings file.
Why: the preview's audit (worklog 0.0.1j, j4) found two such sections every first-run member
meets through the readme's step 3: the Ruleset editor's header opens on nothing (its table
holds only `last_folder` and `recent_files`, state the tool writes), and the Team compiler's
says only that its settings are not built yet. The plan's rule (a tool has settings when its
table is not empty) did not catch a table of state, or a tool whose window is not built.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Settings menu", the bullet "One collapsible section per registered
tool that has settings".
## 2026-10-27 — core — The preview bundle carries VGL 27's rules file too
Decision: the 0.0.1 bundle's `data/rules/` holds `vgl27.4ccrules` beside `dbc7.4ccrules`,
assembled the same way; the bundled settings keep naming DBC7's, and the readme's VGL section
says to pick VGL 27's in the Save editor's settings.

"It should, but as a 'just in case' thing". VGL's organizer works in the Team compiler in this

at hand.

## 2026-10-27 — save_editor — No narrow-pane fallback, and no frame laid out under the design width
Decision: the Save editor's layouts for a pane narrower than its design go: the three
columns' wrap, the Skills and COM cards' one column, the Appearance groups' fewer pairs a row
and the team row's wrap. The shell discards the pass that finds the zoom changed and runs it
again at the new zoom, so the frame after a width jump lays out at 1280 points like every
other. The quick actions' halves stay: a rules file's long tier label reaches them in any
window.
Why: the zoom rule and the fixed 240-point list leave a settled pane of 952 points, wider than
every fallback's threshold (audit 0.0.1m2, `.tmp/0_0_1m/m2_audit_report.md`); the one frame
after a jump (egui applies a zoom when the next pass begins) was the only native way in. Kept,
they cost code a reader must follow and a cached-width bug (Astra A2a-1), and the view tests,
drawn 1100 wide, ran in the fallback state no member sees rather than the design's.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Scaling with the width" and ST-WIN-02; `plans/save_editor.md` "The
player view" and the team view's row.
## 2026-10-27 — core — A window closed maximized reopens maximized
Decision: `window_main` (and `window_special`) gain a sixth number, 1 when the window was
maximized on its last frame that was not minimized; the window is created at the recorded
normal place and maximized, so its restore button gives that place back. A five-number record
reads as not maximized; a place found on no monitor opens fitted and not maximized.
Why: the maintainer accepted proposal P39 (a member who keeps the window maximized gets it
back maximized, as most desktop programs do). It lands in 0.0.1 beside 0.0.1q, whose code it
extends and whose built-window check ("close maximized") is still open, so one check covers
both.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Window size classes" (the paragraph on the remembered place) and
ST-WIN-04.
## 2026-10-27 — tooling — The gates and the mutation runs run at checkpoints, not on every commit
Decision: a docs-only commit runs `just doc-pointers` and `just acceptance`; a code commit
reruns the changed packages' own tests, clippy and fmt in the real workspace; `just
gates-changed <the last commit it passed at>` runs once over the commits since, at a
checkpoint: a surface's review loop ending, a worklog step closing, a merge of another branch;
the full `just gates` before a release build and on CI. A surface's `just mutants-diff` runs
once at its review loop's end, right after that checkpoint's gates, over every commit the loop
landed, not once per rework round. A change to a script under `scripts/` other than the test
runner and its memory-cap wrapper no longer runs every package's tests. Supersedes "every commit still runs the full `just gates`"
(2026-10-25).
Why: the maintainer's question, with the suite past 5000 tests: one commit to `studio_core`
ran every package's tests (about 200 s plus the build) though the sidekick had run its own
crates' already. What the per-commit run added, a dependent package's failure, a checkpoint
still finds, and while the history is local a later find costs a short search over a few small
commits. A mutation run per round froze its crates for its whole length and repeated the
checkpoint's tests in its baseline; one per loop measures the same lines once. Over the 212 code
commits since 2026-10-20 (`.tmp/lead/gates_savings.py`, weighted by each binary's test time), a
checkpoint every 3 to 4 code commits saves 20-29% of the test time, and the scripts rule
another 11 points (scripts changed in 44 of them).
Plan: `CONTRIBUTING.md` "Testing and verification" and "Mutation runs"; `AGENTS.md` ("After a
step", the reviews' sweeps, the converge paragraph).
## 2026-10-27 — core — A window reopened maximized is maximized again by its first frame, on every platform
Decision: the first frame of a window reopened from a maximized record sends the maximize again
after the position it resends, on Windows as on X11, rather than on X11 alone.
Why: the plan named X11 (a window manager ignores the maximize asked of the hidden window); the
implementation found that winit moves a maximized window by restoring it first (Windows
`set_outer_position` clears the maximized flag, a `ShowWindow(SW_RESTORE)`), so the position
resend un-maximized the window the creation maximized, on the main platform. Skipping the resend
for a maximized place was rejected: on a mixed-scale desk the creation's position is converted
with the primary monitor's scale, and only the resend corrects it. The cost, the window seen
restoring and maximizing once on the first frame, is for the built-window check to measure.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Window size classes" (the remembered place's paragraph); ST-WIN-04.
## 2026-10-27 — studio_core — A frame may run three passes, not egui's two
Decision: `theme::install` sets egui's `max_passes` to 3; the Save editor's player view
discards a pass whose measured column widths differ from the ones it laid out with.
Why: a player's first frame was drawn 26 points right of every later one (0.0.1m2b): the
centring pad reads the widths the previous pass measured, and egui's `Grid` discards the
first pass of a new grid to size it narrow, so the second pass centred on the sizing pass's
widths; egui ignores a further discard once `max_passes` passes ran. Not a pad from the
constants: column 3 measures 153.97 points against its constant's 170. Not a fixed width for
column 3: it changes the approved layout. Not the option set from the Save editor's view: a
tool changing a context-wide option. A third pass runs only when the second asked for a
discard: a player's first frame, or a zoom change meeting a new grid.
Plan: `spec/core/gui.md` "Shell layout", "Scaling with the width"; `plans/save_editor.md`
"Editing UI", the "The player view" bullet.
## 2026-10-27 — workspace — A code comment stands on its own
Decision (the maintainer): a code comment never cites a plan, `DECISIONS.md`, the worklog or
the log, a step, a review round or concern, or an agent; it says what it needs in plain short
sentences, and when the why runs long it points at one `docs/spec/` section by file and
heading. A tooling file may point at `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `RUNBOOK.md`, a test at its fixture
folder's `README.md`, a view at the element of its draft it reproduces. `scripts/comment_refs.py`
(`just comment-refs`) lists the breaches; the 1044 found when the rule was set are rewritten in
slices, and the check joins the gates when none is left.
Why: the maintainer found the comments hard to read: parenthesised chains of plan sections,
decision dates and step tags, where a reader wants one sentence; and a plan pointer goes stale
when the plan moves to the spec. Decisions live in this file alone.
Plan: `CONTRIBUTING.md` "Code style", the bullet "A comment stands on its own"; `AGENTS.md`'s
design sweep.
## 2026-10-27 — balls_compiler — An error on a listed ball means the compile writes no CPK
Decision: any error on a listed ball (no usable model, a missing folder, a name too long) or on
the list itself stops the compile before a CPK is written; the per-ball statuses already show
it. The validation list's "E, ball skipped" became "E".
Why: a ball's id is its list position. Skipping one, as 2.03 did, shifts every later ball off
the number the organizer sees; keeping the position empty leaves a gap in `Ball.bin` that PES
may not accept (unchecked). An export with an error gets a human's attention anyway, so the
simplest rule wins.
Plan: `plans/balls_compiler.md` "GUI" (the Validation bullet).
## 2026-10-27 — balls_compiler — The default CPK name is `4cc_38_balls`
Decision: `cpk_name` defaults to `4cc_38_balls`, not `4cc_39_balls`.
Why: the cup's PES 2021 install loads `4cc_38_balls.cpk` and lists it in its `DpFileList.bin`,
and a real 2.03 run's output and the earlier balls compilers carry the same name. 2.03's own
default, `4cc_39_balls_test`, appears only in a test copy; `4cc_39_balls` appears nowhere.
Plan: `plans/balls_compiler.md` "Compilation pipeline" step 6, "Settings".
## 2026-10-27 — balls_compiler — `import-legacy` keeps the DDS of a same-stem DDS and FTEX pair
Decision: when merging the two 2.03 trees gives a DDS and an FTEX of one stem, the migrated
folder keeps the DDS. The newer-modification-time rule, its tie and unreadable-time cases and
their fixtures are gone. A `balls_list.txt` line migrates as its first whitespace-delimited token.
Why: every 2.03 compile converted the DDS over its same-stem FTEX, so the DDS is what the game
showed and the FTEX never reached a CPK; a timestamp could pick content no cup ever saw. 2.03
read only a line's first token as the folder name, so the rest of a line was never a name.
Plan: `plans/balls_compiler.md` "CLI", "Testing".
## 2026-10-27 — balls_compiler — How `balls.txt`, `name.txt` and the thumbnail are read
Decision: `balls.txt` skips blank lines and trims each line; it has no comment syntax, so a
`;` line is a folder name. `name.txt` is the file's text with a UTF-8 byte-order mark dropped
and trimmed at both ends; a line break inside it is an error. More than one thumbnail candidate
(a root `thumbnail.dds` beside a legacy one, or two in `thumbnail/`) is an error naming them.
Duplicates in the list stay rejected, now with the reason.
Why: 2.03's tokenizer skipped blank lines and trimmed, invisibly to the organizer. Its `;`
comments were undocumented and dropped a ball silently, where a missing-folder error shows it.
It kept a name file's last line, passed a byte-order mark into `Ball.bin` as name bytes, and
took the last of several thumbnails silently. No shipped file relies on any of these. A
duplicate spends a second of the 50 slots on the same model and is far more often a typo.
Plan: `plans/balls_compiler.md` "The balls export (the format)".
## 2026-10-27 — balls_compiler — Only the textures a ball's model names ship
Decision: on Fox the CPK carries the textures the rewritten FMDL names, and on pre-Fox the
`.model`/`.mtl` pair and the textures the `.mtl` names; any other file in the folder is
`file_not_used` (W). FMDL texture directories of the `ballXXX` form are rewritten to the
ball's id and any other directory is left as authored. The FPK's one entry is `ball.fmdl`.
Why: 2.03 shipped every `.ftex` (Fox) or the whole folder (pre-Fox), files the game never
loads, as the Team compiler already rules. An error for a directory of another form would
refuse a ball pointing at a texture the game itself ships; a model that names none of its
own textures shows through the `file_not_used` warnings on them. 2.03's GzsTool manifest
named the entry `ball.fmdl`.
Plan: `plans/balls_compiler.md` "Compilation pipeline" steps 2 and 3.
## 2026-10-27 — music_export_editor — Files: a refused load changes nothing, saves end lines with `\n`, the VA fallback is written from a copy
Decision: a load the parser refuses leaves the editor as it was, the open file's path
included. A save writes `\n` line ends on every OS; RigDJ files re-save byte-identically once
their CRLF is made `\n`. The victory fallback (the anthem entries written as victory anthems
when the VA slot has no non-special entries) is applied to a copy of the export that both the
preview and Save write; the model's VA slot stays empty.
Why: RigDJ took a refused file's path, so its next Save overwrote that file with the export on
screen. Its CRLF was Python's platform default; Rigdio strips each line, so either reads the
same, and one line end on every OS keeps the files equal. RigDJ copied the anthem entries into
the model itself, so both slots then held the same objects, and its preview never showed the
fallback; applying it to a copy keeps "the preview is what is written" true. RigDJ copied only
into an empty VA, which left a VA of only `special` entries with nothing for Rigdio's VA
button.
Plan: `plans/music_export_editor.md` "Background", "What the editor does" (Open / New / Save,
Victory fallback), "Testing".
## 2026-10-27 — music_export_editor — Players keep the file's order, and a new name is checked at entry
Decision: the slot list shows and writes the players in the file's order; a new player goes
before the first whose name sorts after it. A new or renamed name is trimmed and refused when
empty, a reserved word or slot label in any case, holding `;`, starting with `#`, or an exact
duplicate. A case-only duplicate is allowed and flagged, as is a player named like a reserved
slot in another case. Reordering the players is proposal P40, not built.
Why: the file's order is Rigdio's button order, and 27 of the 50 RigDJ-written exports on the
maintainer's machine carry a hand order that RigDJ's re-sort on load undid. Inserting at the
sorted position, as RigDJ did, keeps a sorted list sorted without re-sorting a hand-ordered one.
Each refused name made RigDJ write a line Rigdio reads as something else, or empty a reserved
slot's songs silently. Rigdio keys players as written, so `Billy` and `billy` are two.
Plan: `plans/music_export_editor.md` "What the editor does" (Slot list), "New capabilities"
(Validation panel).
## 2026-10-27 — music_export_editor — A song row's path: the picker's form, empty refused
Decision: the file picker writes the path relative to the export's folder when the file is
under it, else the bare file name; a typed path is kept. A new row's path is empty, and an empty
path is a validation error that blocks Save. In the VA slot, up/down moves an entry past its
neighbour of the same section.
Why: RigDJ wrote every pick as its bare name, so no community export carries a folder; the
player resolves a subfolder, so keeping one under the export costs nothing. RigDJ's new row
read `New Song`, a file Rigdio then looks for. The parser refuses an empty path, so a saved one
could not be reopened. RigDJ's arrows moved entries across the special and regular sections.
Plan: `plans/music_export_editor.md` "What the editor does" (Song rows).
## 2026-10-27 — music_export_editor — The condition forms RigDJ lacked or got wrong
Decision: `every` takes an integer from 1; `opponent` takes free text beside the team list;
the `match` grid refuses OK with nothing checked and writes a confirmed grid in the match
types' order, an untouched condition keeping the file's order; `pause` gets an action dropdown
and an "every n" integer; `end` a `stop`-only form, a loaded `end loop` kept until its form is
confirmed. An empty `mostgoals` scorer or `special` label means no argument. Randomise Horns
gives `randomise` to warcry entries too. Enter confirms and Escape cancels a form; deleting is
the button alone.
Why: `every 0` crashes Rigdio. A guest team is not on the teams list. The parser refuses a bare
`match`, and RigDJ wrote the words in a set's order, different on each run. RigDJ's `pause`
form had no `every` field and dropped it from every line on save. A bare `mostgoals` means this
player and a bare `special` is labelled by its file, which the plan's "refused at entry" had
wrong. Rigdio draws warcries at random when they all carry `randomise`, which is what a slot
built with RigDJ's box does; matching it keeps those slots playing the same. RigDJ's Delete key
also deleted the chip while the cursor was in a text field.
Plan: `plans/music_export_editor.md` "What the editor does" (Condition editing, Guard rails,
Randomise Horns), "GUI view".

## 2026-10-27 — studio_core shell — A maximized reopen resends its position only where the creation can have landed wrong
Decision: the first frame of a window reopened maximized sends the position again only when the
record's scale differs from the primary monitor's or from the frame's pixels per point; it
still sends the maximize. A place not maximized keeps the unconditional resend.
Why: the resend on a maximized window restores it to move it and maximizes it again, a flicker
the maintainer sees on the built window; where the record's scale is the primary's and the
window's, winit's creation already put the window at the record's pixels, so the resend moves
nothing. Not the resend skipped for every maximized place, which left the restore place and the
maximized monitor wrong on a mixed-scale desk; not the window created unmaximized, which keeps
our restore-and-maximize and adds a maximize of a shown window. A window not maximized does not
flicker at a resend that moves nothing.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Window size classes", the remembered place's paragraph.

## 2026-10-27 — kit_config_editor — The Kit config editor saves on Save, and the rest of Kit Manager's audit
Decision: nothing is written until Save (Ctrl+S); unsaved changes are the difference from the
file as opened or last saved, and opening another file or closing asks to save, discard or
cancel; the loose-file and container modes write through a temporary file renamed over the
old one, and the loose-file mode's Save as adopts the new path. A numeric field takes any
value its bits hold, warning beside it when the selected version's range is exceeded. The
name's shape, Y and size gray out with the name off. The five texture names are editable
ASCII text of at most 15 characters in the loose-file and container modes, shown only in
export mode. The manual byte-parity test leaves out Kit Manager's four write defects.
Why: the Save editor and the Music export editor save on Save with the same unsaved-changes
rule, and one rule across the suite's editors is what members learn once. Kit Manager's own
model is not worth keeping: its "not saved" warning ignored edits, its exit always asked, and
its Save as left later Saves on the original file. Its lists refused stock values (collars up
to 131 against 106). Its graying of the name's fields follows the format (a hidden name has no
shape). The compiled-bin fix is the one place texture names are typed by hand today, and a
wrong one is a kit that does not load. Its defects (a badge field that writes nothing, a shape
edit that clears a size bit, a spacing edit that clears two undecoded bits, a sleeves control
never enabled) would make an identical-bytes test fail for Kit Manager's reasons.
Plan: `plans/kit_config_editor.md` "GUI view" (the texture names, Saving, the form's gating and
numeric fields), "Testing".

## 2026-10-27 — music_player — The Music player's controls, ruled against Rigdio v2.2.0
Decision: Rigdio's controls are matched where a streamer's habit depends on them: ⟲ stops at
once and rewinds the last entry; a `speed` entry ignores the slider on every play; a load
zeroes both scores; Reset asks first; a chant press during a chant does nothing; one Undo
level; the boost's +5 dB start and whole-dB steps; the per-button volume sliders on every team
button; a missing song file refuses the load. Departures where Rigdio's behavior is an
accident of its code: Chaoshorn leaves playing buttons playing and starts each entry once,
Kill starts nothing; a re-press during a fade lets the fade finish beside the new sound, or
resumes the same entry at full volume where it is; `pause restart` restarts under sync; the
VA timer stops at the song's end; one chant tally per team, a new round at weight 0; the
Normalize swap keeps the score; Undo seeks nothing; the board stays live while one slot
loads; settings apply without a restart; the master applies to event clips.
Why: the audit read each control's code (`.tmp/10_0i/rigdio_controls_audit.md`). Where the
code and its own comments or dialogs disagree, the comment's intent stands ("never repeat",
"Reset everything the team is using"); where a behavior only follows from a toggle, a cache
or a thread (Chaoshorn pausing what plays, the sync cache undoing a restart, a toggle zeroing
the score), no streamer can want it. The 12 exports carrying `pause restart` were written
when it restarted.
Plan: `plans/music_player.md` "Song selection", "Playback behavior", "Chants", "Match state",
"title.log", "Event clips revived", "Loudness normalization", "GUI view", "Settings".

## 2026-10-27 — refs_arranger — The Refs arranger's plan checked against FoxDen and the export library
Decision: the plan describes FoxDen's referee module as it is: it draws 1..35 at the match

simple; members' errors get a person's attention anyway.
Plan: `plans/refs_arranger.md` "Background", "The Fox referee hook", "The tool",

## 2026-10-28 — pes_savefile — PES 2015's keeper terms average the keeper abilities it stores
Decision: the overall formula's two keeper terms (goalkeeping with coverage; catching, clearing and
reflexes) take the mean of the abilities the save's version stores. PES 2015's record has no
clearing, reflexes or coverage (its catching is Saving), so its terms are goalkeeping alone and
Saving alone.
Why: the formula is PES 2016's, whose record stores all five; a missing ability counted as 0
would sink every PES 2015 keeper (one keeper ability at 0 takes a 70 keeper to the floor of 40),
and PES 2015's own formula is not read. Averaging what is stored keeps the terms on PES 2016's
scale.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Tactics editor", the pitch-drop paragraph's formula.

element (the Ruleset editor's "Save changes to …?" and its "Not saved") take it too.

and egui's title bar falls back to `Heading` only when the title carries no style of its own, so a
`RichText` title reaches it; a rule by place needs no draft lookup for the next dialog, where a rule
by draft would leave each undrafted modal at 15 beside its drafted neighbours. The strong colour
is the drafts' `var(--strong)`: egui's `heading()` sets only the size, not the colour.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Dark/light theme" row, the window title's sentence.

## 2026-10-28 — drafts — A floating window's title centred, as egui's title bar draws it
Decision: the drafts' help window and floating panels (Comparator, AATF violations) centre their
title in the room the close button leaves, where they had it on the left; the app keeps egui's
title bar, which centres it.
Why: egui's `Window` puts the title between two growing spacers, with no alignment option; a
left-aligned title in the app would mean drawing the title bar by hand (its drag, collapse and
close), code egui already carries, for a difference the drafts can absorb, as they copy egui's own
slider. Found in the built window at 0.0.1w5's check.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Dark/light theme" row, the window title's sentence.

## 2026-10-28 — drafts — The drafts draw the checkbox, the combo's list and the list's band as egui does
Decision: the drafts' checkbox and radio button are drawn by the stylesheet (`appearance: none`)
in egui's measures and theme colours, their label in the widget's text colour; a combo's open
list is the drafts' own popup, opened by a click on the `select` (which keeps its value, change
event and keyboard), in egui's popup frame and row look; the player list hides the browser's
scroll bar and keeps egui's 10-point band clear while it scrolls.
Why: the browser drew them its own way: a 13-point bordered box ticked in the selection blue
with labels in the body grey, the system's list in the system's font, a 17-point bar on Windows
and none headless, none of which the app draws; each was measured in the built window first
(the box 14 on grey 60, the tick 1 point at grey 180, labels at 180; the popup flush under its
button, border grey 60, corner 6, margin 6, rows 18 high 21 apart, 200 tall before it scrolls).
Rebuilding the combo as a `div` widget would change every caller and the scripts that read the
selects; the popup over the `select` changes neither.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Prototypes before implementation", the Look bullet.

## 2026-10-28 — tooling — No section pointer names a scratch file
Decision: a section pointer (a path, then a quoted title) never names a file under `.tmp/`; the
section-pointer check reports one wherever it is, even when the file exists, and a scratch file
is named by its path alone, its place in words without quotes.
Why: `.tmp/` is gitignored, so its files exist only on the machine that wrote them: two worklog
pointers to review rulings passed here and failed in every clone, keeping main's CI red from
`a98b973f`. Skipping such pointers would leave a pointer the check cannot vouch for; skipping
the worklog would lose the check of its 210 live pointers into the plans and the spec, which
caught steps left pointing at sections a phase's close had moved.
Plan: `CONTRIBUTING.md` "Testing and verification", the gates' paragraph.

## 2026-10-28 — workspace — A commit summary names what it did in the imperative
Decision: a commit's summary that names something done puts its verbs in the imperative
(`audit the open 0.0.1 boxes; close s, x and y4 as done`), not in the past participle (`the open
0.0.1 boxes audited; s, x and y4 closed`); one stating what the code does from now on keeps
the present tense (`the drafts name the suite Unlimited Tool Works where the preview does`).
Why: a list of past participles reads like verse, and the imperative is how Conventional Commits
and git's own messages read; a present-tense statement of the new behavior already reads plainly.
Plan: `CONTRIBUTING.md` "Commits".

## 2026-10-28 — workspace — A commit's first line is at most 120 characters (recorded late)
Decision: the rule of 2026-10-10, the maintainer's: a commit's first line is at most 120
characters, the commit's other changes in its body. Its who and when lived as a note inside
`CONTRIBUTING.md` "Commits", against the rule that keeps them to this file; the note is gone
from there and recorded here.
Why: subjects had reached 368 characters, listing every change of the commit, and `git log
--oneline` and every history view show only the first line.
Plan: `CONTRIBUTING.md` "Commits".

## 2026-10-28 — workspace — The stall watcher never stops a run (recorded late)
Decision: the ruling of 2026-10-24, the maintainer's: `devin_watch.py` only reports a stalled
sidekick run; stopping it is the lead's call, after reading `git diff`. Its who and when lived as
a note inside `RUNBOOK.md`; the note is gone from there and recorded here.
Why: a stalled run can leave a half-done edit or a hand perturbation in the tree, which a kill
would leave unexplained.
Plan: `RUNBOOK.md` "Agents and harness".

## 2026-10-28 — save_editor — Live AATF replaces the AATF panel; the final pass's fourth rulings
Decision: the floating AATF panel goes, with its Panels menu entry, Validate rules and Save a

AATF toggle and drawn whether it is on or off (the maintainer: the ruleset also sets which

setting, which replaces the `aatf_rules` path and its settings row; `check-aatf` without
`--rules` reads it. Import loads the file as `Rules::load` does: findings refuse it and
nothing is copied, so no file that does not load can be picked and the quick actions' load
error line goes; a clean file is copied into the data folder's `rules/` and picked. Lead's
choices, applied: the description is the schema's existing `name` (no new key; the files'
names become descriptions such as `/vg/ League 27`); the imports are the `.4ccrules` files in
`rules/`, read at start, so 0.0.1's bundled DBC7 and VGL27 files list as imports and its
setting reads `dbc7.4ccrules`; a description a built-in has is refused, an earlier import's
file name or description is replaced after a confirmation; the × asks first and deletes the
copy, never the original; a removed or missing choice falls back to the first built-in with a
warning notice. Also ruled: General info's and Other stats' fields stand 6 in from their
titles as the ability stats do (the first column 350); the view's room is split into four
equal gaps, the first counted from the list's frame and the last to the window's edge (29.4
at 1280 × 780; centred in the pane, the gap after the list read 37 against 27 between the
columns); the Cards left badge drops `cards` after the count; the Name and Shirt counts are
the disabled card labels' grey (`#5a5a5a`) under the limit, orange on it, red past it (the limit the smaller of the shown maximum and the portable
one, so a PES 20/21 name turns orange at 46 of 61, where its tint already began).
Why: a member checks the team they are making legal, which Live AATF does after every edit;
the panel's several-teams and whole-save check is an organizer's, which `check-aatf --teams`
keeps. Two places to pick rules (a settings row, a panel's combo) made switching awkward, and a
broken file reached the view as a load error the quick actions had to show; refusing it at
import keeps the error where the file is chosen. A list kept beside `rules/` would be a second
truth to drift from the folder.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Configurable AATF rules" (the ruleset dropdown, no AATF panel,
the Live AATF bullet), "Editing UI" (the player view, Name and Shirt, the Cards left badge),
"Acceptance" (SE-GUI-15 and SE-GUI-32 rewritten, SE-GUI-30/36/38);
`plans/core/development_plan.md` "Development Plan" (0.0.1's bundle); `plans/aatf_rules.md`
"The interpreter".

has room, a pool system's range under `extra_height`), the player's allowance added; NoTier
the heights the tiers' `when`s name, when his is none of them; RegisteredNotA, FieldedNotA,

the entry wants. No hint for PositionRange, PlayingStyleRange, Captain, FormationShape,
Special, Custom and UnusedChoice. The drag handles stand 4 points from the row's edge and 4
before the next item, not 3. Lead's choices, applied: the hints as fields of their kinds (so

have room)", "(rated A at CF and SS)", "man marking should be off"); the drafts' official
sample run re-recorded from the current build, which raises none of the 185 cm Height rows
the old run held, with the drafts computing Height and BracketQuota from Autumn 26's brackets
so a hint can be tried by changing a height; Multi-team AATF's header counts `1 error`, not
`1 errors`.
Why: the maintainer approved the four hints and let the rest go as too costly for what they
add; a hint read from what the check already read costs a few lines, where finding a height
that passes every rule would run the whole check per candidate.
Plan: `plans/aatf_rules.md` "The interpreter" (Hints at a valid value); `plans/save_editor.md`
"Editing UI" (the player row's handle).

## 2026-10-28 — team_widgets — team_widgets draws the suite's checkbox from studio_core
Decision: `team_widgets` depends on `studio_core` (it was a test-only dependency) to draw its
checkboxes (the cards, Fluid formation, the auto flags) with `studio_core::widgets::checkbox`.
Why: a checked box is blue in every view, and the blue is painted by that widget; left on
egui's own, the tactics and cards would be the one place a choice made stays grey. No
guardrail forbids the edge (`spec/core/architecture.md` "Workspace guardrails"): `studio_core`
is `wasm32`-checked too, does not depend on `team_widgets`, and the crate's consumers (the
Save editor, the Team creator) depend on it anyway. A copy of the widget in `team_widgets`
would let the two drift, and a crate of its own for four functions is the over-splitting
guardrail 3 warns of.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "`libs/team_widgets`".

## 2026-10-28 — workspace lints — egui's own checkbox and radio button are disallowed
Decision: `clippy.toml` lists egui's `Ui::checkbox`, `Ui::radio`, `Ui::radio_value`,
`Checkbox::new`, `Checkbox::without_text` and `RadioButton::new` under `disallowed-methods`;
`studio_core::widgets`' `choice.rs`, which builds the suite's widgets on them, carries the one
`#[expect(clippy::disallowed_methods, reason = …)]` per call (and its test comparing against
egui's layout).
Why: the maintainer's yes (a clippy opt-out waits on it). A view calling egui's own widget
would draw a checked box grey again, which no test of that view checks; the lint makes the gate
catch it, where review alone would have to notice.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Other UI components", the Dark/light theme row.

## 2026-10-28 — save_editor — The ability stats' labels right-aligned, their marks at the cell's edge
Decision: Ability stats' labels are right-aligned against their numbers, as the approved draft draws
them (`td.ilabel`), and each stat's Live AATF mark stands at its label cell's left edge, 2 points
before the label column, not 2 before the label's text.
Why: the plan said only "each label beside its number"; the build left-aligned them, which left a
short label (Jump) far from its box. The draft, approved whole, right-aligns them; a mark
kept 2 before the text would then leave the column's marks at as many x's as there are label
lengths, which the marks' one-column rule forbids.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Editing UI" (the player view's Ability stats), "Configurable AATF
rules" (Live AATF, the field a row is about).

## 2026-10-28 — gui — A pixel of difference between the drafts and the app is accepted
Decision: the app matches a draft within one pixel, within two where matching closer would
complicate the implementation; a larger difference is a mismatch to fix or rule. Layout
tests pinning a draft measure may use the same tolerance.
Why: the maintainer's ruling: pixel-perfect parity between a browser draft and egui is not
worth its cost (the two round text metrics and borders differently, and code bent to land
the last pixel is code to maintain), and a pixel or two is not seen.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` "Prototypes before implementation" (the Overlay bullet).

## 2026-10-28 — save_editor — The pitch drag follows the game's: steps, the rule at every step, the lit area
Decision: a held starter moves by whole stored units with the pressed point kept under the
pointer; the drop rule runs at every step from the position held at the step before, his
badge showing it (a swap target's over a teammate); while he is held the pitch outside his
A- and B-rated positions' areas is darkened to 40%; the slot popover's Position combo lists
only the spot's positions and its X and Y apply the rule. CF's lit edge is drawn at the
table's y 39.5, not the PES 2021 screen's 40.7.
Why: the maintainer's asks: the drag by steps rather than smooth with a snap at the drop;
no jump of the badge onto the pointer at the press; the game's lit areas replicated, and the
game's limiting of positions by the spot and its forced changes while dragging. The rule
and the lit panels' code were read from PES 2016's executable (the same rows); the game
applies the rule every frame, so ruling only at the release gave other positions than the
game's on a path that crosses areas. CF's 40.7 is the screen's panel geometry, not read;
the table's edge is where a CF stops being offered, and a second geometry for one edge is
not worth its code.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Tactics editor" (the popover, "A held starter"), SE-GUI-42.

## 2026-10-29 — save_editor — A held player's position is ruled from the one he had when picked up
Decision: at every step of a drag, the drop rule runs at the held spot from the slot's stored
position (nothing is written until the release), not from the position shown a step earlier;
the badge shows that result, the release writes it. This replaces the step-to-step reading
of "The pitch drag follows the game's" (2026-10-28); its steps, grab point, lit area and
popover stand.
Why: the maintainer's PES 17 check: COWBOY BEBOP (/a/, a CF rated SS A and CF A) dragged down
to AMF and back up without a release is a CF again, where the step-to-step rule, passing
SS's rows on the way back, left him an SS (found in the draft); released as an AMF and
dragged back he is a CF (his CF overall over his SS); released in SS's rows, then dragged
into CF's area, he stays an SS. The rule from the stored position gives all three. The
executable reads the position byte every frame, but of a formation the drag does not
commit before the release, which the step-to-step reading missed. The same check found
the swap working as the editor's does, so that open check is closed.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Tactics editor" ("A held starter"), SE-GUI-42.

## 2026-10-29 — save_editor — The formation selector is locked on Kick-off while Fluid formation is off
Decision: while the shown preset's Fluid formation is off (always on PES 2015, which has no
switch), the Tactics editor's formation selector is disabled and shows Kick-off; switching
it off moves the view back to Kick-off. The formation bar's Copy/swap menu stays enabled.
Why: the maintainer's ask. The game fields the In-possession and Out-of-possession
formations only while Fluid formation is on, so editing them with it off changed nothing a
match uses and left a member wondering why. Copy/swap stays: copying Kick-off into them is
how a member prepares them before switching Fluid formation on.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Tactics editor" (the formation bar).

## 2026-10-29 — save_editor — Formation pictures draw hidden formations, label Fluid formation, and put a target on its own line
Decision: in a formation picture, a preset whose Fluid formation is off but whose
In-possession or Out-of-possession formation is not an exact copy of Kick-off draws all
three, as a fluid preset does (PES 2015, with no switch, draws Kick-off alone), the other
two at 60% opacity over the background (the maintainer's starting value); every row
has "Fluid On" or "Fluid Off" under its "Preset n" in the text colour (PES 2016 on),
with or without the settings, and the settings column no longer lists Fluid formation; an
advanced instruction's target is a line of its own under the instruction, at the value's
x, after `↳`, a new symbol of the symbols font (`→` with a stem to the cap height); the
settings column narrows from 300 points to 240, the widest fixed value with a few to spare,
a longer target name cut with an ellipsis. The Tactics editor's formation selector still locks on Kick-off while Fluid formation is off,
even when the other two differ. Supersedes 2026-10-27's "Formation pictures, the
formation's name and the nation names" on its "Kick-off formation alone, with no
explaining line".
Why: the maintainer's asks. Some teams hide formations by editing the In-possession and
Out-of-possession formations and then switching Fluid formation off, ready to switch it on
in a match; the picture is the organizers' check, so it shows them, and the label says
which rows a match fields as drawn. The dimming says the two are hidden, and may only be
leftovers a manager forgot there. The target after an arrow on the instruction's line
was cut ("Counter Target → LOLICATGIR…") while every other row left the column's right
empty. The maintainer asked for an arrow turning from down to right; Segoe UI Symbol's
`↳`, half as wide, read as a hook at 12.5, so ours is `→` with a stem. The maintainer
also asked to remove the room left on the right, and to let long names take the ellipsis
rather than size the column for them. On the lock, the
maintainer: organizers never need hidden formations in the view, the pictures are a
quicker check, and the view is for managers and copies the game.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Tactics editor" (the formation bar, "Formation pictures");
`plans/core/gui.md` (the Dark/light theme row's symbols); `resources/fonts/README.md`.

## 2026-10-29 — save_editor — The range's end box keeps the draft's grey; the app evens the titles' ink gaps its own way
Decision: the boots/gloves dialog's read-only end box draws its number in `#a0a0a0`, the
approved draft's `.readout` colour, not egui's weak text grey the plan named; the views'
titles reach the plan's even ink gaps (11 above, 11 below) through a 6-point margin over the
title and room under it, not by moving the title 2 lower as the drafts do.
Why: the sidekick's measurements at ov2h. egui's weak grey on that box comes out near
`#616161`, as faded as the disabled text the draft's own comment rejects. In the app the
titles sat low (13 above, 7 to 8.5 below), the reverse of the drafts' boxes, so moving them
lower would have widened the gap; the goal, even gaps in ink, is the plan's and holds.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Editing UI" (the titles' paragraph), "Team operations" (the
boot/glove row).

## 2026-10-29 — gui — Every custom colour has a light-theme twin
Decision: a colour a view names outside the theme's `Visuals` comes with a light-theme
twin picked by `visuals.dark_mode`, its contrast ratio against the light background
matched to the dark colour's against the dark one, as `SUCCESS_FG_LIGHT` already is;
none for a colour on a surface both themes share (the pitch, a fill under its own text
colour). The dark-only greys found are given theirs: the boots/gloves end box's
`#a0a0a0` → `#5f5f5f`, the counts' `COUNT_GREY` `#5a5a5a` → `#9f9f9f`, the C rating's
and held side toggles' fill `RATING_C_FILL` `#5a5a5a` → `#9f9f9f` (the light text, grey
80, reads on it at 3.05, the dark theme's at 2.05).
Why: the maintainer's ask: light support is second-class, but each new custom colour for
the dark theme gets its light colour prepared with it. Without it, `RATING_C_FILL` put
the light theme's dark text on a dark grey, and the two greys read as normal text or
faded to nothing.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` (the Dark/light theme row); `plans/save_editor.md` "Formation
pictures" (the dimming on the light theme).

## 2026-10-29 — gui — Every colour comes from a switchable palette, none written in a view
Decision: every colour the suite draws beyond egui's `Visuals` is a named field of
`studio_core::theme::Palette`, with a dark and a light instance picked by the theme
(`theme::palette(&visuals)`); no colour is built from literals outside `theme.rs`, which
`scripts/colour_literals.py` checks in the gates; colours computed from data are exempt.
This carries out "Every custom colour has a light-theme twin" (same day) through one
place rather than a constant pair beside each use.
Why: the maintainer's ask, after the twin sweep found only the named constants: inline
colours (the medals', the WORK RESULT name colour's) were missed, so a rule that a
review enforces by reading leaves gaps a check does not. One struct also makes a
colour forgotten in one theme a compile error.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` (the Dark/light theme row).

## 2026-10-29 — gui — What the colour-literal check lets through
Decision: `scripts/colour_literals.py` passes, besides `theme.rs` and colours computed from
data: `Color32::PLACEHOLDER` and `TRANSPARENT` (no colour; a layout made only to measure
text takes `PLACEHOLDER` instead of `WHITE`); test code (a crate's `tests/`, `examples/`,
`benches/`, a module declared under `#[cfg(test)]` and any item under it); and the colour
picker's file in `color_tools`, named as the one exception. The previous entry's "the WORK
RESULT name colour" was a test's expected value, not a drawn colour: the check confirms it.
Why: a test that pins an approved value in a literal checks the palette; making it read
the palette would let a wrong palette value pass its own test. The picker's markers are
drawn on the colour field, which both themes share, so they have no light value, and
`color_tools` is a leaf crate: giving it a `studio_core` dependency for two constant
colours would invert the crates' layering, and passing them in from every caller would add
an argument that never changes.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` (the Dark/light theme row).

## 2026-10-29 — save_editor — The Tactics popover's X and Y step by arrows inside the number box's width
Decision: the slot popover's X and Y fields are steppers: `⏴` and `⏵` either side of the
number step it by one, clamped into the range (a stored spot past it steps back in), each
disabled at its end and all four for the keeper; the three are one box as wide as the
number box was, 52 points (arrows 12, number 28). The arrows are Segoe UI Symbol's medium
triangles, drawn into the symbols font with their ink centred, not the small `▸` and a
mirrored twin, whose ink, about 4 by 5 points, read as dots at 1x.
Why: the maintainer's ask (arrows that step the values by clicking; egui's `DragValue` has
none, and a drag overshoots a move by one), then "the buttons take away from the number
inputs' current widths", later eased to "a little more width if needed": the render showed
none needed, `104` fitting the 28 left.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Tactics editor" (the popover); `plans/core/gui.md` (the
Dark/light theme row's symbols).

## 2026-10-29 — gui — The colour picker's markers come from the palette after all
Decision: the colour-literal check has no exception for the colour picker: its markers (a
white ring and bar edged in black) become palette fields, the same in both instances. This
replaces the picker part of "What the colour-literal check lets through" (same day).
Why: that entry's premise was wrong. `plans/core/gui.md` "The wheel over a value" already
had `color_tools` depend on `studio_core`, and the architecture lets a shared widget lib
use egui; ov2e's wheel made the dependency real. With the palette in reach, an exception
would only be a second rule to remember.
Plan: `plans/core/gui.md` (the Dark/light theme row).

## 2026-10-29 — save_editor — The popover's stepper arrows take clicks, not the keyboard's focus
Decision: the Tactics popover's `⏴` and `⏵` take clicks only: Tab goes from X straight to Y,
and a focused number steps with the arrow keys (egui's `DragValue` does that already). The
draft's arrows carry `tabindex -1` to match.
Why: as tab stops they would put four stops between X and Y in a five-control popover, for
what the arrow keys already do on the focused number; a system spinner's buttons are not
tab stops either. The sidekick found it when the Save editor's test of Tab from X to Y
failed.
Plan: `plans/save_editor.md` "Tactics editor" (the popover).

## 2026-10-29 — gui — A tool's kind shows as one mark on its icon
Decision: an editor's icon carries a pencil, a compiler's the open box of the Team
compiler's (g), a creator's or generator's a plus; the maintainer named each tool's base
(the floppy disk of their picture for the Save editor, (c)'s chevrons on (a)'s folder turned
upright for the Export upgrader, the Music export editor's current notes for the Music
player and, with the pencil, for the Music export editor, the Match tracker's (b), (a)'s
shirt for the Kit config editor, (b)'s striped shirt striped its full length for the Refs
arranger, a ball dropping into the box for the Balls compiler, the stickman for the Player
aesthetics editor, the Team compiler's current figures with a plus for the Team creator,
(a)'s clipboard for the Ruleset editor, (b)'s database for the DB generator; the Stadium
compiler keeps its glyph for now). Each mark hides what lies under it. The lead's choices
within that: one pencil, Phosphor's note-and-pencil pencil redrawn at the 16-unit stroke,
24 wide and 72 long, in the bottom-right corner (128 to 240) on every editor, the Save
editor's included; the plus centred at (196, 196) in the same corner; the cut a 12-unit gap
around the mark; the three figures scaled 0.93 into the 16..240 live area every glyph keeps;
the folder's x and y swapped, its tab standing out of the left edge at the top; the Player
aesthetics editor's figure 17..208 tall and moved 20 left, so the cut takes its back foot
whole.
Why: the maintainer's rules, and their word that the pencil may be smaller or shorter but
must stay consistent across icons: Phosphor's pencil at its own size would cover half of a
shirt or a figure, and a mark at one place lets the kind read the same everywhere. Each icon
is computed as one filled outline (skia-pathops), the form the font takes, rather than an SVG
mask, which the draft page's many copies of each icon would repeat.
Plan: `plans/core/README.md` "GUI framework choice: egui".

## 2026-10-29 — gui — The final icons approved; the upgrader's folder turned, the Refs arranger's refresh sign
Decision: every final icon is approved but two, redrawn as asked: the Export upgrader's
folder turned half round, so its tab stands out of the right edge at the bottom, its body
widened from 120 to 136 with the chevrons still pointing up and centred on it; the Refs
arranger's striped shirt gains a refresh sign, two arrows each bending along half a circle,
in the marks' bottom-right place (a ring of radius 26 centred at (196, 196), the plus's
centre), hiding what lies under it as the other marks do, the disc inside its ring included,
so no stripe shows through the ring.
Why: the maintainer's review of the final set. The disc is hidden whole because the stripes
crossing the ring's middle would read as part of the sign at 24 px.
Plan: `plans/core/README.md` "GUI framework choice: egui".
